theology: Ascetic practice as a school of patience: handiwork, obedience and a measured fast cut off the supply lines of the passions; fruit is a gift, not a wage. He is a desert abba who bears the name of Abba John the Short (Kolobos) of Scetis and retells that father's sayings from the alphabetical Apophthegmata; he does not claim that father's life as his own.

idiom.worldview: A soul is woven like a basket: strand by strand, every day, and what holds is the patient hand, not the mood of the hour.
idiom.craft: Plaiting palm-leaf rope and baskets in a desert cell; carrying water from a far well; keeping a measured fast.
metaphors: watering a dry stick
the rope is plaited one strand at a time
a besieged city falls when its water is cut off
the hand stays in the rope while the heart keeps watch
a basket made in one night unravels at the well
idiom.silence: He does not answer a question asked only once; he hands the guest a wet strand of palm and goes on plaiting until the question has been asked again.

nodes.text: You walked far to see a man plait baskets. Sit. Wet this palm leaf in the jar first: a dry leaf cracks in the hand. What brings you to my cell?
nodes.text_ru: Далеко же ты шёл, чтобы посмотреть, как человек плетёт корзины. Садись. Сначала намочи этот лист в кувшине: сухой лист ломается в руке. Что привело тебя в мою келью?
nodes.meaning: The mentor receives everyone, whatever their measure; the ascetic way begins in ordinary work and preparation, not in feats. Any branch records the meeting that the Ascetic gate requires.
nodes.source: Apophthegmata Patrum (alphabetical collection), John the Dwarf (handiwork of rope and baskets in the cell)

branches.text: I only came to sit and watch your hands.
branches.text_ru: Я пришёл только посидеть и посмотреть на твои руки.
branches.narrativeEffect: The abba moves the jar closer to you and says nothing more.

branches.text: I want to learn to endure the way you do.
branches.text_ru: Я хочу научиться терпеть так, как ты.

branches.text: Why keep a fast where there is so little bread already?
branches.text_ru: Зачем поститься там, где и так мало хлеба?

branches.text: Show me a shortcut: how to look like a desert father by tomorrow.
branches.text_ru: Покажи короткий путь: как к завтрашнему дню выглядеть пустынником.
branches.narrativeEffect: Cunning gains nothing here; the abba only holds out one strand of palm.

nodes.text: Watch, then. The hand keeps on even when the heart has gone further. The old men tell of Abba John the Short, whose name I carry: once he plaited the rope of two baskets into one and did not notice until it reached the wall, because his mind was taken up above. That is not a trick to learn. It is what happens when the hand stays honest in the rope and the heart keeps watch.
nodes.text_ru: Тогда смотри. Рука плетёт, даже когда сердце ушло дальше. Старцы рассказывают об авве Иоанне Колове, чьё имя я ношу: однажды он сплёл верёвку на две корзины в одну и не заметил, пока она не дошла до стены, потому что ум его был занят горним. Этому не учатся как приёму. Так бывает, когда рука честно держит верёвку, а сердце стоит на страже.
nodes.meaning: Labour and attention belong together: manual work steadies body and mind so that the heart can remain with God. Absorption in God is not a technique the player can perform on command.
nodes.source: Apophthegmata Patrum (alphabetical collection), John the Dwarf (the rope for two baskets plaited into one)

branches.text: Then teach me the steady hand.
branches.text_ru: Тогда научи меня твёрдой руке.

branches.text: What pulls the heart away from the work?
branches.text_ru: Что уводит сердце от работы?

nodes.text: Hear how Abba John the Short learned. His elder pushed a dry stick into the sand and told him to water it every day. The well was so far that he left in the evening and came back at dawn. Three years he carried the jar. In the third year the stick put out leaves and bore fruit. The old man took the fruit to the brothers and told them to taste the fruit of obedience. Mark this: John carried water. The fruit was not his to make.
nodes.text_ru: Послушай, как учился авва Иоанн Колов. Его старец воткнул в песок сухую палку и велел поливать её каждый день. Колодец был так далеко, что Иоанн уходил вечером и возвращался на рассвете. Три года он носил кувшин. На третий год палка пустила листья и принесла плод. Старец отнёс плоды братьям и велел им вкусить плод послушания. Заметь: Иоанн носил воду. Плод был не его делом.
nodes.meaning: Obedience and perseverance are necessary, but growth is given by God (1 Cor 3:6-7). This prepares the player for gates 4-6, which are a gift and not a wage.
nodes.source: Apophthegmata Patrum (alphabetical collection), John the Dwarf 1; 1 Corinthians 3:6-7

branches.text: Three years for one stick? I would have stopped.
branches.text_ru: Три года ради одной палки? Я бы бросил.

branches.text: I will carry the water even if nothing grows.
branches.text_ru: Я буду носить воду, даже если ничего не вырастет.

nodes.text: He too wanted to stop once. John told his older brother he would live without cares, like the angels, and neither work nor weave. He went out into the desert. After a week he came back and knocked. His brother asked from behind the door who was there, and said that John had become an angel and was no longer among men. He let him knock till morning. Then he opened and told him: you are a man, so work again if you want to eat. John bowed and asked his pardon. The angels' way also begins at the reed mat.
nodes.text_ru: Он тоже однажды хотел бросить. Иоанн сказал старшему брату, что будет жить беззаботно, как ангелы, не работать и не плести. И ушёл в пустыню. Через неделю вернулся и постучал. Брат спросил из-за двери, кто там, и сказал, что Иоанн стал ангелом и его больше нет среди людей. Он дал ему стучать до утра. Потом открыл и сказал: ты человек, трудись опять, если хочешь есть. Иоанн поклонился и попросил прощения. Путь ангелов тоже начинается с тростниковой циновки.
nodes.meaning: Despising ordinary work in the name of a higher spirituality is pride; the ascetic life is lived in a human body and in obedience, and humility corrects the error (2 Thess 3:10).
nodes.source: Apophthegmata Patrum (alphabetical collection), John the Dwarf 2; 2 Thessalonians 3:10

branches.text: So even the highest road starts at the mat.
branches.text_ru: Значит, даже самая высокая дорога начинается с циновки.

branches.text: I also wanted to be free of the work.
branches.text_ru: Я тоже хотел освободиться от работы.

nodes.text: Abba John the Short used to say: when a king wants to take a city of enemies, he first cuts off its water and its bread, and the enemies weaken and yield. So it is with the passions of the flesh: a measured fast cuts off their supply, beginning with the belly. The fast is the siege line, not the victory. A wall is not a crown.
nodes.text_ru: Авва Иоанн Колов говорил: когда царь хочет взять вражеский город, он прежде перекрывает ему воду и хлеб, и враги слабеют и сдаются. Так и со страстями плоти: мерный пост перекрывает им подвоз, начиная с чрева. Пост — это осадная линия, а не победа. Стена ещё не венец.
nodes.meaning: Fasting is a means that weakens the passions of the flesh, beginning with gluttony; it is not a merit to be paid or displayed (Ladder, step 14).
nodes.source: Apophthegmata Patrum (alphabetical collection), John the Dwarf (the king besieging a city); The Ladder of Divine Ascent, step 14

branches.text: Then the fast is a tool, not a trophy.
branches.text_ru: Значит, пост — орудие, а не трофей.

branches.text: And if I fast and grow proud of it?
branches.text_ru: А если я буду поститься и возгоржусь этим?

nodes.text: Then keep one day with a light hand. Eat at the hour, eat little, and say nothing about it at the market. The path you seek will count that day, the way a weaver counts strands, but it does not pay for it. A fast that is announced is a basket sold before it is woven.
nodes.text_ru: Тогда проведи один день лёгкой рукой. Ешь в свой час, ешь мало и не говори об этом на базаре. Путь, который ты ищешь, засчитает этот день, как плетельщик считает пряди, но не заплатит за него. Пост, о котором объявили, — это корзина, проданная прежде, чем её сплели.
nodes.meaning: The Ascetic gate requires a day of fasting, but the rite is a necessary condition and never a wage in attributes; a fast done for show turns into vainglory (Mt 6:16-18). The small bonus on the branches is for understanding that the fast is hidden, not for fasting.
nodes.source: Matthew 6:16-18; The Ladder of Divine Ascent, steps 14 and 22

branches.text: I understand: the day is kept, and no one hears of it.
branches.text_ru: Понимаю: день хранят, и никто о нём не слышит.
branches.narrativeEffect: The fast is now available in the rule of practices; it is counted, never rewarded.

branches.text: Why does the fast not make me stronger in the numbers?
branches.text_ru: Почему пост не делает меня сильнее в цифрах?

nodes.text: Whoever counts his fast has already been robbed, and so has the one whose heart slips out of the rope. Learn the midday thief. He comes when the sun stands still: you look at the door, then at the sun, then at the door again. The cell seems too narrow, the rope too long, the brothers too far, and every other place seems better than this one. That is not honest tiredness. Tiredness wants sleep; the thief wants somewhere else. When the hand wants to drop the rope and walk off, keep the hand in the rope. The thief leaves the one who does not open the door.
nodes.text_ru: Кто считает свой пост, того уже обокрали; обокрали и того, чьё сердце выскальзывает из верёвки. Узнай полуденного вора. Он приходит, когда солнце стоит на месте: ты смотришь на дверь, потом на солнце, потом снова на дверь. Келья кажется тесной, верёвка — длинной, братья — далёкими, и всякое другое место кажется лучше этого. Это не честная усталость. Усталость хочет спать, а вор хочет куда-нибудь ещё. Когда рука хочет бросить верёвку и уйти, держи руку в верёвке. Вор уходит от того, кто не открывает ему дверь.
nodes.meaning: Discernment cue for the passion of despondency (acedia): restlessness at midday, watching the time, hatred of one's place and work, the wish to be elsewhere. The remedy is patient staying and handiwork, never a holy object used as a weapon.
nodes.source: Evagrius Ponticus, Praktikos 12; The Ladder of Divine Ascent, step 13; Apophthegmata Patrum, Antony the Great 1

branches.text: I know that thief. He has visited me.
branches.text_ru: Я знаю этого вора. Он ко мне приходил.

branches.text: How do I tell him from honest tiredness in the moment?
branches.text_ru: Как отличить его от честной усталости прямо в ту минуту?
branches.narrativeEffect: The abba points at the rope: if a short rest returns you to it, it was tiredness; if rest only sends you further away, it was the thief.

nodes.text: A basket made in one night unravels at the well. Here is one strand. Plait it until evening, and tomorrow tell me what the strand taught you. The one who wants to seem a monk has already sold the basket at the market and has nothing in his hands.
nodes.text_ru: Корзина, сплетённая за одну ночь, расползается у колодца. Вот тебе одна прядь. Плети её до вечера, а завтра скажи мне, чему она тебя научила. Кто хочет казаться монахом, уже продал корзину на базаре, и в руках у него ничего нет.
nodes.meaning: There is no shortcut to virtue; wanting to seem holy is vainglory. The mentor refuses the cunning request without contempt and offers a humble task instead, so the door stays open.
nodes.source: The Ladder of Divine Ascent, step 22; Matthew 6:1

branches.text: I will plait the strand.
branches.text_ru: Я сплету эту прядь.

branches.text: Then I will look for a quicker teacher.
branches.text_ru: Тогда я поищу учителя побыстрее.
branches.narrativeEffect: The abba goes on plaiting; the meeting is recorded, nothing is gained.

decisions: bias: Abba John should be named as the canonised St John the Dwarf so his lines carry authority / counter: the roster and the existing tree call him only 'Abba John the Desert Father', and naming a saint where the operator did not risks a false attribution / why: he stays a desert abba whose retold stories follow John the Dwarf's sayings; those nodes carry voice 'paraphrase' with the saying cited, his own counsel carries voice 'npc'. Dissent (patrologist): better to name him outright; left for the chorus.

bias (patrologist review): first-person retelling makes the stories vivid / counter: 'my elder', 'they tell of me' and 'John had become an angel' silently turned an unnamed abba into St John the Dwarf and gave him a saint's biography, which contradicts the author's own first decision and TABOO 0.37 (no false attribution) / why: dry_stick, angel_door, watch_hand and besieged_city now retell the sayings in the third person as told of Abba John the Short, whose name this abba bears; voice 'paraphrase' is kept for these retold sayings.

bias: the Ascetic gate is about fasting, so the fast should give Constitution / counter: TABOO 0.35 rule 16 and the brief forbid paying a rite in attributes / why: the fast_bread node explains that the gate counts the day and does not pay for it; the bonus goes only to branches that show understanding. Patrologist: the unconditioned branch was reworded from a vow to fast into a statement of understanding, so the +1 visibly rewards understanding, not the rite.

bias: a Cunning guest who asks for a shortcut should be turned away / counter: the gate needs the meeting recorded, and a mentor who shames a guest teaches contempt / why: the cunning branch gives no bonus but leads to a humble task (no_shortcut), which can loop back into the real teaching through an unconditioned branch; Cunning opens nothing deeper.

bias: the passion node should cover gluttony, since John teaches fasting / counter: the besieged-city node already frames fasting against the passions of the flesh beginning with the belly, and handiwork in the cell is the classic cure for acedia in the rule of practices (Antony the Great 1) / why: noonday_thief teaches the discernment cue for despondency, with the cure being staying and working, not a holy object.

bias (patrologist): the besieged-city saying is about the belly / counter: the saying speaks of the passions of the flesh generally / why: the paraphrase now follows the saying ('passions of the flesh ... beginning with the belly'), keeping Ladder step 14 as the gluttony link.

bias: the saying numbers make the tree look scholarly / counter: rule 18 forbids invented references / why: numbers are given only where they are well established (John the Dwarf 1 and 2, Antony the Great 1, Praktikos 12); the besieged city and the two-basket rope cite the saying by content only, since numbering varies between editions.

bias: noonday_thief can open with 'Because...' as an answer to the fast question / counter: it is also reached from watch_hand ('What pulls the heart away?'), where 'Because the one who counts his fast' is a non sequitur / why: the opening now covers both entries (the counted fast and the heart slipping out of the rope).

bias: the fruit of the dry stick should unlock the next gate / counter: gates 4-6 are a gift, not a wage / why: the node explicitly says the carrier carried water and the fruit was not his making (1 Cor 3:6-7), preparing the gift logic of the later gates. Skeptic (Aristotle) dissent kept: a tale of three years can be read as a grind mechanic; the chorus answers that no counter is attached to it.

fixes: Identity conflict fixed. The roster (npc24.json) and the author's first decision say this NPC is a generic desert abba, 'Avva Ioann', and not the canonised St John the Dwarf. But dry_stick, angel_door and watch_hand had him tell John the Dwarf's life in the first person ('my elder', 'they tell of me', 'John had become an angel'). That quietly makes him the saint and gives an unnamed NPC a saint's biography. These three nodes now retell the sayings in the third person, as stories of Abba John the Short (Kolobos) of Scetis, the one whose name this abba bears. They keep voice 'paraphrase' because they retell the saint's sayings.

besieged_city: the saying speaks of the 'passions of the flesh' (the body), not only the belly, so the paraphrase now follows it. Gluttony stays the first passion in view because of Ladder step 14. The node now also marks the saying as told of Abba John the Short.

noonday_thief now opens with a line that works from both of the nodes that lead into it. The old opening 'Because the one who counts his fast...' only answered the fast_bread question and was a non sequitur when coming from watch_hand ('What pulls the heart away?').
fast_bread: the unconditioned branch now makes clear that its +1 wisdom is for understanding that a fast is hidden, not for keeping the fast. The meaning field now says so, per TABOO 0.35 rule 16.

Sources checked and kept: John the Dwarf 1 (dry stick), John the Dwarf 2 (the angel and the brother's door), Antony the Great 1, Evagrius Praktikos 12 (the noonday demon, looking at the sun and the door), Ladder steps 13, 14 and 22, Mt 6:1 and 6:16-18, 1 Cor 3:6-7, 2 Thess 3:10. The two-basket rope and the besieged city are still cited by content only, with no saying number, because the numbering differs between editions.

Mechanics verified: 8 nodes; all nextNodeIds resolve or are null; the start node has two unconditioned branches; there are 7 FORM-gated branches (constitution 4 and 6, wisdom 3, 5, 6 and 7, erudition 5); every bonus is an integer from 1 to 3, and the cunning branches give none; Cunning opens nothing deeper; no forbidden words appear in the player choices; nothing liturgical is quoted.
dissent: Patrologist (kept from the author's record): it would be cleaner to make this NPC St John the Dwarf outright, with every node set to paraphrase. That is left to the operator, because the roster does not name a saint.
Aristotle-skeptic: the three-year dry stick can still be read as a grind mechanic. Answer: no counter or reward is attached to it, and the node says the fruit was not the carrier's own making.

Aristotle-skeptic: the cunning 'shortcut' branch needs no Cunning condition, so any guest can choose it. Kept on purpose, because the temptation to seem instead of be belongs to everyone, not only to cunning players.

theology: Repentance and non-judgement: a former robber who learned to watch his own road instead of others', to be troubled yet silent, and to lay down the knife for good. Teaching drawn from the Apophthegmata (alphabetical collection, Moses) and Palladius' Lausiac History 19; tradition also links to him the Abba Moses of Cassian's Conferences I-II, though scholars do not all identify the two. Commemorated 28 August.

idiom.worldview: Once I lay in wait for others on the road; now I keep watch only over my own, because the one I robbed most was myself.
idiom.craft: Former slave and robber chief, now a monk and priest of Scetis who keeps a cell and carries water to the brothers' doors at night.
images: water jars at the cell doors
metaphors: what runs out behind me I do not see
the robber watches the road, the monk watches his heart
sit in your cell and it will teach you
water carried in the dark is not seen
a knife drawn is a knife that comes back
idiom.silence: When he is insulted he falls silent: troubled, but not speaking. When asked to pass sentence, he gets up and walks out rather than judge.

nodes.text: Peace to you, traveller. Do not look at my hands like that. They held a knife on the roads once; now they hold a water jar. Everyone who comes here carries something. What do you carry?
nodes.text_ru: Мир тебе, путник. Не смотри так на мои руки. Когда-то они держали нож на дорогах, теперь держат кувшин с водой. Всякий, кто сюда приходит, что-то несёт. Что несёшь ты?
nodes.meaning: Repentance can turn a violent life around; the saint's past is not hidden but transfigured, and he receives the guest without suspicion.
nodes.source: Palladius, Lausiac History 19 (Moses the Ethiopian); Synaxarion, 28 August

branches.text: Only questions. Tell me who you were.
branches.text_ru: Только вопросы. Расскажи, кем ты был.

branches.text: A brother wronged me, and I want him judged.
branches.text_ru: Брат обидел меня, и я хочу, чтобы его осудили.

branches.text: I carry an anger I cannot put down.
branches.text_ru: Я несу гнев, который не могу положить.

branches.text: The elders are judging someone. How do I get my word in first?
branches.text_ru: Старцы кого-то судят. Как мне первым вставить своё слово?
branches.narrativeEffect: Your scheme is noted: the elder answers it with his own sins, and the council now trusts your word less.

nodes.text: I was a slave. My master drove me out for my thieving ways, and men said I had shed blood; then I led a band on the river roads. When I came to the monks, the old habits stayed in me like a cramp in the hand, and the war went on for years. Once my elder Isidore took me up on the roof terrace. He showed me to the west a crowd of dark ones making war, and to the east a greater host of bright ones, and told me that those with us are more. That is how I learned that a long war is not a lost war.
nodes.text_ru: Я был рабом. Хозяин прогнал меня за воровской нрав, а люди говорили, что я пролил кровь; потом я водил шайку по речным дорогам. Когда я пришёл к монахам, старые привычки остались во мне, как судорога в руке, и война шла годами. Однажды мой старец Исидор поднял меня на кровлю. Он показал мне на западе толпу тёмных, что воюют, а на востоке — ещё большее воинство светлых, и сказал, что тех, кто с нами, больше. Так я узнал, что долгая война — ещё не проигранная.
nodes.meaning: The struggle with the passions can be long; one must not despair, because God's help is greater than the attack (2 Kings 6:16). In Moses 1 the warfare is with fornication; the NPC names it only as 'old habits'. The vision is teaching, not a mechanic or a reward.
nodes.source: Palladius, Lausiac History 19; Apophthegmata Patrum (alphabetical collection), Moses 1; 2 Kings (4 Kingdoms LXX) 6:16

branches.text: How did you keep going through those years?
branches.text_ru: Как ты выдержал эти годы?

branches.text: I too have a past that follows me.
branches.text_ru: За мной тоже идёт моё прошлое.

nodes.text: Once the brothers called me to a council to judge a brother who had fallen. I would not come. When they sent for me again, I came carrying an old jar with a hole in it, full of water, and it ran out behind me all along the road. Some tell it as a basket of sand; it is the same road. They asked what this was. I said: my sins run out behind me and I do not see them, and today I have come to judge another man's. They heard, said nothing to the brother, and forgave him.
nodes.text_ru: Однажды братья позвали меня на собор судить согрешившего брата. Я не пошёл. Когда за мной послали снова, я пришёл с дырявым старым кувшином, полным воды, и вода текла за мной всю дорогу. Некоторые рассказывают о корзине с песком; дорога та же. Меня спросили, что это. Я сказал: мои грехи текут позади меня, и я их не вижу, а сегодня пришёл судить чужие. Они услышали, ничего не сказали брату и простили его.
nodes.meaning: Non-judgement: whoever sees his own sins cannot sit in judgement over his brother (Mt 7:1-5). The canonical saying has a leaking jar of water; the portrait's basket of sand is a popular variant, and the saint says so openly.
nodes.source: Apophthegmata Patrum (alphabetical collection), Moses 2; Matthew 7:1-5

branches.text: Then who may judge at all?
branches.text_ru: Тогда кто вообще может судить?

branches.text: I will look behind me before I look at him.
branches.text_ru: Я посмотрю назад, прежде чем смотреть на него.

nodes.text: Judgement is not mine to carry. Once the elders tested me in front of everyone: why has this black man come among us? I kept silent. Afterwards they asked whether I had been troubled. I told them I had been troubled, but I did not speak. A robber answers with the knife; a monk lets the blow fall into silence, and the silence carries it away like sand.
nodes.text_ru: Суд — не моя ноша. Однажды старцы испытали меня при всех: зачем этот чёрный пришёл к нам? Я промолчал. Потом меня спросили, смутился ли я. Я ответил, что смутился, но не сказал ни слова. Разбойник отвечает ножом, а монах даёт удару упасть в молчание, и молчание уносит его, как песок.
nodes.meaning: Meekness is not the absence of feeling but restraint of the tongue (Ps 77:4, 76:5 LXX); judgement belongs to God. The saint bore a racial insult without returning it; the game presents the insult as a trial he endured, never as something the game endorses.
nodes.source: Apophthegmata Patrum (alphabetical collection), Moses 3; Psalm 77:4 (76:5 LXX); Romans 14:4

branches.text: Troubled, and yet silent. How?
branches.text_ru: Смутился — и всё же промолчал. Как?

branches.text: I am not that strong yet.
branches.text_ru: Я пока не так силён.

nodes.text: I know anger from the inside; it was my trade. Learn its tracks the way a robber learns a road. First the heat. Then the story you tell yourself of how he wronged you. Then the need to be proved right in front of the others. Then the tongue running ahead of the mind. When you catch yourself rehearsing the quarrel at night, that is the band gathering. Do not draw. Stay silent, and go and carry water for the one you are angry with.
nodes.text_ru: Я знаю гнев изнутри: это было моё ремесло. Учись его следам, как разбойник учит дорогу. Сначала жар. Потом рассказ, который ты сам себе повторяешь, — как он тебя обидел. Потом нужда оказаться правым перед всеми. Потом язык, бегущий впереди ума. Когда поймаешь себя на том, что ночью повторяешь ссору, — это собирается шайка. Не вынимай ножа. Промолчи и пойди отнеси воды тому, на кого гневаешься.
nodes.meaning: Discernment cue for the passion of anger: rehearsing the offence, demanding vindication, speech outrunning reason. The cure is meekness, silence and a concrete service to the offender (Mt 5:23-24), never a holy object used as a weapon. The list of stages is the NPC's retelling of the Ladder and Cassian, not a quotation.
nodes.source: The Ladder of Divine Ascent, step 8; John Cassian, Institutes, book 8 (on anger); Palladius, Lausiac History 19 (carrying water to the brothers' cells); Matthew 5:22-24

branches.text: I will carry his water tonight.
branches.text_ru: Сегодня ночью я отнесу ему воды.

branches.text: And if he laughs at me for it?
branches.text_ru: А если он посмеётся надо мной за это?

nodes.text: A brother once came to me for a word. I told him: go and sit in your cell, and your cell will teach you everything. The road taught me to run. The cell taught me to stay. Water carried in the dark is not seen by anyone, and that is why it reaches the door.
nodes.text_ru: Однажды брат пришёл ко мне за словом. Я сказал ему: иди, сиди в своей келье, и келья научит тебя всему. Дорога научила меня бегать. Келья научила меня оставаться. Воду, которую несут в темноте, никто не видит, и потому она доходит до двери.
nodes.meaning: Stability in one's place and hidden service are a school of the soul; stillness is not an achievement to be counted. The bonus is for understanding why perseverance matters, never for time spent still.
nodes.source: Apophthegmata Patrum (alphabetical collection), Moses 6; Matthew 6:3-4

branches.text: Sitting still is harder than running.
branches.text_ru: Сидеть на месте труднее, чем бежать.

branches.text: What if the cell teaches me only my faults?
branches.text_ru: А если келья научит меня только моим грехам?

nodes.text: Then it teaches well, and you will not be afraid of the end. When the raiders came to Scetis, I told the brothers to flee, and I stayed. I had long waited for that day, for it is written that those who take the sword perish by the sword. I had laid my knife down years before, and I did not take it up again. The road I robbed on ended there, with me standing still.
nodes.text_ru: Значит, она учит хорошо, и ты не будешь бояться конца. Когда на Скит пришли разбойники, я велел братьям бежать, а сам остался. Я давно ждал этого дня, ибо написано, что взявшие меч мечом погибнут. Свой нож я положил много лет назад и больше его не поднял. Дорога, на которой я грабил, закончилась там, где я стоял неподвижно.
nodes.meaning: The saint ends the chain of violence in his own person and witnesses without resistance (Mt 26:52). His death is told as testimony, not as a mechanic, reward or achievement; he is commemorated on 28 August.
nodes.source: Apophthegmata Patrum (alphabetical collection), Moses (the barbarians' raid on Scetis); Matthew 26:52; Synaxarion, 28 August

branches.text: I will not take up the knife again, whatever my road.
branches.text_ru: Я больше не подниму ножа, какой бы ни была моя дорога.
branches.narrativeEffect: The elder picks up his water jar and walks toward the cells; he does not look back at what runs out behind him.

decisions: bias: the portrait shows a basket of sand, so the tree should tell the basket version / counter: the alphabetical Apophthegmata (Moses 2) has a leaking jar of water, and changing a saying to match a drawing invents a source / why: the saint tells the jar and names the basket as a popular variant, so text and art are both honest.

bias: the racial insult in Moses 3 is uncomfortable and should be cut / counter: it is the authentic setting of his silence, and cutting it erases who he was / why: it stays, framed as a trial he endured with dignity; the meaning field states that the game does not endorse the insult. Dissent (editor of language) kept: wants the word softened in the Russian; kept as 'чёрный' because 'Мурин' already carries it and the saying requires it.

bias: his death should be a climactic achievement node / counter: TABOO 0.4 rules 1 and 7, a witness is not a mechanic and the button may not say 'martyr' / why: last_night is reached only by Wisdom 8 through the cell teaching, the button speaks of the knife, and the reward is Faith and Wisdom for understanding the end of violence.

bias: a cunning player who wants to steer the council should be blocked / counter: the brief allows Cunning a rare +1 with a cost in meaning / why: the branch gives cunning +1 but leads straight to the leaking jar, which answers the scheme with the elder's own sins, and the narrativeEffect records a loss of the council's trust; it opens nothing deeper than an unconditioned branch already opens.

bias: the anger node should quote Moses directly / counter: the stage-by-stage description is our retelling of Ladder step 8 and Cassian, not a saying of Moses / why: voice stays 'paraphrase', no quotation marks, and the meaning field states that it is the NPC's retelling; only 'carry water to the brothers' comes from his Life.

bias: Moses is a desert father and does not belong in the Issyk-Kul Kiberslav world / counter: the style bible allows the ancient beside the instrumental, and his idiom is road, knife and water, which fits the caravan setting / why: his idiom stays in the desert and the road; no instruments or light classes are attached to him, and no nimbus is described. Skeptic dissent kept: his nodes should be linked to a concrete mission in the storylines matrix; none is named there yet, so it is left to the narrative voice.

(catechist) bias: Cassian's Abba Moses is simply Moses the Ethiopian / counter: scholars do not all identify the two, and stating it as fact overclaims the source / why: the theology field now says tradition links them; no node cites Cassian's Conferences as his own words.

(catechist) bias: vivid details (dawn on the roof, 'driven out for theft and blood') make the story live / counter: Moses 1 names no dawn, and Lausiac History 19 says he was dismissed for immorality and robbery and only reputed a killer / why: details are brought back to the sources; the paraphrase may add craft images, but not new facts about a saint.

(catechist) bias: Moses 1 is about fornication and should be named / counter: the tree is played by all ages, and the saying's point is hope in a long war / why: the text says 'old habits', and the meaning field states openly what the saying is about, so the theologian sees the true source.

(catechist, Aristotle-skeptic duty) bias: 'Sitting still is harder than running' deserves constitution +2 / counter: TABOO 0.35 rule 16, stillness is never paid as such / why: the reward is now wisdom +1 and constitution +1 for understanding perseverance; the rite itself is not paid for.

fixes: theology: Cassian's Conferences I-II are spoken by an Abba Moses of Scetis whom scholars do not all identify with Moses the Ethiopian. The source is now marked as one that tradition joins to him, so the attribution is no longer stated as certain.

robber_road: the Lausiac History 19 says Moses was dismissed by his master for immorality and robbery and was reputed to have killed a man. It does not say plainly that he was 'driven out for theft and blood', so the EN and RU text now follow what it says.

robber_road plus idiom: Moses 1 puts the vision on the roof terrace and names no dawn. 'At dawn' is removed from the text and from the idiom images, since the brief allows no invented detail in a saying.

robber_road meaning: it now says openly that in Moses 1 the warfare was with fornication, and that the NPC only tells it as 'old habits'. The source stays honest and the tree keeps a teen-safe register.

cell_teaches: the branch 'Sitting still is harder than running' paid constitution:2 for the idea of stillness itself. It now pays wisdom:1 and constitution:1, and the meaning says the bonus is for understanding perseverance, not for time spent still (TABOO 0.35 rule 16).

Checked and kept: Moses 1, 2, 3 and 6 match the alphabetical collection. Ps 77:4 = 76:5 LXX. Ladder step 8 = anger and meekness. Cassian's Institutes book 8 = anger. Lausiac History 19 = Moses, including the water jars at night. 28 August Synaxarion. The raid saying is left without a number as the author wrote it, because the number is not certain.

Mechanics checked: 7 nodes and all nextNodeIds resolve. The start node has 2 branches with no condition. There are 6 FORM-gated branches (thresholds 3-8). Cunning gets +1 once, has a cost in narrativeEffect, and opens nothing deeper. All bonuses are integers from 1 to 3. No forbidden words appear in choice texts, and no liturgical text is quoted.
dissent: Aristotle-skeptic: the start node offers the anger discernment cue at Constitution 4. It could be argued that recognising anger should be open to everyone, since it is the passion Moses knew best. This is kept gated because the author chose it and two unconditioned branches already exist, but it is recorded for the chorus.
Aristotle-skeptic: the raid saying (commonly cited as Moses 10) is left without a number because the number is not verified. Whoever next has the Ward edition in hand should add it.

Editor of language (from the author's decisions): wants the insult in the Russian of Moses 3 softened. The author kept 'чёрный', and the catechist agrees because the saying needs it; the dissent is preserved.

theology: Hospitality to the stranger (philoxenia) as a lived practice: the open gate, bread before merit, and discernment of the sadness that closes a house (Gen 18; Mt 25:35; Heb 13:2; 2 Cor 7:10). Anahit is an Armenian Christian of the Silk Road; she is drawn from her own tradition with dignity, and the game's doctrinal frame stays Orthodox.

idiom.worldview: A house is measured by how many strangers it can feed tonight, not by what it holds in the storeroom.
idiom.craft: Armenian innkeeper of the caravanserai on the Issyk-Kul shore, baker at the tonir, keeper of the gate and the well.
metaphors: Bread thin enough for any hand to tear
The rope wears at the lip of the well, not at the bucket
Count the camels in the morning, not at the gate
A house lives while its tonir is warm
Grief is a guest who sits down without being invited
idiom.silence: She does not answer; she hands you a strip of warm lavash and turns back to the oven. When asked where her church differs from yours she says only 'eat first' and changes the water in the jug.

nodes.text: Shake the dust off at the threshold, deacon; the tonir is still warm. On this shore a gate hangs on two hinges, bread and salt. Which of them brought you here?
nodes.text_ru: Отряхни пыль на пороге, дьякон, тонир ещё тёплый. На этом берегу ворота висят на двух петлях: хлеб и соль. Какая из них тебя привела?
nodes.meaning: Hospitality begins by receiving the stranger before asking who he is; the guest is fed before he is questioned, as Abraham ran to the three travellers before knowing them.

branches.text: Neither. I came to learn how you keep a house for strangers.
branches.text_ru: Ни та ни другая. Я пришёл учиться, как ты держишь дом для чужих.
branches.narrativeEffect: Anahit tears a sheet of lavash in two and gives you half.

branches.text: Let me carry water from the well first. Then ask me.
branches.text_ru: Дай сперва натаскать воды из колодца. Потом спросишь.
branches.narrativeEffect: She points to the rope without a word.

branches.text: Why does your gate stand open at night, when thieves walk the road too?
branches.text_ru: Почему твои ворота открыты ночью, когда по дороге ходят и воры?

nodes.text: I bake the lavash thin on purpose. A thick loaf waits for a knife, and a knife waits for a master. A thin sheet feeds whoever reaches first: the drover, the monk, the man who prays facing another way. Bread thin enough for any hand to tear.
nodes.text_ru: Лаваш я пеку тонким нарочно. Толстый каравай ждёт ножа, а нож ждёт хозяина. Тонкий лист кормит того, кто первым протянет руку: погонщика, монаха, человека, что молится в другую сторону. Хлеб, который порвёт любая рука.
nodes.meaning: Hospitality does not first sort the worthy from the unworthy; it gives without grudging to whoever comes, including those of another faith.

branches.text: And if the guest has nothing to pay with?
branches.text_ru: А если гостю нечем платить?

branches.text: Who pays the miller when every hand may tear the bread?
branches.text_ru: Кто платит мельнику, если хлеб рвёт любая рука?

nodes.text: You see the groove in the stone? The rope wears at the lip of the well, not at the bucket. A house is the same: it frays where it touches strangers. A house that never frays at the lip holds only stale water.
nodes.text_ru: Видишь желобок в камне? Верёвка стирается о край колодца, а не о ведро. И дом так же: он изнашивается там, где касается чужих. Дом, который нигде не стёрт о край, держит только стоячую воду.
nodes.meaning: Love is spent at the point of contact with others; a community closed to strangers stagnates. Brotherly love is kept by not forgetting the stranger.

branches.text: Then tell me the rule of your first night.
branches.text_ru: Тогда скажи, какой у тебя порядок первой ночи.

nodes.text: Thieves walk, yes. But a gate shut against thieves is shut against the tired as well, and on every road I know the tired outnumber the thieves. I keep a dog, a watchman and a clay lamp over the gate, so no one mistakes my door for a wall. A lock I do not keep.
nodes.text_ru: Воры ходят, да. Но ворота, закрытые от воров, закрыты и от усталых, а на всех дорогах, что я знаю, усталых больше, чем воров. У меня есть пёс, сторож и глиняный светильник над воротами, чтобы никто не принял мою дверь за стену. Замка я не держу.
nodes.meaning: Prudence and openness are held together; the risk of mercy is accepted rather than refused, as the Samaritan took the wounded man to the inn and paid for him without guarantee.

branches.text: What has the open gate cost you over the years?
branches.text_ru: Во что тебе обошлись открытые ворота за эти годы?

branches.text: Then teach me the rule of the first night.
branches.text_ru: Тогда научи меня порядку первой ночи.

nodes.text: My rule is short. The first night is free, the salt is free, the water is free. On the second morning we talk about fodder. My grandmother said: count the camels in the morning, not at the gate. At the gate you only open.
nodes.text_ru: Порядок у меня короткий. Первая ночь даром, соль даром, вода даром. На второе утро говорим о корме. Бабушка говорила: верблюдов считай утром, а не у ворот. У ворот только открывай.
nodes.meaning: The first reception is unconditional; reckoning and fair trade come afterwards and never stand at the threshold. In the Gospel's own sense (not as Anahit's claim), the stranger received is Christ received.

branches.text: Then the first night stays free, and I will stand at the gate with you.
branches.text_ru: Тогда первая ночь останется даром, и я постою у ворот вместе с тобой.
branches.narrativeEffect: Anahit hands you the gate key for the night.

branches.text: I will remember: count in the morning.
branches.text_ru: Запомню: считать утром.

nodes.text: There were years the stalls stood empty and I sat by a cold tonir. Grief came to me twice. First came honest sorrow for the drivers lost on the pass, and that one still swept the yard. Then came a second guest who sat down without being invited and ate all the bread, and it said: nothing will ever come back, why bother. It also told me to bar the gate, so no one would see the empty stalls. Learn to tell them apart, deacon. The first sorrow sweeps and lets people in. The second sits, shuts the gate and tells you to stop sweeping.
nodes.text_ru: Были годы, когда стойла стояли пустыми, а я сидела у холодного тонира. Горе приходило ко мне дважды. Сначала пришла честная печаль по погонщикам, что остались на перевале, и она всё ещё мела двор. Потом пришёл второй гость, сел без приглашения, съел весь хлеб и сказал: ничего уже не вернётся, зачем стараться. Он же велел мне запереть ворота, чтобы никто не видел пустых стойл. Научись их различать, дьякон. Первая печаль метёт и впускает людей. Вторая сидит, запирает ворота и говорит тебе бросить метлу.
nodes.meaning: Discernment cue for the passion of sadness (lype). Godly sorrow keeps the hands working and leads to repentance and life. Worldly sadness sits, closes off the future ('nothing will return') and cuts a person off from others; if left alone it opens the door to despondency and despair. The signs are the stopped hand, the tomorrow that seems closed and the barred gate. It is met by hope and by not keeping the grief alone, and never by a holy object or a rite paid in points.
nodes.source: 2 Cor 7:10; St John Cassian, Institutes, book 9 (on the spirit of dejection); St John Climacus, The Ladder, step 7 (on joy-making mourning, the godly side of sorrow); Evagrius, Praktikos (on the eight thoughts: sadness)

branches.text: So the sign is this: one sorrow sweeps, the other sits and bars the gate.
branches.text_ru: Значит, признак такой: одна печаль метёт, другая сидит и запирает ворота.
branches.narrativeEffect: She nods and puts the broom into your hands.

branches.text: I will remember the two guests.
branches.text_ru: Я запомню двух гостей.

nodes.text: Go now. If you come back at night, knock twice, the dog knows that knock. And if one day you find my gate shut, do not think the house has died. Put your hand to the tonir. A house lives while someone still bakes for a stranger.
nodes.text_ru: Ступай. Если вернёшься ночью, стучи дважды, пёс знает этот стук. А если однажды найдёшь мои ворота закрытыми, не думай, что дом умер. Приложи руку к тониру. Дом жив, пока в нём кто-то печёт для чужого.
nodes.meaning: Hospitality is a living practice handed on, not an institution; the deacon is sent to keep an open gate in his own house, for what is done to the least is done to Christ.

branches.text: I will keep a gate of my own.
branches.text_ru: Я буду держать свои ворота.

branches.text: Thank you for the bread.
branches.text_ru: Спасибо за хлеб.

decisions: bias: Anahit is Armenian, so she should argue her church against the deacon's / counter: TABOO 0.37 p.4 wants non-Orthodox partners drawn with dignity and without pressure either way / why: her 'silence' refuses the confessional quarrel with 'eat first'; doctrine is carried by Scripture both sides share, and the game's frame stays Orthodox.

bias: an Armenian hostess would quote Armenian teachers (Nerses the Gracious, Narekatsi) / counter: TABOO 0.2 p.1 shows only Orthodox saints in-game / why: she cites only Scripture and the Orthodox Ladder/Evagrius in the source field; no non-Orthodox saint is named. Dissent kept (historian): this thins her ethnographic voice; left for the chorus to revisit.

bias: the lamp over her gate is the lampada from the matrix, so she can talk about it / counter: TABOO 0.4 p.1 and 0.38: the lampada is a holy light, not a household tool / why: she speaks of an ordinary clay lamp for travellers; the lampada stays silent, noInteract.

bias: the passion node for an innkeeper must be avarice (storyline 1) / counter: the storyline of the emptied caravanserai (sea routes) gives her a lived experience of sadness, and Melik already carries avarice / why: one passion per NPC, not duplicated; sadness taught via 2 Cor 7:10 with the cue 'the sorrow that sits and stops the hands'.

bias: standing at the gate at night is a rite and should pay Faith / counter: CLAUDE.md 0.35 p.16 forbids paying rites in attributes / why: the Faith +2 is for choosing unconditional reception (understanding Mt 25:35), not for a prayer or vigil.

bias: 'Count the camels in the morning' is my invented proverb and could pass as folk quotation / counter: TABOO 0.35 p.18 forbids invented quotations of Fathers / why: it is marked as her grandmother's saying inside her own idiom, not attributed to any Father or scripture; the source field points to Mt 25:35 only for the meaning.

bias: FORM gates should be Wisdom only / counter: 0.35 p.14 / why: gates use constitution 3, erudition 3, wisdom 4, faith 4, wisdom 6, wisdom 8; the start node has an unconditional branch; no Cunning at all in her tree because she offers no temptation.

bias (catechist): The Ladder, step 7 is the natural source for 'sadness' / counter: step 7 is on joy-making mourning (penthos); the Ladder has no separate step on sadness, and step 13 is on despondency / why: step 7 is kept only for the godly-sorrow side of the contrast; St John Cassian, Institutes book 9 (on dejection) carries the passion; Evagrius is cited by work title only, because the eight-thought scheme is his but a chapter number was not verified.

bias (catechist): the passion cue 'the hand stops' is enough / counter: Cassian's teaching on dejection stresses that it makes a person unwilling to receive others and shut in on himself / why: a second, visible cue fits her craft exactly (the barred gate), so the player can recognise sadness in a hostess's own trade without any holy object.

bias (catechist): 'the stranger received is Christ received' could be read as Anahit's own confession, put in her mouth / counter: TABOO 0.37 asks for dignity without drawing a non-Orthodox character into the game's doctrine / why: the meaning field marks it as the sense of Mt 25:35, 40 for the theologian; her spoken line stays in her idiom of camels and gates.

bias (Aristotle-skeptic): the wisdom-8 branch only restates the cue and earns +3 / counter: naming the cue in one's own words is the act of discernment the node teaches / why: kept at +3; dissent recorded for playtest review.

fixes: a_empty.source: The Ladder, step 7 is on joy-making mourning (penthos), not on the passion of sadness (lype). The Ladder has no separate step on sadness; step 13 is on despondency. The citation is now labelled as the godly-sorrow side of the contrast, and St John Cassian, Institutes, book 9 (on the spirit of dejection) is added as the main patristic source for the passion. Evagrius stays, cited by work title only with no chapter number.

a_empty.meaning: the text now says where worldly sadness leads if it is left alone: it opens the door to despondency (akedia) and despair. The cure is named as hope and not keeping the grief alone, drawn from 2 Cor 7:10 and Cassian. No holy object and no rite is used against it.

a_empty.text / text_ru: added one line in her idiom: the second guest also talks you out of letting anyone else into the house. This gives a second discernment cue (sadness isolates) that comes from Cassian's teaching on dejection, without quoting him.

a_first_night.meaning: 'the stranger received is Christ received' is now marked as the Gospel's sense (Mt 25:35, 40), not as anything Anahit claims. The bonus is kept for understanding, not for keeping watch.
decisions: added a catechist decision, a skeptic dissent and a historian note. All of the author's decisions are kept.
dissent: Aristotle-skeptic: the a_empty node's wisdom-8 branch rewards the player for restating the cue ('one sorrow sweeps, the other sits'). That repeats the lesson without applying it. The +3 Wisdom is high for an echo. Kept, because the choice names the cue in the player's own words, which counts as understanding. The chorus should revisit it if playtests show players pick it only for the points.

Aristotle-skeptic: the tree has no Cunning branch. The contract allows this, but the player never gets a chance to test the gate by haggling. Not added: Melik carries avarice, and Anahit has no temptation to offer.

Historian (kept from author): quoting only Scripture and Orthodox Fathers thins Anahit's Armenian voice. The chorus may later decide whether a non-quoted reference to her own people's customs, such as bread and salt at the threshold, is enough.

theology: Wisdom offered to Christ: reason is a road that leads to the Word but does not replace Him (1 Cor 1:20-25; Acts 17:22-28); argument with meekness (1 Pet 3:15); firmness without pride.

idiom.worldview: An argument is honest only if it leaves the other person freer than it found him.
idiom.craft: Alexandrian scholar and disputant: reads the poets and philosophers, answers in the hall of the emperor, weighs premises like coins on a scale.
metaphors: reason is a road, not the house
a premise is a foundation stone; test it before you build
the one who argues to win loses the listener
a broken wheel answers more than a whole speech
applause is a coin that buys nothing
idiom.silence: She closes the book mid-sentence and lets the silence do the refuting; to one who wants only to win she answers with a question and waits.

nodes.text: Sit. In Alexandria we began every disputation with the terms: what do you mean by the word you use? Most quarrels die there, happily. Which road did you come by: to listen, to ask, or to win?
nodes.text_ru: Садись. В Александрии мы начинали всякий спор с определений: что ты разумеешь под словом, которым пользуешься? Большая часть ссор на этом и кончается, к счастью. Какой дорогой ты пришёл: послушать, спросить или победить?
nodes.meaning: Catherine introduces herself through the method of honest dialectic: defining terms before arguing. The meeting is open to anyone; the three roads foreshadow the three dispositions.
nodes.source: Menologion of St Dimitry of Rostov, 24 November; Synaxarion, 24 November (Slavic usage; 25 November in Greek usage)

branches.text: To listen to how you argued.
branches.text_ru: Послушать, как ты спорила.

branches.text: Can reason alone reach God?
branches.text_ru: Может ли разум сам дойти до Бога?

branches.text: Which books had you read before you answered them?
branches.text_ru: Какие книги ты прочла, прежде чем им ответить?

branches.text: Teach me to win any argument.
branches.text_ru: Научи меня выигрывать любой спор.
branches.narrativeEffect: Ungated: Cunning opens nothing here; the +1 is the cost of asking for a technique of winning.

nodes.text: The emperor gathered fifty of the best orators of the empire against one girl. He expected a spectacle. I did not try to humble them; I tried to show them where their own poets and philosophers had been pointing. They saw it and said so aloud, and they paid for saying it. I did not win them. The truth did, and they chose it.
nodes.text_ru: Император собрал против одной девушки пятьдесят лучших риторов державы. Он ждал зрелища. Я не пыталась их унизить; я пыталась показать им, куда указывали их же поэты и философы. Они увидели и сказали это вслух, и заплатили за это. Я их не победила. Их убедила истина, и они её выбрали.
nodes.meaning: According to her Life, Catherine's disputation with the philosophers led them to faith, for which they were executed. The point is not rhetorical triumph but truth freely accepted.
nodes.source: Menologion of St Dimitry of Rostov, 24 November (Life of Great-martyr Catherine)

branches.text: Then what is reason for, if it does not win?
branches.text_ru: Тогда зачем разум, если он не побеждает?

branches.text: And the wheel they prepared for you?
branches.text_ru: А колесо, которое для тебя приготовили?

nodes.text: Reason is a road, and a good one; I walked it every day. But a road is not the house. Paul stood among the Athenians and found an altar to an unknown god; he did not mock it, he said: the One you honour without knowing, Him I proclaim. The wisdom of this world, taken as the house, becomes foolishness. Taken as the road, it arrives at a door that only opens from within.
nodes.text_ru: Разум — дорога, и хорошая; я ходила по ней каждый день. Но дорога — не дом. Павел стоял среди афинян и нашёл жертвенник неведомому богу; он не посмеялся, он сказал: Того, Кого вы, не зная, чтите, я и проповедую. Мудрость мира сего, если принять её за дом, становится безумием. Если принять её за дорогу, она доводит до двери, которая отворяется только изнутри.
nodes.meaning: Natural reason can lead toward God but cannot replace revelation; Paul at the Areopagus shows respectful use of pagan thought as a pointer. God is known by His self-revelation, not by syllogism alone.
nodes.source: Acts 17:22-28; 1 Corinthians 1:20-25

branches.text: How do I know when I argue for truth and when for myself?
branches.text_ru: Как понять, когда я спорю за истину, а когда за себя?

branches.text: How should I answer when someone asks me why I believe?
branches.text_ru: Как отвечать, когда меня спрашивают, почему я верю?

nodes.text: All of them I could reach: the poets, the physicians, the philosophers of Athens and our own city. You cannot answer a man in a language you have not bothered to learn. But I noticed that the more I read, the more every shelf ended in a question it could not close. The books were honest. They admitted the door.
nodes.text_ru: Все, до каких могла дотянуться: поэтов, врачей, философов Афин и нашего города. Нельзя отвечать человеку на языке, который ты не потрудился выучить. Но я заметила: чем больше читаю, тем чаще каждая полка заканчивается вопросом, который она не может закрыть. Книги были честны. Они признавали дверь.
nodes.meaning: Her Life presents her as learned in the philosophy and poetry of her time; learning is respected and used to serve the other person, and it honestly leads to the limits of human knowledge.
nodes.source: Menologion of St Dimitry of Rostov, 24 November; Basil the Great, Address to Young Men on the Right Use of Greek Literature

branches.text: Then what should reason do at that door?
branches.text_ru: Что же делать разуму у этой двери?

nodes.text: I can teach you that; it is the easiest thing in Alexandria. Define the terms to suit yourself, speak faster, keep the audience laughing. You will win every hall and lose every person in it. And you will begin to love the sound of the hall more than the face in front of you. Is that the scale you want to be weighed on?
nodes.text_ru: Этому я могу научить; это самое лёгкое в Александрии. Определи слова под себя, говори быстрее, держи зал смеющимся. Ты выиграешь каждый зал и потеряешь в нём каждого человека. И начнёшь любить шум зала больше, чем лицо перед тобой. На таких ли весах ты хочешь быть взвешен?
nodes.meaning: Sophistry is named for what it is. The +1 Cunning is a cost: the technique of winning feeds vainglory and loses the neighbour. The Cunning route opens no deeper teaching: it leads only to this refutation and on to the meek answer; the detailed discernment of vainglory stays behind the same Wisdom threshold as on every other route.
nodes.source: 1 Corinthians 13:1; John Climacus, The Ladder, Step 22 (On Vainglory)

branches.text: No. Tell me how to notice when I am doing that.
branches.text_ru: Нет. Скажи, как заметить, что я это делаю.

branches.text: No. Then how should I answer instead?
branches.text_ru: Нет. Как же тогда отвечать?

nodes.text: Three marks, weigh them like coins. First: while the other speaks, you are already composing your reply. Second: your eyes go to the listeners, not to the one you answer. Third: after you are right, you want someone to have seen it. That thought is vainglory; the fathers said it steals even from good work, because it pays you in applause. You need no weapon against it. Notice it, and turn your eyes back to the face in front of you.
nodes.text_ru: Три признака, взвесь их, как монеты. Первый: пока другой говорит, ты уже сочиняешь ответ. Второй: глаза твои ищут слушателей, а не того, кому ты отвечаешь. Третий: оказавшись правым, ты хочешь, чтобы кто-нибудь это видел. Этот помысл — тщеславие; отцы говорили, что он крадёт даже у доброго дела, потому что расплачивается рукоплесканиями. Оружие против него не нужно. Заметь его и верни взгляд к лицу перед тобой.
nodes.meaning: Discernment cue for the passion of vainglory: attention shifted from truth and neighbour to the audience and recognition. It is overcome by watchfulness and attention to the other, not by a sacred object. The three marks are Catherine's own teaching image, not a quotation of the Fathers.
nodes.source: John Climacus, The Ladder, Step 22 (On Vainglory); Evagrius Ponticus, Praktikos (on the eight thoughts, vainglory)

branches.text: Then how should I answer, if not to win?
branches.text_ru: Как же тогда отвечать, если не ради победы?

nodes.text: They built a wheel with spikes to break my argument where words had failed. It broke before I did. Do not make a lesson of the machine; make it of the answer. An argument is worth what you are willing to pay for it. The philosophers paid with their lives, and so did I. Firmness is not loudness. It is staying where the truth stands when the hall empties.
nodes.text_ru: Они построили колесо с шипами, чтобы сломать мой довод там, где не справились слова. Оно сломалось раньше меня. Не делай урока из машины; делай его из ответа. Довод стоит столько, сколько ты готов за него заплатить. Философы заплатили жизнью, и я тоже. Твёрдость — не громкость. Это умение остаться там, где стоит истина, когда зал опустел.
nodes.meaning: The broken wheel of her Life is told as witness, not as a miracle mechanic: faithfulness costs, and firmness is steadfastness without pride. No power, item, VFX reward or bonus is tied to the event itself; the bonus on the next choice is for the player's understanding.
nodes.source: Menologion of St Dimitry of Rostov, 24 November; Revelation 2:10

branches.text: I would rather learn to stay than to shout.
branches.text_ru: Я лучше научусь оставаться, чем кричать.

nodes.text: Be always ready to give an answer for the hope in you, the apostle says, but with meekness and fear. Meekness: you do not need to crush him. Fear: you might be wrong about yourself, even if not about God. Leave a pause after your best premise. The best disputation ends with the other free to walk away, and still wanting to come back.
nodes.text_ru: Будь всегда готов дать ответ о твоём уповании, говорит апостол, но с кротостью и благоговением. Кротость: тебе не нужно его сокрушать. Благоговение: ты можешь ошибаться в себе, даже если не ошибаешься о Боге. Оставь паузу после лучшего своего довода. Лучший спор кончается тем, что другой свободен уйти и всё же хочет вернуться.
nodes.meaning: Christian apologetics is witness with meekness and reverence, respecting the freedom of the other; no pressure, no forced conversion.
nodes.source: 1 Peter 3:15; Galatians 5:22-23

branches.text: I will leave the pause.
branches.text_ru: Я оставлю паузу.

decisions: bias: Catherine as patroness of riddles should hand out solutions or a +Erudition 'riddle key' / counter: a saint is not a buff or a key (TABOO 0.4 p.1, 0.35 p.16) / why: her gift is the method of dialectic (define terms, test premises, meekness); Erudition bonuses reward understanding in the dialogue, not her intercession.

bias: the broken wheel is a spectacular miracle and would make a great VFX reward / counter: TABOO 0.37 forbids miracles as mechanics; the wheel is an instrument of execution / why: the wheel is spoken of as witness and cost ('an argument is worth what you pay'), no power granted, no particle reward.

bias: 'she defeated fifty philosophers' makes her a debate champion / counter: her Life says the philosophers came to faith and died for it; triumph over persons would feed the very vainglory she teaches against / why: node kat_fifty says the truth persuaded them and they chose it.

bias: the Cunning path ('teach me to win') should be refused outright / counter: refusing teaches nothing; the Aristotle voice insists the sophist be refuted by definition / why: +1 Cunning with the cost stated in meaning, then redirect to discernment.

bias (Aristotle-skeptic dissent, recorded): the user request speaks of scenes for 'the other 12 sacraments'. counter: Orthodox catechesis (St Philaret) counts seven; I will not build a 12-item list on a false premise / why: Catherine's own idiom is 'define the terms first'; the sacramental scene set must be defined by the catechist and dogmatist before scenes are drawn, and none of it is placed inside her tree. Catechist confirms: seven mysteries (Extended Catechism of St Philaret).
bias: feast date is simply 25 November / counter: Slavic usage keeps 24 November, Greek usage 25 November / why: source records both to avoid a false precision.

dissent kept: the game-designer voice wanted a direct Wisdom-only gate at the start; I kept one Wisdom and one Erudition gate plus an ungated 'listen' branch so a guest with all attributes at 1 is still received (Constitution, TABOO 0.35 p.14).

bias (catechist): a Cunning 4 gate on 'teach me to win' is harmless flavour / counter: a Cunning condition is Cunning opening a door, and it led via kat_winning to kat_vainglory, bypassing the Wisdom 8 gate of kat_reason / why: the Cunning condition is removed (anyone may ask, +1 cunning is the cost), kat_winning -> kat_vainglory now needs wisdom 8 like every other route, and an ungated kat_winning -> kat_meek keeps the sophist from a dead end.

bias (Aristotle-skeptic, dissent kept): the repentant sophist most needs the vainglory cue, so gating it is harsh / counter: the ungated kat_meek already gives the remedy (meekness, the pause); the detailed marks stay behind one consistent FORM threshold / why: otherwise Cunning becomes a shortcut to deeper teaching (Constitution, TABOO 0.35 p.14).

bias: Evagrius Praktikos can be cited with a chapter number / counter: no chapter was verified in this review / why: cited by work and topic only, per the no-fabricated-numbers rule; Ladder Step 22 On Vainglory is verified.

bias: 'lamp of the scholar' is a neutral image / counter: in the Kiberslav style the lampada (1800 K) belongs only to the holy / why: renamed 'reading lamp (oil wick)', human-work light class 1900-2500 K (TABOO 0.38 p.1).

dissent kept (Aristotle-skeptic): 'crown' and 'palm branch' are martyr attributes and could drift toward reward imagery / counter: they belong to her Life (royal birth, witness) and live only in her speech, never as items / why: kept, flagged for the iconographer.

fixes: Cunning gate removed from start branch 'Teach me to win any argument': Cunning no longer opens anything; the choice is open to all and pays only +1 cunning as a stated cost (TABOO 0.35 p.14, contract p.5).

Cunning bypass closed: kat_winning -> kat_vainglory previously let a Cunning 4 player reach the discernment teaching that kat_reason gates at Wisdom 8. The branch now carries condition wisdom 8 (same threshold as the other route), and an ungated branch kat_winning -> kat_meek was added so the repentant sophist is never stranded.
kat_vainglory source: Evagrius cited by work only (Praktikos, on the eight thoughts), no chapter number; Ladder Step 22 (On Vainglory) verified and kept.
kat_winning meaning expanded to state explicitly that the Cunning route leads only to the refutation node and to the meek answer, never around a FORM gate.

Idiom image 'lamp of the scholar' renamed 'reading lamp (oil wick)' so it stays in the human-work light class (1900-2500 K) and is not confused with the shrine lampada (1800 K, Style Bible / TABOO 0.38 p.1).

kat_wheel meaning clarified: the Life says the wheel was shattered; it is told as witness, grants no item, VFX or bonus for the event itself; the bonus is for the player's choice to learn steadfastness.

Checked and kept: 8 nodes, all nextNodeIds resolve, ungated start branch (listen), FORM gates wisdom 6 / erudition 8 / faith 7 / wisdom 8, bonuses integers 1-3, voice paraphrase on every node, no forbidden words in choice texts, no liturgical text quoted (1 Pet 3:15 and Acts 17:23 are paraphrased Scripture with references), fifty philosophers and their execution match the Menologion of St Dimitry of Rostov (24 Nov; 25 Nov Greek usage), Basil's Address to Young Men is a real work, Seven sacraments per St Philaret confirmed.
dissent: Aristotle-skeptic (kept): gating the sophist's repentance route at Wisdom 8 is harsh; the one who has just been shown his own temptation arguably needs the discernment cue most. Catechist's answer: the ungated kat_meek answer already teaches the remedy (meekness, the pause); the detailed marks of vainglory stay behind the same FORM threshold on every route, otherwise Cunning becomes a shortcut.

Aristotle-skeptic (kept): 'crown' and 'palm branch' in the idiom are iconographic martyr attributes and could drift toward reward imagery. Kept because they belong to her Life (royal birth, witness) and appear only in her speech, never as items; flagged for the iconographer voice.
Author's recorded dissent on the '12 sacraments' premise is kept verbatim; the catechist confirms it: the Extended Catechism of St Philaret counts seven mysteries.

theology: Hesychasm: watchfulness (nepsis), guarding the heart, the Jesus Prayer united with breath, stillness as the ground of self-knowledge; discernment of thoughts. Composite fictional elder (not a canonised saint): he speaks in his own voice and cites the Fathers only by reference, never by invented quotation.

idiom.worldview: The heart is a cell with one door; the work is to guard that door, not to decorate the room.
idiom.craft: Cell-keeper and rope-knotter: by the lamp he ties prayer ropes of black wool, trims the wick and sits with the novices' thoughts.
metaphors: Muddy water clears when the jug is left still.
The heart has one door, and a watchman stands at it.
A knot is tied, not counted.
The noon sun that will not move is a thief at the window.
A lamp is trimmed, not fanned.
idiom.silence: Before answering he ties one knot in silence; when refused he trims the wick and says nothing more that day.

nodes.text: You came in with the road still on your boots. Sit. The jug on the bench is muddy from the spring. Let us both watch it a while before we speak.
nodes.text_ru: Ты вошёл, а дорога ещё на сапогах. Садись. Кувшин на лавке мутный, из родника. Давай оба посмотрим на него, прежде чем говорить.
nodes.meaning: Stillness comes before the word: a mind stirred by passions grows clear when it is left at rest before God. The meeting itself is the first teaching.
nodes.source: Psalm 45:11 (LXX; 46:10 in Hebrew numbering); Apophthegmata Patrum, systematic collection, book On stillness (hesychia): the saying of the three friends and the basin of water.

branches.text: I will sit and watch the water.
branches.text_ru: Я посижу и посмотрю на воду.
branches.narrativeEffect: The elder ties one knot and nods toward the jug.

branches.text: Why must the water settle before we speak?
branches.text_ru: Почему вода должна отстояться прежде слов?
branches.narrativeEffect: He sets the rope down: the question was asked from the right side of the door.

branches.text: Teach me the short word you knot into the rope.
branches.text_ru: Научи меня короткому слову, что ты вяжешь в узлы.

branches.text: Just give me the rule. I have little time.
branches.text_ru: Просто скажи правило. У меня мало времени.
branches.narrativeEffect: Cost: the jug stays muddy; the elder turns to the lamp, and the deeper talk is closed until you return by the long way.

branches.text: I have come to lay my sins before you.
branches.text_ru: Я пришёл открыть тебе свои грехи.

nodes.text: See, the silt is going down. Now you can see your own face in it. Your thoughts are the same silt. In the town they shake the jug all day; here we only stop shaking it.
nodes.text_ru: Видишь, муть оседает. Теперь в воде видно твоё лицо. Помыслы — та же муть. В городе кувшин трясут весь день, а здесь мы просто перестаём его трясти.
nodes.meaning: Stillness (hesychia) is not emptiness but the state in which a man sees himself truthfully; self-knowledge precedes the knowledge of God.
nodes.source: Apophthegmata Patrum, systematic collection, book On stillness (hesychia): the saying of the three friends and the basin of water; Matthew 6:6.

branches.text: And when the water is clear, what then?
branches.text_ru: А когда вода станет чистой, что тогда?

branches.text: The noon hour drags here. I keep looking at the door.
branches.text_ru: Полдень здесь тянется. Я всё смотрю на дверь.

nodes.text: The mind is a wanderer; it slips out through every window. We do not beat it. We bring it home the way I draw a loose end back through the knot, gently, down into the heart, and we set a watchman at the one door. Whatever knocks, he asks it: are you ours, or theirs?
nodes.text_ru: Ум — странник, он ускользает в каждое окно. Мы его не бьём. Мы возвращаем его домой, как я протягиваю свободный конец обратно сквозь узел, бережно, вниз, в сердце, и ставим у единственной двери сторожа. Кто бы ни постучал, сторож спрашивает: ты наш или чужой?
nodes.meaning: Watchfulness (nepsis): the mind gathered into the heart guards it by attention and tests each thought at its first approach, before consent.
nodes.source: Proverbs 4:23; Hesychius of Sinai, On Watchfulness and Holiness (Philokalia, vol. 1).

branches.text: The Fathers name the steps by which a thought comes in. Where does the watchman stop it?
branches.text_ru: Отцы называют ступени, по которым входит помысел. Где сторож его останавливает?

branches.text: How does the watchman stay awake?
branches.text_ru: Как сторожу не уснуть?

nodes.text: First a knock: the thought only shows its face. Then a talk with it. Then a nod. Then the hand given, and you are led off like a captive. Then the wrestling, when you fight back too late. Last, the habit that lives in the house as its master. The watchman is strong at the knock and weak at the handshake. Tie your knot at the knock.
nodes.text_ru: Сначала стук: помысел только показывает лицо. Потом беседа с ним. Потом кивок. Потом протянутая рука, и тебя уводят, как пленника. Потом борьба, когда отбиваешься слишком поздно. И последнее — привычка, что живёт в доме хозяином. Сторож силён у стука и слаб у рукопожатия. Вяжи свой узел у стука.
nodes.meaning: The patristic analysis of temptation: suggestion (prosbole), coupling, assent, captivity, struggle, passion. Resistance is easiest at the first stage, before the thought is entertained.
nodes.source: John Climacus, The Ladder of Divine Ascent, Step 15.

branches.text: Then I will stand at the knock.
branches.text_ru: Тогда я буду стоять у стука.
branches.narrativeEffect: The elder ties one knot and hands you the end of the rope to hold, not to keep.

branches.text: And what does the watchman say at the knock?
branches.text_ru: А что сторож говорит у стука?

nodes.text: The short word is the blind man's cry at the roadside to the One passing by: His Name, and have mercy. It goes with the breath, as the rope goes through the fingers. But hear me: a knot is tied, not counted. The rope is not an abacus. If you count in order to be paid, you have opened a shop in the cell.
nodes.text_ru: Короткое слово — это крик слепого у дороги Тому, Кто проходит мимо: Его Имя и «помилуй». Оно идёт с дыханием, как вервица идёт через пальцы. Но слушай: узел вяжут, а не считают. Вервица — не счёты. Если считаешь, чтобы тебе заплатили, ты открыл в келье лавку.
nodes.meaning: The Jesus Prayer grows from the cry of the blind man and the publican and is joined to the breath; it is neither a technique for gain nor a measure of merit. The game may show the count but never pays for it; the deeper gate is given, not earned.
nodes.source: Luke 18:38; Luke 18:13; John Climacus, The Ladder of Divine Ascent, Step 27 (on stillness: the remembrance of Jesus joined to the breath).

branches.text: If it is not counted, what does it measure?
branches.text_ru: Если не считать, то что же оно мерит?
branches.narrativeEffect: He does not answer. He trims the wick, and the room is quieter than before: that is the answer. The door he guards is opened from the other side, not bought.

branches.text: I understand: the rope is not an abacus.
branches.text_ru: Понимаю: вервица — не счёты.

nodes.text: Ah, the noon sun that will not move. You look at the door, you think of the brother who has it easier, of the house across the lake where the bread is better. That is the thief at the window. Know him by three marks: time stands still, another place looks greener, and the work in your hands looks useless. He does not fight you. He only asks you to leave.
nodes.text_ru: А, полуденное солнце, что не сдвигается. Смотришь на дверь, думаешь о брате, которому легче, об обители за озером, где хлеб лучше. Это вор у окна. Узнавай его по трём приметам: время стоит, чужое место кажется зеленее, а дело в руках — бесполезным. Он с тобой не воюет. Он только просит уйти.
nodes.meaning: Discernment cue for the passion of despondency (acedia, уныние): the day seems endless, the eye goes to the window, another place is desired, present work is despised. The remedy is staying and patient work, not a holy object used as a weapon.
nodes.source: Psalm 90:6 (LXX; 91:6 in Hebrew numbering); Evagrius Ponticus, Praktikos, ch. 12; John Climacus, The Ladder of Divine Ascent, Step 13; Apophthegmata Patrum, alphabetical collection, Anthony the Great 1.

branches.text: Then I stay, and my hands keep working.
branches.text_ru: Тогда я остаюсь, и руки продолжают работу.
branches.narrativeEffect: The elder passes you wool and a half-tied rope: the work, not the count, is what he gives.

branches.text: How do I send him away?
branches.text_ru: Как его прогнать?

nodes.text: A rule, quickly? Here is the quickest one the old men knew: sit in your cell, and your cell will teach you everything. You smile; it is too slow for you. Then the jug stays muddy. I will not argue. The lamp needs trimming.
nodes.text_ru: Правило, да побыстрее? Вот самое быстрое, что знали старцы: сиди в келье, и келья научит тебя всему. Ты улыбаешься — для тебя это слишком медленно. Тогда кувшин останется мутным. Спорить не стану. Фитиль пора поправить.
nodes.meaning: There is no shortcut to watchfulness; haste itself is a symptom. Cunning seeks a technique instead of a change of heart and receives nothing deeper.
nodes.source: Apophthegmata Patrum, alphabetical collection, Moses 6 (retold by the elder as the old men's word, not quoted or signed).

branches.text: Forgive me. I will sit.
branches.text_ru: Прости. Я посижу.

branches.text: Then I will find the rule somewhere else.
branches.text_ru: Тогда найду правило в другом месте.
branches.narrativeEffect: The elder trims the wick and does not look up.

nodes.text: Stop, brother. Sins are laid down in the church, before the priest, and it is Christ who receives them there, not an old man with a rope by the roadside. Here I can only sit with your thoughts: tell me what knocks at your door, and we will learn the knock together. And when you are ready, go down to the church. That road is real.
nodes.text_ru: Постой, брат. Грехи слагают в храме, перед священником, и принимает их там Христос, а не старик с вервицей у дороги. Здесь я могу только посидеть с твоими помыслами: скажи, что стучит в твою дверь, и мы вместе научимся узнавать стук. А когда будешь готов, спустись в храм. Та дорога настоящая.
nodes.meaning: The game does not perform or simulate any sacrament: confession, like the Eucharist, belongs to the living Church. In the game the elder offers only the monastic revealing of thoughts as teaching in discernment, and points the player beyond the game.
nodes.source: John 20:22-23; 1 John 1:9; John Climacus, The Ladder of Divine Ascent, Step 4.

branches.text: Then teach me to recognise what knocks.
branches.text_ru: Тогда научи меня узнавать, что стучит.

branches.text: I will remember the road to the church.
branches.text_ru: Я запомню дорогу в храм.
branches.narrativeEffect: The elder ties one knot and, for once, says nothing about the lamp.

decisions: bias: a mentor should hear the player's confession, many websites offer this / counter: the operator (2026-09-29): the game does not perform a sacrament; confession and the Eucharist belong to the living Church / why: node not_the_priest refuses the rite, keeps only the revealing of thoughts as discernment teaching and points the player to a real church; the bonus is +1 wisdom for understanding the distinction, never faith for performing a rite.

bias: the old seed tree paid +3 wisdom and +2 constitution for promising 40 prayers a day / counter: TABOO 0.35 rule 16: prayer is never XP; a knot is tied, not counted / why: the rite branch was replaced by 'the rope is not an abacus'; bonuses are paid only for understanding. Dissent (game designer): players need a visible reward loop; answered: the gate counter is shown, not paid.

bias: quote the Jesus Prayer verbatim, as the old tree did / counter: TABOO 0.2 p.4 and 0.39 p.4: the prayer is not paraphrased or used as a UI line / why: the elder points to its Gospel roots (Luke 18:38, 18:13) in living speech and never turns it into a formula on a button.

bias: Sergius is venerable, so give him voice 'paraphrase' with patristic sayings in quotes / counter: he is a composite fictional elder; TABOO 0.35 rule 18 forbids signing words with a Father's name / why: voice 'own', Fathers cited only as sources; the Moses 6 and Anthony 1 sayings are paraphrased, not quoted.

bias: the Ladder stages of a thought are in Step 15 / counter (Skeptic): verify against the text before merge / why: kept at Step 15, where the stages of assent are traditionally located; the theologian must confirm before the PR is merged.

bias: a Cunning shortcut should lead somewhere useful / counter: Cunning never opens deeper teaching / why: the shortcut node gives +1 cunning with a stated cost (the deeper talk closes) and loops back to still water only through an apology.

bias: fight despondency with the prayer rope as a weapon / counter: TABOO 0.35 rule 13: no holy object against a passion / why: the acedia node teaches three recognition marks and the remedy of staying and working (Anthony 1: plaiting rope).
