bias (liturgist): the ison is the natural sound of Kassia's choir / counter (Aristotle-skeptic, patrologist): the sustained ison is attested in later Byzantine and post-Byzantine chant, not securely in the 9th century / why: kept as the game's sacred-sound idiom (TABOO 0.35 rule 10) and flagged in meaning; dissent kept.
bias: Russian 'крюки' reads naturally for church notation / counter (language editor, historian): kryuki are Russian znamenny notation, anachronistic in Byzantium / why: replaced with 'невмы'.
bias: Kassia's own honey-and-medicine line / counter (patrologist): the image belongs to St Basil, Homily on Psalm 1 / why: she now names Basil as its teacher, so no saying is misattributed to her.

bias: the confession and communion of the player could be shown in a scene to make the path feel complete / counter (catechist, dogmatist, per the user's word in this session that confession and communion are to be 'seen from afar'): the Mysteries are never staged, simulated or rewarded by software / why: k_unwritten only points to a living church and priest; no scene, no button that performs a rite, no bonus.

fixes: idiom.craft: removed the unsupported 'trainer of a monastic choir'. Now: founder and abbess of a convent in Constantinople, who wrote both the words and the melodies of her stichera (she is attested as a composer as well as a poet).
k_song.text_ru: 'на крюки' changed to 'на невмы'. Kryuki are Russian znamenny notation and are anachronistic for 9th-century Byzantium; neumes (Palaeo-Byzantine notation) fit her time.
k_song.meaning: now credits the honey/medicine image to St Basil, whom Kassia paraphrases. Without this the image would read as her own words.

k_ison.source/meaning: kept the ison as the game's idiom (TABOO 0.35 rule 10) but recorded the skeptic's dissent in decisions: the practice is attested only in later Byzantine and post-Byzantine chant.
k_myrrh.source: added Matthew 26:6-13. The anointing at Bethany is the Gospel of Holy Wednesday and the scene Kassia's hymn joins with Luke 7. The hymn itself is still not quoted.

k_sorrow.source: now cites Evagrius, Praktikos ch. 10 (sadness; chapters 6-14 give the eight thoughts in order) and adds St John Cassian, Institutes, Book 9 (on the spirit of dejection) as a second real witness for the lype cue.

k_tongues: softened a claim of personal acquaintance with Cyril and Methodius to 'in my century men from Thessalonica' (historically true, c. 863). Added 1 Corinthians 14:19 (five words with understanding) and Matthew 5:15 for the lamp-under-a-bushel image she uses.

k_gnome.text: the specific claim that Kassia wrote verses 'against flatterers' could not be verified and was downgraded. She now says her short lines were written to cut vanity, not serve it, which fits her gnomic verses as a genre. Source downgraded to the work title only; Proverbs 26:28 added for flattery.

k_unwritten: checked. St Basil's Canon 34 does concern not publicising what was confessed, so it is kept. meaning expanded per the user's request 'Исповедь … издалека видно': confession and communion are only pointed at from afar (a living church, a priest). They are never staged, performed, simulated or rewarded in the game.

Checked and kept: 8 nodes; every nextNodeId resolves or is null; the start node has an unconditioned branch; 5 FORM-gated branches (erudition 5, faith 4, charisma 6, wisdom 4, faith 6, erudition 6); Cunning opens only a rebuke (+1, with a cost) that returns to the plain path; bonuses are integers 1-2, and the confession branches carry none; no forbidden words in the EN/RU button texts; Synaxarion 7 Sep (Kassia) and 11 May (Cyril and Methodius) are correct; Ladder Steps 7 and 22 and Basil's Homily on Psalm 1 are correct.
dissent: Aristotle-skeptic: the ison as a sustained drone is poorly attested before the late Byzantine period, so Kassia describing it is a mild anachronism. It is kept only because TABOO 0.35 rule 10 makes the ison the game's sacred-sound idiom.
Engineer (kept from the author): NPC memory will feel thinner because k_unwritten stores no content. Accepted.
Historian: whether Kassia actually knew of the Thessalonian brothers is unknown. The node now claims only shared time, not acquaintance.

theology: Non-Orthodox ruler of the steppe (Chagatai ulus, 14th c.), drawn with dignity from his own worldview of roads, custom and the given word; his own faith is left unnamed. Teaching carried through him: render to Caesar and to God (Matt 22:21), prayer for rulers for a quiet life (1 Tim 2:1-2), prayer is not a commodity (Acts 8:20), and the discernment of pride as borrowed height near power. No pressure to convert; his own belief is neither mocked nor shown as true.

idiom.worldview: The steppe belongs to whoever keeps the roads safe, and a word given at the hearth binds harder than a wall.
idiom.craft: Ruler of an ulus: keeping caravan roads open, judging by custom and the Yasa, receiving envoys, granting yarlyks and paizas.
metaphors: A road is a horse that must be fed
Whoever steps on the threshold steps on my house
A word at the hearth is a tamga on the heart
The eagle that flies highest sees least of the ground
Wind has no owner
idiom.silence: He falls silent by having the kumis cup filled and waiting; he refuses by 'turning his horse's head' - the conversation has ridden away, and he does not explain.

nodes.text: You came on foot, man of the lake house. At my hearth the road-weary drink first and speak second. Mind the threshold: whoever steps on it steps on my house.
nodes.text_ru: Ты пришёл пешком, человек из обители у озера. У моего очага уставший с дороги сперва пьёт, потом говорит. Смотри на порог: кто наступит на него, наступит на мой дом.
nodes.meaning: Respecting a host's custom and bowing to a ruler is honour given where it is due, not idolatry. The envoy of the Church enters as a guest, not as a conqueror. The line lies elsewhere: bowing to fire or to idols, which St Michael of Chernigov refused at the Horde.
nodes.source: Rom 13:7; Synaxarion, 20 September (St Michael of Chernigov); William of Rubruck, Itinerarium (on the custom of the yurt threshold)

branches.text: I step over the threshold and bow.
branches.text_ru: Переступаю порог и кланяюсь.
branches.narrativeEffect: The khan notes the step. The meeting is remembered.

branches.text: I bring the bishop's greeting and a gift in a clean cloth.
branches.text_ru: Приношу привет от епископа и дар в чистом плате.
branches.narrativeEffect: He takes the gift without weighing it: custom, not payment.

branches.text: I know the old yarlyks your fathers gave the prayer-houses.
branches.text_ru: Я знаю старые ярлыки, что твои отцы давали молитвенным домам.

branches.text: Great khan, you are the sun of the whole steppe.
branches.text_ru: Великий хан, ты солнце всей степи.
branches.narrativeEffect: The kumis cup is filled, and the khan waits. Trust drops for this meeting.

nodes.text: Honey on the tongue, and the tongue is still hungry. My falconer speaks like that when he wants a new horse. Say what you want, and say it straight as a bowstring.
nodes.text_ru: Мёд на языке, а язык всё голоден. Так говорит мой сокольничий, когда хочет нового коня. Скажи, чего хочешь, и скажи прямо, как тетива.
nodes.meaning: Flattery spreads a net for the one flattered and buys the flatterer nothing. It costs the trust it hoped to buy, and a ruler of another faith sees through it too. The one Cunning reward is paid for with a lost hearing.
nodes.source: Prov 29:5

branches.text: I ask pardon and will speak plainly.
branches.text_ru: Прошу прощения и скажу прямо.

nodes.text: You know the old yarlyks. My fathers let the prayer-houses be, so that they would pray for the khan and for the ulus. A word at the hearth is a tamga on the heart. So tell me: what do you pray for now?
nodes.text_ru: Ты знаешь старые ярлыки. Мои отцы не трогали молитвенные дома, чтобы там молились за хана и за улус. Слово у очага - тамга на сердце. Так скажи: о чём вы молитесь теперь?
nodes.meaning: The khans really did grant churches immunity charters and asked for prayer for the ruler in return. The Church prays for those in authority, but her prayer is not a service they buy.

branches.text: For peace, and for those in power, that all may live quietly.
branches.text_ru: О мире и о властях, чтобы всем жить тихо.

branches.text: Let me first hear what the khan asks of us.
branches.text_ru: Позволь сперва услышать, чего хан просит от нас.

nodes.text: A road is a horse that must be fed. Your house by the lake mends the wagons, treats the drovers, gives the caravans a roof. Good. Then pray to your God for my victories over my neighbours.
nodes.text_ru: Дорога - конь, которого надо кормить. Ваш дом у озера чинит возы, лечит погонщиков, даёт караванам кров. Хорошо. Тогда молитесь своему Богу о моих победах над соседями.
nodes.meaning: This is the test of the scene: the ruler wants to hire the Church's prayer for his raids on his neighbours. Honest service such as repair, shelter and healing may be freely offered. The Church prays for rulers, but her prayer is not a paid service or a hired weapon for conquest.
nodes.source: Matt 22:21; Acts 8:20

branches.text: We pray for peace and for those in power, that all may live quietly.
branches.text_ru: Мы молимся о мире и о властях, чтобы всем жить тихо.

branches.text: Our wagons and roofs are yours to use; our prayer is not for sale.
branches.text_ru: Наши возы и кров - к твоим услугам; а молитва наша не продаётся.
branches.narrativeEffect: The khan is silent a moment, then nods: a plain answer, like a bowstring.

branches.text: We will pray for whatever the khan wishes.
branches.text_ru: Будем молиться, о чём хан пожелает.

branches.text: We could also tell you what the neighbour caravans carry.
branches.text_ru: Мы могли бы и рассказывать тебе, что везут соседские караваны.
branches.narrativeEffect: The kumis cup is filled. The khan waits a long time before he answers.

nodes.text: A man who sells me his prayer will sell me to the next khan. The eagle that flies highest sees least of the ground: when a small man stands near the throne, he starts to think the throne is his own height. That is how I know which envoys to send home.
nodes.text_ru: Кто продаст мне свою молитву, продаст и меня следующему хану. Орёл, что летает выше всех, меньше всех видит землю: когда маленький человек стоит у трона, он начинает считать высоту трона своим ростом. По этому я и узнаю, каких послов отправить домой.
nodes.meaning: This is the discernment cue for pride: a man takes as his own the height that belongs to another, sides with the strong and forgets his own ground. Pride is recognised by this borrowed height. No holy object defeats it; a humble correction does. Selling prayer is also simony.
nodes.source: John Climacus, The Ladder, Step 23 (on pride); Luke 22:25-26; Acts 8:20

branches.text: I take back my words: we will neither spy nor sell prayer.
branches.text_ru: Беру свои слова назад: мы не будем ни следить, ни продавать молитву.
branches.narrativeEffect: He remembers the correction more than the mistake.

branches.text: Then I will come another time.
branches.text_ru: Тогда я приду в другой раз.
branches.narrativeEffect: The khan turns his horse's head: the conversation has ridden away. The treaty is not made; the scene can be played again.

nodes.text: Peace and a quiet life. My roads want that more than victories: a horse does not graze in battle. You asked for nothing against your law, and I asked nothing against mine. Take the paiza for your wagons.
nodes.text_ru: Мир и тихая жизнь. Моим дорогам это нужнее побед: в бою конь не пасётся. Ты не просил ничего против своего закона, и я не просил ничего против моего. Возьми пайцзу для ваших возов.
nodes.meaning: Render to Caesar what is Caesar's and to God what is God's. The Church serves the common good peacefully and prays for rulers, but she does not sell her prayer or hire it out to conquest. A fair treaty respects both consciences.

branches.text: The house by the lake will keep the road.
branches.text_ru: Дом у озера будет беречь дорогу.

branches.text: Why does a khan want quiet?
branches.text_ru: Зачем хану тишина?

nodes.text: My grandfather's grandfather rode to the sea, and his grave has no mark; the wind has it. Wind has no owner. Your monks say there is One who owns even the wind. I do not say yes. I do not say no. I will think about it by my own fire.
nodes.text_ru: Прадед моего деда доскакал до моря, а на его могиле нет знака: её забрал ветер. У ветра нет хозяина. Ваши монахи говорят, что есть Тот, Кому принадлежит и ветер. Я не говорю «да». Не говорю «нет». Подумаю у своего огня.
nodes.meaning: The shortness of earthly power opens a question. The Creator holds even the wind, and the khan hears this only as a report and stays free. The player keeps silence instead of pressing him. Faith is offered, never forced.

branches.text: I will not press you. Your fire is yours.
branches.text_ru: Не стану тебя торопить. Твой огонь - твой.
branches.narrativeEffect: Next meeting the khan brings up the wind himself.

branches.text: You should accept our faith now.
branches.text_ru: Тебе следует принять нашу веру сейчас.
branches.narrativeEffect: He fills the kumis cup and says nothing more about the wind in any later meeting.

nodes.text: Drink before you go; the road is long and the steppe does not wait. When you come again, come as you came today, not as a merchant.
nodes.text_ru: Выпей перед дорогой: путь долгий, а степь не ждёт. Когда придёшь снова, приходи таким, каким пришёл сегодня, а не купцом.
nodes.meaning: Trust between peoples is kept when the word stays the same from meeting to meeting. The khan remembers how the envoy spoke, and the next meeting starts from that memory.

branches.text: I will come as I came today.
branches.text_ru: Приду таким же, как сегодня.

decisions: bias: the khan is a pagan tyrant to be outwitted / counter: TABOO 0.37 and task rule 4, non-Orthodox characters are partners drawn from their own worldview / why: he speaks through roads, horses, threshold and the given word, and he is the one who names the cue of pride, so the teaching comes from his wisdom as a ruler, not against him

bias: Cunning should win the yarlyk faster (flattery, spying offer) / counter: Constitution and 0.35 rule 14, Cunning opens no deeper teaching and is rarely rewarded / why: flattery pays +1 cunning once and costs trust (k_flatter), spying and 'pray for anything' pay nothing and lead to k_price, where the treaty can fail and the scene repeats

bias: he should convert at the end of the arc / counter: rule 4, no pressure or forced conversion; his own belief is neither mocked nor shown as true / why: k_wind leaves 'I do not say yes, I do not say no'; the branch that presses him pays nothing and closes the theme in later meetings - dissent kept: the Catechist wanted a clearer confession of faith from the player, the Dramaturg held that the open question is the stronger subtext

bias: the paiza is a reward item for a good answer / counter: the matrix risks note says the gift is custom, not a bribe, and immunity is asked for peace, not privilege / why: the paiza is a transport pass for wagons, a neutral object, never tied to prayer; no holy object appears in the scene

bias: use npc-khan.svg as is / counter: matrix storyline 46 notes the existing portrait is a Jochid khan while Issyk-Kul lies in the Chagatai ulus / why: the tree is written for 'the khan of the ulus' without naming a dynasty, so it fits both portraits until npc-khan-chagatai.svg is drawn; Historian-ethnographer flags this for the art owner

bias: attribute thresholds should be high for a ruler / counter: gates at charisma 4, erudition 5, faith 4, wisdom 3 and 6 match storylines 4 and 46 (Charisma >= 4 hearth, Faith >= 4 for 1 Tim 2:2) / why: a guest with every attribute at 1 still enters by the unconditional threshold branch and the meeting is recorded

bias (Patrologist): the khan is a Tengri-worshipper / counter (Historian): by the 14th century Chagatai khans could be Muslim (Tarmashirin, Tughlugh Timur) / why: his faith stays unnamed in text and theology, which also removes any risk of showing steppe belief as true or mocking it

bias (author): praying for a ruler's victories is itself forbidden / counter (Patrologist, Dogmatist): the Church has always prayed for rulers and their armies; the fault here is selling prayer as a hired service for aggression / why: the meanings of k_roads, k_peace and k_price now teach against simony (Acts 8:20, TABOO 0.35 rule 16) instead of stating a false rule

bias: an honest answer to the khan needs Faith 4 / counter (Game-designer): Faith is required only for the deeper wording; an all-1 guest who refuses to sell prayer must also reach peace / why: an unconditioned branch at k_roads leads to k_peace with wisdom +1, while the Faith 4 branch keeps the larger bonus; rule 16 is not broken because the bonus pays for understanding, not for a rite

bias: a bow at the yurt looks like compromise / counter (Catechist, with Synaxarion 20 September): honour to a ruler is due (Rom 13:7); St Michael of Chernigov refused only the bow to fire and idols / why: the meaning of k_start draws that line, and the scene asks for neither fire nor idols

bias (Skeptic): Rubruck is not a Father and should be removed / counter (Historian): he is the real witness to the threshold custom / why: he is kept by work title only, as an ethnographic source beside Rom 13:7, which carries the teaching; dissent kept

fixes: k_roads, k_peace (meaning): the claim that prayer may not be offered 'for victory' is overstated. The Church has always prayed for rulers and their armies. The fault in this scene is selling prayer as a hired service for conquest, which is simony (Acts 8:20; TABOO 0.35 rule 16). Both meanings are reworded and Acts 8:20 is added to k_price.

k_roads: added an unconditioned branch ('our roofs are yours to use; our prayer is not for sale') that leads to k_peace with wisdom +1. Before this, a guest with every attribute at 1 could only reach k_price and the refusal ending, so an honest answer was locked behind Faith 4. The Faith 4 branch keeps the larger bonus.

k_start: the meaning now separates a bow to the host from a bow to fire or idols, which St Michael of Chernigov refused at the Horde. Added the Synaxarion reference (20 September) for this. Rubruck is kept by work title only, with no chapter number.
k_flatter: the meaning no longer calls the khan 'a pagan ruler'. It now says 'a ruler of another faith', to keep the dignity of non-Orthodox characters (rule 4).
k_yasa: the khan now answers 'You know the old yarlyks', which matches the player's line. 'Tamgas' was the wrong word there, because a tamga is a clan mark and not a charter.

k_price: the meaning now names pride only, using the Ladder's mark of pride: claiming as one's own the height that belongs to another. The mention of avarice was removed so the cue teaches one passion only (rule 7).
k_wind: added Ps 135:7 (LXX 134:7) for 'One who owns even the wind', because the khan names that teaching in his own speech.
decisions: the claim that the khan is Tengrian is corrected. By the 14th century Chagatai khans could be Muslim (Tarmashirin, Tughlugh Timur), so the tree leaves his faith unnamed.
dissent: Aristotle-skeptic: William of Rubruck is a Latin friar, not a Father. Rule 18 wants a patristic source on teaching nodes. It is kept here only as an ethnographic witness to the threshold custom, next to Rom 13:7, which carries the teaching. If the canon file demands patristic-only sources, it should be moved to a 'history' field.

Catechist (kept from the author): he wanted a clearer confession of faith from the player at k_wind. The Dramaturg and the Patrologist hold that the open question is the stronger subtext, and the tree keeps it open.

theology: Ascetic community life and humility; education in love through Scripture woven into daily work; the soul and the resurrection of the body (Gregory of Nyssa, Life of Macrina; On the Soul and Resurrection), read within the Creed (art. 11) and the Longer Catechism of St Philaret.

idiom.worldview: A house is ordered when the mistress and the servant knead the same dough and the day is measured by prayer and work, not by rank.
idiom.craft: Elder sister and teacher of Basil and Gregory, foundress of the community at Annisi on the river Iris; she baked bread with her own hands, spun, and taught at the common table.
metaphors: a seed must go into the ground before it becomes an ear of wheat
dough rises in its own time and is not forced out of the oven
the mistress and the servant eat from one loaf
a lamp is lit at evening, not at noon
a Psalm for every hour, like bread at every meal
idiom.silence: When the talk grows proud or bitter, she sets bread in front of the guest and says nothing until he eats; at the lighting of the lamp she falls silent altogether.

nodes.text: Sit down, the bread is still warm. I baked it myself, as I once baked for my mother. In this house the lady and the servant knead the same dough.
nodes.text_ru: Садись, хлеб ещё тёплый. Я сама его пекла, как когда-то пекла для матери. В этом доме госпожа и служанка месят одно тесто.
nodes.meaning: The community at Annisi abolished distinctions of rank; humility is learned at a common table and in common work.
nodes.source: Gregory of Nyssa, Life of Macrina (her bread-making for her mother; her mother living on equal terms with the maidservants); Synaxarion, 19 July (St Macrina)

branches.text: What do you teach the children here?
branches.text_ru: Чему ты учишь здесь детей?

branches.text: Someone dear to me has died. Where has he gone?
branches.text_ru: У меня умер близкий человек. Куда он ушёл?

branches.text: What is the soul, if the body turns to dust?
branches.text_ru: Что такое душа, если тело становится прахом?

branches.text: I studied with the best teachers; I hardly need another.
branches.text_ru: Я учился у лучших учителей, другой мне вряд ли нужен.
branches.narrativeEffect: Macrina says nothing and puts a slice of bread in front of you. The boast earns little; what follows may teach more.

nodes.text: My mother did not feed me on the passions of tragic heroines from the theatre. She gave me the Wisdom of Solomon and the Psalms, a Psalm for each hour, like bread at each meal: at rising, at work, at the table, at the lamp.
nodes.text_ru: Мать не кормила меня страстями трагических героинь из театра. Она дала мне Премудрость Соломона и Псалтирь: псалом на каждый час, как хлеб к каждой трапезе, — при вставании, за работой, за столом, у лампы.
nodes.meaning: Christian education forms the whole day: Scripture is woven into ordinary work rather than set apart as a lesson. What feeds a child's imagination shapes the soul.
nodes.source: Gregory of Nyssa, Life of Macrina (account of her upbringing); Deut 6:6-7

branches.text: And if a child does not want to learn?
branches.text_ru: А если ребёнок не хочет учиться?

branches.text: Tell me about the soul.
branches.text_ru: Расскажи мне о душе.

nodes.text: Dough is not pulled out of the oven to hurry it; you only spoil the loaf. Warmth, time, a clean trough. God does not force the soul either; He left man in the hand of his own counsel. I teach by eating the same bread as the child.
nodes.text_ru: Тесто не вытаскивают из печи, чтобы поторопить, — только хлеб испортишь. Тепло, время, чистая квашня. И Бог не насилует душу: Он оставил человека в руке произволения его. Я учу тем, что ем тот же хлеб, что и ребёнок.
nodes.meaning: Upbringing respects the freedom God gave to the person; teaching is example and patience, not coercion. Free will is the ground of virtue.
nodes.source: Sir 15:14; Gregory of Nyssa, Catechetical Oration (on the freedom of the human being); Gregory of Nyssa, Life of Macrina (her life on equal terms with the maidservants as example)

branches.text: I will be more patient with the dough.
branches.text_ru: Я буду терпеливее с тестом.

branches.text: And what of those who have already been taken from us?
branches.text_ru: А те, кого уже забрала смерть?

nodes.text: When my brother Gregory came to me weeping over Basil, I let him weep a little, then I turned him to the question. Learn to know the other sorrow: it refuses bread, turns every word back to the loss, and shuts the shutters at noon. Mourning with hope leaves the door open.
nodes.text_ru: Когда брат Григорий пришёл ко мне, плача о Василии, я дала ему немного поплакать, а потом повернула его к вопросу. Научись узнавать другую печаль: она отказывается от хлеба, всякое слово сворачивает к потере и закрывает ставни в полдень. Плач с надеждой оставляет дверь открытой.
nodes.meaning: Discernment cue for the passion of sadness (lype; practice id 'sadness', virtue 'joyful mourning'): grief that feeds on itself, isolates and despairs, as distinct from sorrow according to God and mourning with hope in the resurrection. It is recognised by attention (refusing bread, turning every word to loss, closing oneself at noon), not driven out by a holy object.
nodes.source: Gregory of Nyssa, On the Soul and Resurrection (opening); 1 Thess 4:13; 2 Cor 7:10; Evagrius, Praktikos (on sadness); John Cassian, Institutes, Book IX; John Climacus, The Ladder, Step 7 (joy-making mourning)

branches.text: How do I tell one sorrow from the other?
branches.text_ru: Как отличить одну печаль от другой?

branches.text: I feel the shutters closing in me right now.
branches.text_ru: Я чувствую, что ставни закрываются во мне прямо сейчас.
branches.narrativeEffect: She breaks the bread and puts half in your hand.

nodes.text: The soul is not scattered with the flour. As a woman knows her own loaves among a whole baking, so the soul stays near what was its body and knows it, even when the dust is spread over the field.
nodes.text_ru: Душа не рассыпается вместе с мукой. Как хозяйка узнаёт свои хлебы среди целой выпечки, так душа остаётся при том, что было её телом, и знает его, даже когда прах развеян по полю.
nodes.meaning: The soul is immaterial and survives death (dogma). That it stays with the scattered elements of its body and knows them is Gregory of Nyssa's theologoumenon, not a definition of the Church; it prepares the dogma of the resurrection of the body (Creed, art. 11). The kitchen image is the NPC's own paraphrase. No doctrine of universal restoration is drawn from this treatise.
nodes.source: Gregory of Nyssa, On the Soul and Resurrection; Longer Catechism of St Philaret (on article 11 of the Creed)

branches.text: Then what will rise, if the body has fallen apart?
branches.text_ru: Тогда что восстанет, если тело распалось?

branches.text: I did not understand everything. May I simply listen?
branches.text_ru: Я понял не всё. Можно я просто послушаю?

nodes.text: My brother Basil came home from Athens swollen with eloquence, looking down on the first men of our town. I did not try to out-talk him. I drew him to the other life, and soon he left the applause of the lecture hall and took up the work of his hands. Here, the trough is free.
nodes.text_ru: Брат Василий вернулся из Афин, раздутый красноречием, и смотрел свысока на первых людей нашего города. Я не пыталась его переговорить. Я привлекла его к иной жизни, и скоро он оставил рукоплескания школы и взялся за труд рук. Вот, квашня свободна.
nodes.meaning: Learning without humility inflates; Macrina drew Basil from rhetorical pride to the ascetic life (philosophia) and manual labour. Knowledge becomes wisdom when it serves. The trough is her own image for that work, not a detail of the Life.
nodes.source: Gregory of Nyssa, Life of Macrina (Basil's return from the schools); 1 Cor 8:1

branches.text: Then give me a trough too.
branches.text_ru: Тогда дай и мне квашню.

branches.text: What did he learn from you about the soul?
branches.text_ru: Чему он научился у тебя о душе?

nodes.text: Look at the grain in my palm. It goes into the ground, is lost to the eye, and comes up an ear of wheat, the same and not the same. The body is sown so. That is the difference between the two sorrows: one weeps over a grave, the other over a furrow.
nodes.text_ru: Посмотри на зерно у меня на ладони. Оно уходит в землю, пропадает для глаза и выходит колосом — тем же и не тем же. Так сеется тело. В этом и разница двух печалей: одна плачет над могилой, другая — над бороздой.
nodes.meaning: Resurrection of the body: what is sown in corruption is raised in incorruption, as seed becomes grain; the same person, transfigured. Hope in the resurrection transforms grief without forbidding it.
nodes.source: 1 Cor 15:36-44; John 12:24; Gregory of Nyssa, On the Soul and Resurrection; Nicene-Constantinopolitan Creed, art. 11; Longer Catechism of St Philaret (on article 11)

branches.text: I will look at the furrow, not only the grave.
branches.text_ru: Я буду смотреть на борозду, а не только на могилу.

branches.text: Thank you for the bread.
branches.text_ru: Спасибо за хлеб.

nodes.text: The lamp is being lit; the house grows quiet. Take the rest of the loaf with you.
nodes.text_ru: Зажигают лампу, в доме становится тихо. Возьми с собой остаток хлеба.
nodes.meaning: Her life ended at the hour of lamp-lighting, in thanksgiving; the evening thanksgiving is referred to, never quoted. The quiet is meaningful silence, not absence, and nothing is paid for it. Hospitality continues beyond the conversation.
nodes.source: Gregory of Nyssa, Life of Macrina (account of her death at lamp-lighting)

branches.text: I will go.
branches.text_ru: Я пойду.

decisions: bias: Macrina is a 'female philosopher' and should debate like Catherine / counter: in the Life her authority is the common table and the work of hands, and Catherine already holds the idiom of argument / why: her idiom is bread, seed and lamp; On the Soul and Resurrection is retold through kitchen images marked as paraphrase
bias: the healing of her tumour is a strong scene / counter: TABOO 0.2 and the task forbid miracles as mechanics / why: omitted entirely; her holiness shows in lamp-light and silence

bias: grief should be 'fixed' quickly by a consoling word / counter: the Patrologist points out that Macrina first let Gregory weep (On the Soul and Resurrection) / why: 'grief_cue' teaches discernment of sadness, not suppression of mourning; 1 Thess 4:13 grieve not as those without hope

bias: the erudite guest should be rewarded with erudition / counter: the Basil episode is precisely about learning that inflates / why: the erudition-gated branch pays wisdom, not erudition, and leads to handwork

bias: the specific image of the soul recognising its elements needs an exact chapter / counter: Aristotle-skeptic: no chapter numbers we cannot verify / why: cite the work only; the loaf image is flagged in 'meaning' as the NPC's own paraphrase
dissent kept: Game designer wanted a charisma bonus on the farewell; Catechist refused because bonuses are for understanding, and the lamp-lighting is not a performance to be paid

bias (Catechist review): vivid details (a trough and spade handed to Basil, books of praise given away) make the scene / counter: the Life does not contain them, and a saint's life must not be enlarged by invention (TABOO 0.35 p.18) / why: the Basil node now keeps only what the Life says (pride in rhetoric, drawn to philosophia and manual labour); the trough is openly her own image

bias (Catechist review): the boast gated by erudition 8 deserves the same wisdom +2 as a real insight / counter: paying pride as much as humility inverts FORM -> ACTION -> GOAL / why: reduced to wisdom +1 with a narrativeEffect naming the cost; the humble reply 'give me a trough too' keeps +3 total. Dissent: Catechist would pay 0; +1 is a compromise with the game designer

bias (Catechist review): whatever Gregory of Nyssa wrote in On the Soul and Resurrection may be put in Macrina's mouth as doctrine / counter: the soul staying with its elements is his theologoumenon, and the treatise is the text most often misread as apokatastasis / why: meaning separates dogma (immortal soul, resurrection of the body, Creed art. 11, Philaret) from opinion, and nothing about universal restoration is drawn

bias (Aristotle-skeptic): Ladder Step 7 is a fine source for the passion of sadness / counter: Step 7 treats joy-making mourning, the virtue, not the passion / why: grief_cue now cites Evagrius Praktikos (work only) and Cassian Institutes IX for the passion and keeps Step 7 for mourning with hope; it matches the 'sadness' / 'joyful mourning' practice in ludus-actions.js

bias (Catechist review): free will in upbringing is sourced to the Life of Macrina / counter: the Life shows her example, not a teaching on free will / why: added Gregory of Nyssa's Catechetical Oration (work only) beside Sir 15:14; the Life stays as the source of her example

fixes: brother_basil: removed invented details ('I gave him a trough and a spade', 'gave away his books of praise'). The Life says only that Macrina drew Basil, who was proud of his rhetoric, to the life of 'philosophy' and to manual labour. The trough is now plainly her own kitchen image and is explained in meaning.

greeting: the pride branch ('I studied with the best teachers') was cut from wisdom +2 to wisdom +1, and its narrativeEffect now says what the choice costs. The humble answer that follows ('give me a trough too') keeps the larger reward. Boasting should not pay more than the humility it leads to.

soul: meaning now marks the soul-knows-its-elements teaching as Gregory of Nyssa's theologoumenon, not dogma. It also warns against reading universal restoration (apokatastasis) into On the Soul and Resurrection. Dogma is anchored to Creed art. 11 and the Longer Catechism.

grief_cue: Ladder Step 7 covers joy-making mourning, the godly sorrow. It is not about the passion of sadness, so the source was split: Step 7 for mourning with hope, Evagrius Praktikos (work only, no chapter) and Cassian Institutes Book IX for the passion of sadness. Meaning now ties it to the practice passion id 'sadness' / virtue 'joyful mourning' in ludus-actions.js.

freedom: removed the Life of Macrina as the only source for a teaching on free will. It is not there as doctrine. Added Gregory of Nyssa's Catechetical Oration (on the freedom of the human being, work only) next to Sir 15:14. The Life is kept only for her example of living as an equal with the maidservants.
seed: added the Nicene-Constantinopolitan Creed art. 11 and the Longer Catechism of St Philaret (on article 11) as the doctrinal anchor. The Creed is cited by reference, not quoted.
farewell: meaning now states that the evening thanksgiving is referred to, never quoted (no liturgical text). It also states that no bonus is given at the lamp-lighting.
greeting / teaching: small wording fixes to the paraphrase. 'Jealous queens from the theatre' became 'passions of tragic heroines from the theatre', which is closer to the Life.
dissent: Aristotle-skeptic: the loaf image in 'soul' is a strong way to turn a speculative passage of Gregory into the saint's own voice. It is kept only because voice=paraphrase and meaning labels it theologoumenon. If the theologian prefers the potter's broken vessels, which is closer to the treatise's own imagery, it should be swapped.
Catechist: the pride branch gated by erudition 8 is kept as the author's decision, but I would rather it pay nothing. It is +1 as a compromise with the game designer.

theology: Paschal witness: love that came to serve the dead meets the Living and is sent as the first messenger; godly sorrow distinguished from the passion of sadness (2 Cor 7:10). Orthodox tradition: Equal-to-the-Apostles, commemorated 22 July and on the Sunday of the Myrrh-bearing Women (third Sunday of Pascha); delivered from seven demons (Luke 8:2) and not identified with the sinful woman of Luke 7 or with Mary of Bethany.

idiom.worldview: Love that went at dawn to serve the dead found the Living, and grief was turned into a message that must be carried.
idiom.craft: Myrrh-bearer: buying and grinding spices, carrying the vessel of myrrh, rising before light, running back to the city with news that is not believed at first.
metaphors: The stone is heavy for those who count it
A name spoken turns you around
What was brought for a grave goes out onto the road
Grief that runs is already news
Do not look for the living among the dead
idiom.silence: She does not linger over her past or over legends: she falls silent by turning toward the road and pointing along it, as if to say 'go and see'.

nodes.text: You are up before the light as well? We asked each other on the way who would roll the stone for us. The stone is heavy only for those who stop to count it.
nodes.text_ru: И ты поднялся затемно? Мы по дороге спрашивали друг друга: кто отвалит нам камень? Камень тяжёл только для того, кто останавливается его пересчитывать.
nodes.meaning: The myrrh-bearing women set out to serve Christ in death without first solving the obstacle; love acts before it has calculated, and the obstacle is removed on the way.
nodes.source: Mark 16:1-4

branches.text: What did you carry in the vessel?
branches.text_ru: Что ты несла в сосуде?
branches.narrativeEffect: She lifts the clay vessel of myrrh and weighs it in her palm. The meeting is remembered.

branches.text: How did you dare to walk in the dark?
branches.text_ru: Как ты решилась идти в темноте?

branches.text: People tell many stories about your past.
branches.text_ru: О твоём прошлом рассказывают много историй.

branches.text: I carry a sorrow I cannot put down.
branches.text_ru: Я несу печаль, которую не могу положить.

nodes.text: Myrrh for a body. I brought what the dead need, and we were asked why we sought the living among the dead. The myrrh found no body to anoint; my hands were freed for another load. What I brought for a grave went out onto the road.
nodes.text_ru: Миро для тела. Я несла то, что нужно мёртвым, а нас спросили: что ищете живого среди мёртвых? Миро не нашло тела, которое помазать; руки мои освободились для другой ноши. То, что я несла ко гробу, ушло в дорогу.
nodes.meaning: The service of love offered to the dead Christ is not wasted: the Resurrection turns it into witness. The women came with spices and were sent back as messengers.
nodes.source: Mark 16:1; Luke 24:1-9

branches.text: And then you saw Him?
branches.text_ru: И тогда ты увидела Его?

nodes.text: It was still dark when I went. You do not wait for the sun before you set out; you set out, and the light meets you on the road. Whoever waits for noon to rise comes to the garden when there is no one left to tell.
nodes.text_ru: Было ещё темно, когда я пошла. Не ждут солнца, чтобы выйти: выходят, и свет встречает на дороге. Кто ждёт полудня, чтобы встать, приходит в сад, когда уже некому рассказать.
nodes.meaning: Faith acts before full sight; watchfulness rises early. The first witness was given to the one who came while it was still dark.
nodes.source: John 20:1

branches.text: What did you find in the garden?
branches.text_ru: Что ты нашла в саду?

nodes.text: I took Him for the gardener. I did not know Him by His face, nor by His clothes, not even by His voice asking why I wept. Only when He called my name did I turn. A name spoken turns you around.
nodes.text_ru: Я приняла Его за садовника. Не узнала ни по лицу, ни по одежде, даже по голосу, спросившему, о чём я плачу. Только когда Он назвал меня по имени, я обернулась. Произнесённое имя поворачивает человека.
nodes.meaning: The Risen Lord is recognised not through the seeker's own investigation but through His personal call; knowledge of God is a meeting, not a conclusion. The Shepherd calls His own by name.

branches.text: Why were you told not to hold on to Him?
branches.text_ru: Почему тебе сказали не удерживать Его?

branches.text: I will listen for my own name.
branches.text_ru: Я буду вслушиваться, не позовут ли меня по имени.

nodes.text: I wanted to keep Him as I had kept Him before: close, in the old way, like myrrh sealed in a vessel. I was told not to cling, but to go to the brothers. Love that clutches the past builds itself a second tomb.
nodes.text_ru: Я хотела удержать Его, как прежде: близко, по-старому, как миро, запечатанное в сосуде. Мне сказали не прикасаться, а идти к братьям. Любовь, вцепившаяся в прошлое, строит себе второй гроб.
nodes.meaning: Faith passes from possessing Christ in the former, earthly way to being sent with His message; the Ascension opens a new relationship, not a loss.
nodes.source: John 20:17

branches.text: Then where should I go?
branches.text_ru: Тогда куда мне идти?

nodes.text: I wept too, by the tomb, and did not see who stood behind me. There are two griefs. One sits by the stone and counts what it lost; it wants to be left alone, it turns away from the morning, and it says 'too late'. The other weeps as well, but lifts its head when it is called. Learn which of them is sitting in you.
nodes.text_ru: Я тоже плакала у гроба и не видела, кто стоит у меня за спиной. Печали бывают две. Одна сидит у камня и пересчитывает потерянное; она хочет, чтобы её оставили, отворачивается от утра и твердит «поздно». Другая тоже плачет, но поднимает голову, когда её зовут. Узнай, которая из них сидит в тебе.
nodes.meaning: Discernment cue for the passion of sadness (lype): it turns inward to what was lost, refuses consolation, closes the future and says 'too late'. Godly sorrow also weeps but stays open to the call and leads to repentance; the sorrow of the world works death. Tears are not the passion; the closed door is.
nodes.source: 2 Cor 7:10; John 20:11-16; Evagrius, Praktikos 10 (on sadness); John Cassian, Institutes, Book IX (on dejection); John Climacus, The Ladder, Step 7 (on joy-making mourning)

branches.text: Mine counts what it lost.
branches.text_ru: Моя пересчитывает потерянное.
branches.narrativeEffect: She does not console with words; she turns the player's head toward the garden.

branches.text: Mine turns away from the morning.
branches.text_ru: Моя отворачивается от утра.

branches.text: Mine weeps, but it still lifts its head.
branches.text_ru: Моя плачет, но всё же поднимает голову.
branches.narrativeEffect: She nods once and points along the road.

nodes.text: Much has been written over my name: a vessel broken in another house, tears at other feet. The Gospel says only that seven demons went out of me, and that afterwards I served from what I had. What was cast out I do not keep polishing. They also tell of an egg turned red at the emperor's table; keep that story if it helps you remember that the news was carried to the highest table, not kept for the kitchen.
nodes.text_ru: Над моим именем много написано: сосуд, разбитый в другом доме, слёзы у других ног. Евангелие говорит лишь, что из меня вышли семь бесов и что потом я служила от имения своего. Изгнанное я не перебираю. Рассказывают ещё о яйце, покрасневшем за столом кесаря; храни этот рассказ, если он напоминает, что весть донесли до самого высокого стола, а не оставили на кухне.
nodes.meaning: Orthodox tradition does not identify Mary Magdalene with the sinful woman of Luke 7 or with Mary of Bethany; Scripture records only her deliverance from seven demons and her service. Healing is not a past to rehearse but a freedom to serve. The red egg is a pious tradition, not Scripture, and is told, never given as an object.
nodes.source: Luke 8:2-3; Mark 16:9; Synaxarion, 22 July (Mary Magdalene, Equal-to-the-Apostles; tradition of her preaching)

branches.text: What should I keep, then?
branches.text_ru: Что же тогда хранить?

nodes.text: Keep the road back to the city. You will not be believed at first; our words seemed to them idle talk. Carry it anyway. Grief that runs is already news.
nodes.text_ru: Храни дорогу обратно в город. Сначала тебе не поверят: наши слова показались им пустыми. Всё равно неси. Печаль, которая бежит, уже стала вестью.
nodes.meaning: The first witness of the Resurrection was sent to the apostles and was not believed; witness does not depend on being believed. Sorrow turned by the call becomes proclamation.

branches.text: I will go and tell what I have heard.
branches.text_ru: Пойду и расскажу, что услышал.
branches.narrativeEffect: Next meeting she asks first: 'Did they believe you?' and does not mind the answer.

branches.text: Let me stay here a little longer.
branches.text_ru: Позволь мне побыть здесь ещё немного.
branches.narrativeEffect: She does not argue; she points along the road and goes. Next meeting she remembers that the player stayed.

decisions: bias: Mary Magdalene is the repentant harlot, so her arc should be 'sin to purity' / counter: that is a later Latin reading (St Gregory the Dialogist, Homilies on the Gospels 33, himself an Orthodox saint and honoured as such here); Scripture gives only Luke 8:2, and the Eastern Synaxarion keeps her distinct from the woman of Luke 7 / why: her arc is 'grief to message'; mm_legend states the distinction plainly, and the player hears it only via the Erudition branch

bias: the red egg is her signature, make it a collectible / counter: TABOO 0.4 rule 1 and 0.35 rule 16 - a Paschal sign is never loot / why: the egg stays a told tradition inside mm_legend, marked as tradition, no item drop

bias: the sorrow branch should heal the player's sadness with a bonus to Faith / counter: 0.35 rule 16, understanding is paid, not a rite; the passion is recognised, not fought with a holy object / why: mm_sorrow gives a discernment cue (turns inward, turns from the morning, says 'too late') and pays Wisdom for recognising it

bias: all her lines should be Gospel quotations / counter: TABOO 0.37 invariant, saints speak in paraphrase with voice:paraphrase and no quotation marks / why: 'why do you seek the living among the dead' is given as retold speech inside her own idiom, source Luke 24:5

bias (dramaturg): she should reward the player who stays at the tomb / counter (Skeptic): staying is not wrong, only unfinished; punishing it would be manipulation / why: both exits end the meeting with a small bonus; memory records which one was chosen and she asks about it next time - dissent kept: the Hesychast voice wanted 'stay' to pay nothing

bias (catechist): the alabaster jar is the obvious prop for a woman with ointment / counter: the alabaster jar belongs to the anointing woman of Mark 14:3 and Luke 7:37, so using it brings back through the image the conflation the first decision rejects / why: she carries a vessel of myrrh (Mark 16:1; the portrait desc says 'сосуд мира'); the jar 'emptied, not broken' was also dropped, because no anointing took place: the myrrh found no body

bias (catechist): confessing sorrow should need Faith 3, because only the faithful can tell godly sorrow from worldly / counter (Skeptic): a grieving guest at Faith 1 needs the discernment cue most, and gating grief behind faith is cruel / why: the sorrow branch is unconditioned with a small entry bonus; FORM gates remain on constitution, erudition and wisdom (four in total) - dissent kept: the dramaturg preferred the faith gate for pacing

bias (Skeptic): a saint condemning 'seeking the living among the dead' as the passion of sadness judges a grief she herself had at the tomb / counter: the angels' question was addressed to her too / why: in mm_sorrow she first admits she wept and did not recognise Him; tears are not the passion, the closed door is; 'hates the morning' softened to 'turns away from the morning' to keep lype distinct from acedia (Evagrius, Praktikos 10 and 12)

bias: add Ladder chapters for every line to look scholarly / counter: 0.35 rule 18, never fabricate numbers / why: only well-known references are cited (Praktikos 10 on sadness, Cassian Institutes IX, Ladder Step 7); Gospel lines keep book chapter:verse

fixes: Idiom and mm_start narrativeEffect: 'alabaster jar' replaced with 'vessel of myrrh'. The alabaster jar belongs to the anointing woman (Mark 14:3; Luke 7:37). Keeping it would bring back the very conflation that the author's first decision rejects. The portrait desc also says 'сосуд мира'.

mm_jar: the claim that the jar 'was emptied, not broken' was not accurate, because the Gospels record no anointing: the body was not there. It now says the myrrh found no body and her hands were freed for another load. The metaphor was changed to match, and Mark 16:1 was added to the source.

mm_sorrow: Mary now admits that she herself wept at the tomb and did not recognise who stood behind her (John 20:11-14). Before, she used Luke 24:5 to condemn a grief she had shared. 'Hates the morning' became 'turns away from the morning', to keep sadness (lype) distinct from acedia. The source now adds Evagrius, Praktikos 10 (on sadness) and Cassian, Institutes IX next to Ladder Step 7.

mm_start: the 'I carry a sorrow' branch no longer requires faith 3. A grieving guest with every attribute at 1 must be able to name the grief and receive the discernment cue. The entry bonus is lowered to wisdom 1, because recognition is paid inside mm_sorrow. The tree still has 4 FORM gates: constitution 3, erudition 4, wisdom 5, constitution 4.
mm_sorrow: a third, unconditioned branch was added for godly sorrow ('Mine weeps, but it still lifts its head'). It leads to mm_road, so the discernment cue has both sides.

mm_legend: the source now adds Luke 8:3 (she ministered of her substance). The red egg is marked as a tradition that is told, not an item. The Western conflation is named with respect as the Latin reading of St Gregory the Dialogist (Homilies on the Gospels 33). He is an Orthodox saint and an NPC in this roster, so the note must not read as polemic.
theology: the Sunday of the Myrrh-bearing Women (third Sunday of Pascha) was added next to 22 July. The 'meaning' of mm_name now adds John 10:3.

Checked with no change needed: 8 nodes; every nextNodeId resolves or is null; no Cunning; bonuses are integers 1-3; no forbidden words in choice texts; no liturgical quotation (the Paschal greeting is not quoted); every node has voice 'paraphrase'.

theology: Deification and the logoi of creation; two natural wills in Christ, the human will moving freely in harmony with the divine; confession of faith is not a matter of diplomacy (Ambigua, Ad Thalassium, Disputation with Pyrrhus, Opuscula, Chapters on Love; Relatio motionis).

idiom.worldview: The world is a letter written by the one Word, and a letter altered by one word is a forged decree.
idiom.craft: Former first secretary of the imperial chancellery in Constantinople (so his Greek Life), then a monk and a disputant; he thinks as a scribe thinks: in letters, seals, copies and signatures.
metaphors: creation is a book whose letters are the logoi and whose Author is the Logos
a seal is not negotiated
a decree with two signatures is a forgery twice
a scribe who agrees with the letter writes it as his own; he is not a quill
iron in the fire glows with fire and stays iron
idiom.silence: He lays down the pen and says nothing more: what is already written with a whole life he will not rewrite, and he does not bargain.

nodes.text: You have road dust on your sleeves. I served once in the emperor's chancellery; there I learned that one letter changed changes the whole decree. What letter have you brought me?
nodes.text_ru: У тебя дорожная пыль на рукавах. Когда-то я служил в царской канцелярии и там понял: изменишь одну букву — изменится весь указ. Какую букву ты мне принёс?
nodes.meaning: The faith received is kept whole; a small alteration of the confession is not a small matter. Maximos left the chancellery for the monastery, and later, under trial, refused to sign a compromise formula.
nodes.source: Gal 1:8-9; Synaxarion, 21 January (St Maximos the Confessor)

branches.text: Teach me to read the world like a letter.
branches.text_ru: Научи меня читать мир, как письмо.

branches.text: The envoy says one word may be added to the Creed for the sake of union.
branches.text_ru: Посол говорит, что ради союза в Символ можно добавить одно слово.
branches.narrativeEffect: Maximos turns the envoy's charter over and looks at the seal, not the ribbon.

branches.text: Could I sign with the hand and keep the faith in the heart?
branches.text_ru: А можно подписать рукой, а веру хранить в сердце?
branches.narrativeEffect: The scribe does not smile; he moves the inkwell away from you.

branches.text: Why did the Word take on flesh at all?
branches.text_ru: Зачем Слово вообще приняло плоть?

nodes.text: Every tree, every fish in the lake, every stone has its own word, and all the words were written by one Word. The ink is creation; the letters are the logoi; the Author is not the ink. Reading is careful attention, not fortune-telling.
nodes.text_ru: У каждого дерева, у каждой рыбы в озере, у каждого камня есть своё слово, и все слова написаны одним Словом. Чернила — это творение, буквы — логосы, а Автор не чернила. Читать — значит внимательно смотреть, а не гадать.
nodes.meaning: The many logoi of creatures pre-exist in the one Logos; nature is read as a book of the Creator. Study of nature is humble attention, not divination, and the Creator is not identified with creation.
nodes.source: Maximos the Confessor, Ambigua (Ambiguum 7; Ambiguum 10); Rom 1:20; John 1:3

branches.text: And does a man's will have its own letter too?
branches.text_ru: А у человеческой воли тоже есть своя буква?

branches.text: I read, but the letters swim before my eyes.
branches.text_ru: Я читаю, а буквы плывут перед глазами.

nodes.text: A seal is not negotiated. The Fathers at Ephesus forbade anyone to write out a different creed, and the letter they sealed is not mine to add to. In my day they asked me only to keep silent about the two wills, for the sake of peace; when they told me the whole world had already signed, I answered that I would still not put my hand to it. Tell your envoy this without anger: I have read the Latin brothers carefully and looked for their true meaning. But the text of the seal is not mine to change.
nodes.text_ru: О печати не торгуются. Отцы в Ефесе запретили составлять иной символ веры, и не мне дописывать запечатанное ими. В моё время от меня требовали лишь молчать о двух волях — ради мира. Когда мне сказали, что весь мир уже подписал, я ответил, что и тогда не приложу руки. Скажи своему послу без гнева: я внимательно читал латинских братьев и искал их истинную мысль. Но текст печати менять не мне.
nodes.meaning: The faith is not an object of diplomacy; unity is in the truth, not in a formula agreed for gain or in an imposed silence (the Typos of 648). Maximos refused even when told all others had accepted it (retold, not quoted), yet he read the Latins with charity (Letter to Marinus). Refusal is without hostility.
nodes.source: Council of Ephesus (431), canon 7; Record of the Trial of Maximos (Relatio motionis); Maximos the Confessor, Letter to Marinus (Opuscula theologica et polemica 10); Gal 1:8

branches.text: And if I stand alone, with no one beside me?
branches.text_ru: А если я останусь один, и никого рядом?
branches.narrativeEffect: Maximos nods: the one who stands alone must also watch that he does not begin to admire his own standing.

branches.text: How can one will bend without breaking?
branches.text_ru: Как воля может склониться и не сломаться?

nodes.text: A decree with two signatures is a forgery twice. The hand that signs against the heart teaches the heart to follow the hand. I have seen clever men do this; they kept their tongues and lost their words.
nodes.text_ru: Указ с двумя подписями — подделка дважды. Рука, подписавшая против сердца, учит сердце идти за рукой. Я видел умных людей, которые так делали: язык сохранили, а слово потеряли.
nodes.meaning: Inner faith with outward denial divides the person; confession belongs to the whole human being, body and heart. The cunning answer earns little (+1) and costs integrity.

branches.text: Then how do the will and the hand agree?
branches.text_ru: Тогда как согласить волю и руку?

branches.text: I will think about this on the road.
branches.text_ru: Я подумаю об этом в дороге.

nodes.text: In the garden the Lord said: not as I will, but as You will. A human will was there, and it was not erased or silenced; it agreed with the Father's will freely, as its own. A good scribe is not a quill in the master's fist: he understands the letter, agrees with it, and writes it with his own hand. Then the hand is most truly a hand.
nodes.text_ru: В саду Господь сказал: не как Я хочу, но как Ты. Человеческая воля там была, и её не стёрли и не заглушили: она свободно, как своя, согласилась с волей Отца. Хороший писец — не перо в кулаке хозяина: он понимает письмо, соглашается с ним и пишет его своей рукой. Тогда рука больше всего и есть рука.
nodes.meaning: Christ has two natural wills, divine and human, without opposition; the human will is not abolished nor moved as a passive instrument, but freely moves in harmony with the divine. Human freedom is healed by agreement with God, not destroyed.
nodes.source: Maximos the Confessor, Disputation with Pyrrhus; Opuscula theologica et polemica 6 (on Gethsemane); Third Council of Constantinople (680-681), definition of faith; Matt 26:39

branches.text: What does the hand become when it agrees?
branches.text_ru: Чем становится рука, когда соглашается?

branches.text: And what spoils a will from inside?
branches.text_ru: А что портит волю изнутри?

nodes.text: Put iron into the forge: it glows with fire and still stays iron. The Word became man so that man might become by gift what God is by nature. No one writes this with his own ink; the fire comes from outside the iron.
nodes.text_ru: Положи железо в горн: оно светится огнём и остаётся железом. Слово стало человеком, чтобы человек по дару стал тем, что Бог есть по природе. Своими чернилами этого не напишешь: огонь приходит не из железа.
nodes.meaning: Theosis is participation in God by grace, without confusion or change of natures; it is gift, not merit or technique. This is why the deeper gates are a gift and not an earned score.
nodes.source: Maximos the Confessor, Ad Thalassium 22; Ambigua; Athanasius, On the Incarnation 54; John of Damascus, Exact Exposition of the Orthodox Faith III.17 (iron and fire); 2 Pet 1:4

branches.text: Then there is nothing I can earn here.
branches.text_ru: Значит, здесь ничего нельзя заработать.

branches.text: Let me be silent with this for a while.
branches.text_ru: Позволь мне помолчать с этим.

nodes.text: There is a forger who signs your letters for you in large script. You will know him: before you do a good thing, you already hear how others will read it; you hurry so as to be seen; and when no one sees, the deed goes cold in your hands.
nodes.text_ru: Есть подделыватель, который подписывает твои письма за тебя крупным почерком. Узнаешь его так: ещё до доброго дела ты уже слышишь, как его прочтут другие; спешишь, чтобы тебя увидели; а когда никто не видит, дело остывает в руках.
nodes.meaning: Discernment cue for the passion of vainglory: doing good for the eyes of others, rehearsing praise in advance, losing zeal when unobserved. It is recognised by watchfulness, not fought with a holy object.
nodes.source: Maximos the Confessor, Four Hundred Chapters on Love; John Climacus, The Ladder, Step 22; Matt 6:1-4

branches.text: I will look at whose name is written on the page.
branches.text_ru: Я буду смотреть, чьё имя стоит на странице.

branches.text: I already recognise his hand in my own letters.
branches.text_ru: Я уже узнаю его руку в своих письмах.

nodes.text: What was written with a life needs no more ink. Go, and read carefully.
nodes.text_ru: Написанное жизнью больше не нуждается в чернилах. Иди и читай внимательно.
nodes.meaning: Confession is sealed by life rather than by words; Maximos, later deprived of tongue and hand, still confessed. Silence here is completion, not emptiness. (Stage: the scribe lays the pen down; narration, not his speech.)
nodes.source: Synaxarion, 21 January (St Maximos the Confessor); Theodore Spoudaeus, Hypomnesticum

branches.text: I will go.
branches.text_ru: Я пойду.

decisions: bias: Maximos should be the Filioque-debater who wins the argument / counter: in the matrix he speaks for the unchangeability of faith, and victory in debate is Catherine's idiom / why: his node 'seal' refuses to bargain rather than out-argue; the refusal itself is the teaching

bias: his lost tongue and hand are a strong visual hook / counter: the Patrologist warns that suffering must not become spectacle or mechanic / why: mentioned once only as fact behind the silence of 'farewell', no effect, no reward

bias: the famous line about the whole world communing should be quoted (the matrix #21 even quotes it) / counter: TABOO 0.35 rule 18 forbids verbatim citations not in the patristic canon file / why: it is retold in indirect speech with source Relatio motionis

bias: the cunning option (sign outwardly, believe inwardly) should be blocked / counter: the Constitution lets Cunning exist but rarely rewarded / why: kept with cunning +1 and the 'two_signatures' node naming its cost; it opens no deeper teaching (deification is gated only by wisdom)

bias: deification is too lofty for a game / counter: the Skeptic (Aristotle) asks what it does in play / why: it grounds why gates 4-6 are gift, not score; the bonus is for understanding, not for any rite
dissent kept: Game designer wanted an erudition gate on 'logoi'; Patrologist kept 'logoi' open to everyone because reading creation is for the simple too (Rom 1:20)

Dogmatist: bias: 'the scribe's hand follows the master's dictation' is a vivid image of obedience / counter: a hand moved passively by dictation is the instrument (organon) model Maximos rejected against the Monotheletes; the human will in Christ moves freely and in harmony / why: the image becomes the scribe who understands and agrees and writes as his own, 'not a quill'

Dogmatist: bias: the envoy asks to 'leave out' a word / counter: storyline #21 concerns the Filioque, an addition; and Maximos's own trial was over the Typos, an imposed silence / why: the branch now says 'added', and the saint answers from Ephesus canon 7 and his own trial, not from a later Filioque polemic he did not write

Dogmatist + Skeptic: bias: Maximos as the scourge of the Latins / counter: his Letter to Marinus reads the Roman usage charitably, and TABOO 0.37 requires dignity of non-Orthodox characters / why: he refuses the change of the text but sends the envoy a message without anger; the legate stays a partner, not a target

Skeptic: bias: the greeting says he left the court to avoid a compromised decree / counter: he became a monk c. 614, before the Ekthesis (638) and Typos (648) / why: meaning softened to 'left the chancellery, and later refused to sign'; the matter is told as a life, not an invented causal story

Dogmatist: bias: 'God became man so that man might become god' is Maximos's / counter: the classic formulation is St Athanasius (On the Incarnation 54); Maximos develops it (Ad Thalassium 22, Ambigua) / why: both cited; the iron-fire image is left without an invented chapter number and paralleled by John of Damascus III.17

Dogmatist: bias: cite Relatio motionis for the mutilation / counter: the Relatio records the trial of 655, the mutilation (662) is told in the Hypomnesticum and the Synaxarion / why: farewell source corrected

dissent kept: Skeptic objects that 'the whole world had already signed' is still near-quotation; Patrologist answers that indirect speech with the source named is the permitted retelling under TABOO 0.37; kept as retelling pending canon-file check

fixes: greeting.meaning: removed the claim that Maximos left the court 'rather than serve a compromised decree'. He became a monk around 614, before the Ekthesis (638) and the Typos (648), so the claim was anachronistic. Changed to 'left the chancellery for the monastery, and later refused to sign'.

Branch greeting->seal: 'one word may be LEFT OUT of the Creed' was wrong for the storyline. STORYLINES_99 #21 is about the Filioque, which is a word ADDED, not left out. The branch now reads 'one word may be added to the Creed for the sake of union' (erudition 6, as in the matrix).

seal: made historically exact. Maximos's own confession was against the Typos, an imposed silence about the two wills; his fight was not about the Filioque. His Letter to Marinus even explained the Latin usage charitably. So he now speaks of the council's ban on composing another creed and of his own trial, and the envoy is not treated as an enemy. Sources: Council of Ephesus canon 7; Relatio motionis; Letter to Marinus (Opusculum 10).

wills: took out the 'follows the dictation' image. A hand moved passively by dictation is the instrument (organon) model, which reads as Monothelete. Maximos teaches that the human will moves freely and in harmony, as its own. The node now says the scribe agrees with the letter and writes it as his own, and is not a quill. Idiom metaphor 4 is changed to match. Added Opusculum 6 (on Gethsemane) and the horos of the Sixth Ecumenical Council.

logoi -> wills branch: 'study of stars and waters is reading' led nowhere logically, and the stars sit next to astrology risk (rule 23). Rewritten as 'And does a man's will have its own letter too?' This bridges from logos of nature to will. Gate erudition 4 kept.

deification: the line 'God became man so that man might become god' is St Athanasius (On the Incarnation 54). Added that source. Kept Ad Thalassium 22 and the Ambigua (Maximos on theosis by grace). The iron-in-fire image is not tied to a chapter number I can't verify; John of Damascus, Exact Exposition III.17 is added as the parallel.
farewell.source: the loss of tongue and hand is not in the Relatio motionis (655). It is told in the Hypomnesticum of Theodore Spoudaeus and in the Synaxarion. Source corrected.
farewell: narration moved out of the saint's quoted voice ('The scribe puts down the pen' is stage narration). Voice kept as paraphrase for his one line.
seal -> vainglory_cue branch: its meaning now names why standing alone leads to the vainglory cue: the lone confessor is tempted to admire his own firmness.

Checked: 8 nodes; all nextNodeIds resolve; the start node has two unconditioned branches; FORM gates on erudition 6, wisdom 8, erudition 4, constitution 5, wisdom 6, wisdom 10; bonuses are integers 1-3; cunning +1 only, leads to no deeper teaching directly; no forbidden words in choice texts; no liturgical text quoted (Gethsemane words are Scripture in living speech with source).
dissent: Skeptic: the retold 'whole world had signed' line in 'seal' stays close to verbatim. It is kept as indirect speech until data/patristic-canon.json confirms the wording.
Game designer (from the author's record): wanted an erudition gate on 'logoi'. The Patrologist kept it open. The Dogmatist sides with the Patrologist.

Storyline matrix #21 quotes Maximos verbatim in its ЦЕЛЬ line and frames the scene around the Filioque. The matrix should be edited to retell the quote and to note that Maximos's own confession concerned the Typos. The lead should route this to the matrix owner (not changed here).

npcName: Melik Ashot, Keeper of the Scales
theology: Just measure and honest office: tribute may be lawful, extortion and bribery are not; alms with a request for prayer are ancient and good, but prayer is never a purchased service with a price (Prov 11:1; Lk 3:12-13; Acts 10:4; Acts 8:18-20; Ex 23:8; Mic 6:8). Wealth is entrusted, not owned (theme of the storyline: St John Chrysostom on wealth). Melik Ashot is an Armenian notable who collects tribute for the Chagatai khan; he is a partner in dialogue from his own station and confession, not a villain.

idiom.worldview: A city stands on true weights: the khan's yarlyk gives power, but only the scale gives trust.
idiom.craft: Armenian melik and tribute collector under the Chagatai khan, keeper of the weights, seals and toll board at the Issyk-Kul market and the Chu ford.
metaphors: A false weight grows lighter every year, for the one who uses it
The seal remembers what the hand forgets
A gift opens the hand; a bribe keeps a finger on the pan
When a coin comes with a whisper, weigh the whisper
A scale is useless in a drowned market
idiom.silence: He lays a weight on the empty pan and waits until the other side answers. When a question touches his soul he says only 'the scale is not balanced yet' and closes the ledger.

nodes.text: Deacon of the lake-house. Put nothing on my table yet. First tell me what you have come to weigh: silver, grain or words? Everything that crosses the Chu ford passes my scales. The khan's yarlyk says so.
nodes.text_ru: Дьякон с озёрного двора. Ничего пока не клади на мой стол. Сперва скажи, что ты пришёл взвесить: серебро, зерно или слова? Всё, что переходит брод на Чу, проходит через мои весы. Так сказано в ханском ярлыке.
nodes.meaning: The official sees the world as measure; the dialogue will test whether measure serves truth or gain, since just weight and balance belong to God.
nodes.source: Prov 16:11

branches.text: Words. I came to hear how you keep the measure.
branches.text_ru: Слова. Я пришёл послушать, как ты держишь меру.

branches.text: The old yarlyk freed the fishermen's shore from toll. Is it still in your chest?
branches.text_ru: Прежний ярлык освободил рыбачий берег от пошлины. Он ещё лежит в твоём сундуке?

branches.text: The fishermen are grumbling at the pier. Will you hear them through me?
branches.text_ru: Рыбаки ропщут на пристани. Выслушаешь их через меня?

nodes.text: These bronze weights came down from my grandfather's family, who left Ani when the city emptied. Nobody filed them, and I will not. A merchant who files his weight gains a crumb a day and loses the market in a year. A false weight grows lighter every year, for the one who uses it.
nodes.text_ru: Эти бронзовые гири достались мне от деда, чья семья ушла из Ани, когда город опустел. Никто их не подпиливал, и я не стану. Купец, что подпиливает гирю, выигрывает крошку в день и теряет рынок за год. Фальшивая гиря год от года легчает для того, кто ею пользуется.
nodes.meaning: Justice in measure is a matter of God's order, not only of trade; dishonesty impoverishes the dishonest before it harms the buyer.

branches.text: And the silver from the Herat yard, what do you weigh it for?
branches.text_ru: А серебро с Гератского двора, ради чего ты его взвешиваешь?

branches.text: Does a weight grow heavier when it is called a gift?
branches.text_ru: Тяжелеет ли гиря, если её назвать подарком?

nodes.text: You read seals, then. Yes, the old yarlyk stands, with the khan's tamga in red wax. The seal remembers what the hand forgets. I cannot raise a toll the seal forbids, not because I am kind, but because the seal is older than my greed.
nodes.text_ru: Значит, ты читаешь печати. Да, прежний ярлык в силе, с ханской тамгой на красном воске. Печать помнит то, что забывает рука. Я не могу поднять пошлину, которую печать запрещает, и не по доброте, а потому, что печать старше моей жадности.
nodes.meaning: Written law and prior right restrain power; appealing to what was justly granted is honest persuasion, not pressure. Ancient boundaries are not to be moved.
nodes.source: Prov 22:28; Deut 19:14

branches.text: Then let us bring the fishermen to the board together.
branches.text_ru: Тогда пойдём к доске пошлин вместе с рыбаками.

nodes.text: They say my toll is heavy. Tell them the truth from both pans: the tribute goes to the khan, and the khan's peace keeps robbers off the road. But tell them also that I take no more than the board says. The Forerunner told the tax-gatherers the same; I remember that much from the Gospel my mother read aloud.
nodes.text_ru: Говорят, моя пошлина тяжела. Скажи им правду с обеих чаш: дань идёт хану, а ханский мир держит разбойников подальше от дороги. Но скажи и то, что я не беру больше, чем написано на доске. Предтеча говорил мытарям то же самое, это я помню из Евангелия, которое мать читала вслух.
nodes.meaning: Lawful tribute may be paid so as not to give offence, but exacting more than is appointed is injustice; the official is bound by the measure he administers.

branches.text: Then say it yourself at the pier, and I will stand beside you.
branches.text_ru: Тогда скажи это сам на пристани, а я встану рядом.

branches.text: I will carry your words to them.
branches.text_ru: Я передам им твои слова.

nodes.text: Now, a matter between us. Here is a tenth of the silver from the Herat yard. Take it to your house, and let your brothers remember my shop in their prayers, so that the caravans keep coming. A fair trade: my silver on one pan, your words on the other.
nodes.text_ru: А теперь дело между нами. Вот десятая доля серебра с Гератского двора. Отнеси её в свою обитель, и пусть братия поминает мою лавку в молитвах, чтобы караваны не переводились. Честный обмен: моё серебро на одной чаше, ваши слова на другой.
nodes.meaning: Alms joined to a request for prayer are ancient and good (Cornelius); what is wrong is the logic of the scale, prayer as a purchased service with a guaranteed return. The test is to receive the alms and refuse the price.

branches.text: We will take it as bread for the hungry, and the brothers will remember you freely. But not as a price: our prayer does not go on your scale.
branches.text_ru: Мы примем это как хлеб для голодных, и братия помянет тебя даром. Но не как плату: наша молитва на твои весы не ложится.
branches.narrativeEffect: Melik lifts the silver off the pan and sets the pan swinging empty; the silver goes to the kitchen ledger, not to the scale.

branches.text: I cannot weigh this. Let me ask the elder first.
branches.text_ru: Я не умею это взвесить. Дай сперва спросить старца.

branches.text: I'll take it. No one needs to know how it is spent.
branches.text_ru: Возьму. Никому не нужно знать, на что оно пойдёт.
branches.narrativeEffect: A low machine-like dissonance (passion_avarice) rises under the market noise; the purse feels heavier than its weight.

nodes.text: Ah. 'No one needs to know.' I have said those words over a spare purse myself. Listen, deacon, I will tell you how I learned to hear it. The silver itself is quiet. What speaks is the little voice that comes with it: no one will know, just this once, it is for a good cause. When a coin comes with a whisper, weigh the whisper, not the coin.
nodes.text_ru: А. «Никому не нужно знать». Я сам говорил эти слова над лишним кошелём. Слушай, дьякон, скажу, как я научился это слышать. Серебро само молчит. Говорит тихий голос, что приходит вместе с ним: никто не узнает, только раз, это ради доброго дела. Когда монета приходит с шёпотом, взвешивай шёпот, а не монету.
nodes.meaning: Discernment cue for the passion of avarice: gain that arrives with secrecy and self-justification ('no one will know', 'just once', 'for a good cause'). The Cunning choice is marked as a fall, not a victory; the remedy is openness and mercy (a receipt, alms), not a holy object.
nodes.source: 1 Tim 6:9-10; Josh 7:21; Ex 23:8; St John Climacus, The Ladder, steps 16-17

branches.text: Then let it go into the poor's share, with a receipt in your ledger.
branches.text_ru: Тогда пусть оно уйдёт в долю бедных, с распиской в твоей книге.
branches.narrativeEffect: The dissonance fades into the quiet of the treasury.

branches.text: Put it back in the chest. I was wrong.
branches.text_ru: Положи его обратно в сундук. Я был неправ.

nodes.text: A gift. Yes, there is a gift and there is a bribe, and on my scale they weigh exactly the same. The difference is in the hand afterwards. A gift opens the hand and forgets. A bribe keeps a finger on the pan. Whoever comes to my table, let him bring nothing with him that asks.
nodes.text_ru: Дар. Да, есть дар и есть взятка, и на моих весах они весят одинаково. Разница в руке после. Дар разжимает руку и забывает. Взятка держит палец на чаше. Кто бы ни пришёл к моему столу, пусть не приносит с собой ничего, что просит.
nodes.meaning: A gift expects no return; a bribe blinds judgment and binds the receiver. The difference lies not in the object but in the intention and the claim that follows it.

branches.text: Then the lake-house will come to your board with empty hands and a true count.
branches.text_ru: Тогда озёрный двор придёт к твоей доске с пустыми руками и честным счётом.

branches.text: A finger on the pan. I will watch for it in myself.
branches.text_ru: Палец на чаше. Я буду замечать его в себе.

nodes.text: I serve the khan, I keep the scales, and when the market is closed I pray in my own church. We are not the same, you and I, but we can both keep the weights clean. Go. If your scribe is right and the water is rising, come to me: a scale is useless in a drowned market.
nodes.text_ru: Я служу хану, храню весы, а когда рынок закрыт, молюсь в своей церкви. Мы с тобой не одно и то же, но оба можем держать гири честными. Ступай. Если твой писец прав и вода поднимается, приходи ко мне: весы бесполезны на затопленном рынке.
nodes.meaning: Neighbours of different confessions and stations share the duty of justice and mercy; the scene foreshadows the flood mission where the melik must be persuaded to move the town.
nodes.source: Mic 6:8; Mic 6:11

branches.text: Keep the weights clean, Melik. I will come when the water rises.
branches.text_ru: Держи гири честными, мелик. Я приду, когда вода поднимется.

decisions: bias: a tax man for the Mongol khan should be the villain of the market / counter: TABOO 0.37 p.4 and historical reality (Armenian notables served Chagatai administration and also founded churches and caravanserais) / why: Melik is a conscientious official tempted like anyone; he himself teaches the avarice cue from his own fall, which keeps him a partner, not a target.

bias: tribute to a non-Christian khan is itself unjust / counter: Rom 13:7, Mt 17:24-27 and Lk 3:12-13 allow lawful tribute and forbid only extortion / why: the teaching is 'no more than the board says'. Dissent kept (Aristotle-skeptic): the khan's peace is also a protection racket; the flood and tarkhan storylines should show its limits.

bias: the Cunning branch 'take the silver' should give a bigger payoff to be tempting / counter: 0.35 p.15-16, contract p.5 (Cunning at most +1, with cost) / why: Cunning +1 only, the meaning marks it as a fall, it triggers the passion_avarice dissonance, and it opens no deeper teaching; the way out is by Wisdom 7 or plain repentance.

bias: refusing silver for prayer should pay Faith as a pious act / counter: prayer is never paid in attributes (0.35 p.16) / why: the Faith +2 rewards understanding that prayer is not a commodity (Acts 8:20), i.e. discernment, not performing any rite.

bias: the grandfather's weights from Ani is colourful but anachronistic / counter: Ani declined after the 13th-century invasions and its families dispersed along trade routes into the 14th century / why: kept as family memory, not a dated event. Dissent kept (historian, myself): an Armenian presence at Issyk-Kul is attested mainly via the Catalan Atlas tradition of an Armenian monastery; the chorus should keep the Armenian quarter modest in size.

bias: Melik, as an Armenian Christian, may name 'our prophet John' / counter: Armenians honour John the Forerunner in the same Gospel; 'your prophet' would falsely make him a non-Christian / why: he says 'the Forerunner' and 'the Gospel my mother read', living speech with source Lk 3:12-13, no liturgical text quoted.
