bias: every exchange should route through Wisdom checks / counter: 0.35 p.14 and contract p.5 / why: gates are erudition 3, charisma 4, wisdom 5, faith 4, charisma 6, wisdom 6, wisdom 7; the start node keeps one unconditional branch so a guest with every attribute at 1 can talk.

bias: his proverbs ('a false weight grows lighter', 'weigh the whisper') might be read as quotations of Scripture / counter: 0.35 p.18 forbids invented citations / why: they are his own trade sayings in his idiom; the Scripture they echo (Prov 11:1, Ex 23:8) is given only in the source field, never as a quoted verse in his mouth.

bias (patrologist): 'silver for prayers' is simply simony and must be refused outright / counter: alms joined to a request for prayer are ancient and blameless (Acts 10:4, Cornelius; 1 Tim 2:1); Acts 8:18-20 condemns buying the gift of God, i.e. the logic of price and guaranteed return / why: the Faith-gated choice now receives the silver as bread for the hungry and remembers Melik freely, while refusing the scale; teaching that all offerings for prayer are simony would itself be false doctrine.

bias (patrologist): the Faith-gated refusal deserves Faith +2 / counter: 0.35 p.16, the bonus pays understanding, not a pious act / why: changed to wisdom 2 + faith 1, since what is gained is discernment between alms and price.

bias (Aristotle-skeptic): the Cunning path should reach the richest wisdom reward because it contains the repentance / counter: contract p.5, Cunning must never net more than the honest path / why: m_no_one bonuses reduced to wisdom 2 (Wisdom 7) and wisdom 1 (plain repentance); the fall teaches, but does not pay better than not falling.

bias (ethnographer): the lake-house sending wine to the tax board is a friendly gesture / counter: in the node that teaches gift versus bribe, a monastery's gift to the official who taxes its fishermen is exactly the 'finger on the pan' / why: replaced by 'empty hands and a true count', which makes the teaching act consistent with itself.

fixes: m_prayer_silver: the doctrine was overstated. Giving alms to a monastery and asking for prayers is ancient and lawful (Acts 10:4, Cornelius; 1 Tim 2:1). Simony (Acts 8:18-20) is the logic of a price: a purchased service with a guaranteed return. The node's meaning and source now separate the two, and the Faith-gated choice becomes 'take it as alms, remember him freely, not as a price' instead of refusing the silver outright.

m_prayer_silver Faith branch: the bonus changed from faith 2 + wisdom 1 to wisdom 2 + faith 1. It pays for understanding the difference between alms and price. It does not pay for the rite of praying (0.35 p.16).

m_no_one: the rewards on the Cunning path were cut so that the fall never pays more than the honest path. Wisdom-7 repentance went from wisdom 3 to 2, and plain repentance from wisdom 2 to 1. Total on the Cunning path is now at most cunning 1 + wisdom 2.
m_no_one source: Josh 7:21 added (Achan hid what he took; secrecy is the cue). The Ladder is kept as 'steps 16-17' (on love of money and on non-possessiveness), which are real step numbers.

m_gift Wisdom-6 branch: 'the lake-house will send wine with no letter' made a monastery send a gift to a tax official, which contradicts the node's own teaching. It is now 'we will come to your board with empty hands and a true count'.
m_pier source: Mt 17:24-27 added (the stater in the fish), because the matrix storyline for Melik and the fisherman uses it.

Checks passed and kept: 8 nodes; every nextNodeId resolves or is null; the start node has an unconditioned branch; FORM gates are erudition 3, charisma 4, wisdom 5, faith 4, charisma 6, wisdom 6 and wisdom 7; bonuses are integers from 1 to 3; Cunning gives +1 once and opens no gate; none of the forbidden words appear in player choices in either English or Russian; no liturgical text is quoted; voice is 'own' because Melik is not a saint.
dissent: Aristotle-skeptic: the avarice discernment node (m_no_one) can be reached only through the Cunning choice, so a player who never falls never hears the cue. I suggest a later storyline node (matrix line 1952: 'treasury, debt, temptation') that repeats the cue on a non-Cunning path. This tree is not rebuilt for it.

Patrologist: whether an Orthodox monastery should commemorate a non-Chalcedonian Armenian needs care. The branch promises only that the brothers will 'remember you' in private prayer (1 Tim 2:1), not commemoration at the altar. Keep that wording if the tree is edited later.
Ethnographer (kept from author): the Armenian presence at Issyk-Kul is thinly attested, so the Armenian quarter should stay small in scale.

theology: Learning subject to the Word: the patriarch-scholar who read everything, guarded the Creed unaltered (procession of the Spirit from the Father), and sent the Gospel to the Slavs in their own tongue.

idiom.worldview: Read everything, keep the marrow, mark the error in the margin, and never let the book become your master instead of the Word.
idiom.craft: Scholar-bibliophile and patriarch of Constantinople: reader, epitomist, letter-writer, shepherd.
images: the lost sheep on the shoulders
metaphors: An epitome keeps the marrow and leaves the bones
The margin is where discernment writes
The Creed is the one codex that is copied, never glossed
A seal is not lent
New letters for an old Gospel
idiom.silence: When pressed to judge a stranger or to put his seal on a favour, he closes the codex and trims the lamp without a word.

nodes.text: Sit by the lamp. When I was sent away on an embassy, my brother Tarasius asked me for the books I had read while we were apart, so I wrote him the marrow of each one, codex after codex. Reading is my craft. The shepherd's staff leans by the shelf so that I do not forget whom the books serve.
nodes.text_ru: Садись у светильника. Когда меня отправляли с посольством, брат мой Тарасий попросил у меня книги, прочитанные мною без него, и я выписал ему самую суть каждой, кодекс за кодексом. Чтение — моё ремесло. Пастырский посох стоит у полки, чтобы я не забывал, кому служат книги.
nodes.meaning: Christian learning is legitimate and broad, but it is subordinate to pastoral service and the Word.
nodes.source: St Photius, Bibliotheca (Myriobiblon), dedicatory letter to Tarasius

branches.text: Why read the books of pagans at all?
branches.text_ru: Зачем вообще читать книги язычников?

branches.text: Teach me how you make an epitome.
branches.text_ru: Научи меня, как ты делаешь выписку-сокращение.

branches.text: Tell me of the brothers who went north with new letters.
branches.text_ru: Расскажи о братьях, что ушли на север с новыми буквами.

branches.text: Put your seal on a letter for me; doors will open.
branches.text_ru: Приложи свою печать к письму для меня — передо мной откроются двери.

branches.text: Something weighs on me. May I tell you what I did?
branches.text_ru: Меня что-то тяготит. Можно рассказать тебе, что я сделал?

nodes.text: Basil taught the young to read like the bee, which does not take the whole flower, only what makes honey. So I read the novelists and the orators. Read to the end before you judge. Keep the marrow, leave the bones. Name an author's style honestly, even when you disagree with him. And in the margin write plainly where he strays from the truth; that line is worth more than the rest of the page. The book was never my master.
nodes.text_ru: Василий учил юношей читать, как пчела, что берёт с цветка не всё, а только то, из чего будет мёд. Так я читал сочинителей и риторов. Дочитай до конца, прежде чем судить. Сохрани мозг кости, а кости оставь. Честно назови слог автора, даже если не согласен с ним. А на полях прямо напиши, где он уклоняется от истины: эта строка стоит больше всей страницы. Книга никогда не была мне господином.
nodes.meaning: Pagan and secular learning may be read with discernment, taking what is useful and rejecting what corrupts; fairness to the author and clarity about error are both duties of the Christian reader.
nodes.source: St Basil the Great, Address to Young Men on the Right Use of Greek Literature (image of the bee); St Photius, Bibliotheca (critical reviews of secular works)

branches.text: Is there a text you would never gloss or trim?
branches.text_ru: Есть ли текст, который ты никогда не стал бы сокращать или дополнять?

branches.text: And how do I know I am reading for honey and not for show?
branches.text_ru: А как понять, что я читаю ради мёда, а не напоказ?

nodes.text: One codex is copied and never glossed: the Creed the councils gave. Add a single word in the margin, and the margin becomes the text. I wrote at length that the Spirit proceeds from the Father, as the Lord said, and that no one Church may rewrite on its own what all the councils sealed.
nodes.text_ru: Один кодекс переписывают, но не дополняют: Символ, данный соборами. Допиши на полях одно слово — и поле станет текстом. Я много писал о том, что Дух исходит от Отца, как сказал Господь, и что ни одна Церковь в одиночку не вправе переписывать то, что запечатали все соборы.
nodes.meaning: The Nicene-Constantinopolitan Creed is not altered unilaterally; the Holy Spirit proceeds from the Father (against the Filioque addition). Stated as teaching, without hostility to persons.
nodes.source: John 15:26; Council of Ephesus (431), canon 7; St Photius, Mystagogy of the Holy Spirit; St Photius, Encyclical Letter to the Eastern Patriarchs (867)

branches.text: I will copy it, and not add.
branches.text_ru: Буду переписывать и не добавлять.

nodes.text: Constantine and Methodius went to the Slavs, and Constantine shaped letters for a tongue that had none. The Gospel does not need a foreign alphabet to enter a heart; each people heard it in its own speech at Pentecost. I also wrote to the Bulgarian prince on how a ruler should live.
nodes.text_ru: Константин и Мефодий пошли к славянам, и Константин сложил буквы для языка, у которого их не было. Евангелию не нужна чужая азбука, чтобы войти в сердце: в Пятидесятницу каждый народ слышал его на своём наречии. Я писал и болгарскому князю — о том, каким должен быть правитель.
nodes.meaning: Mission in the people's own language; faith is not bound to one culture; rulers are called to Christian virtue.
nodes.source: Acts 2:6-8; Life of Constantine-Cyril (Vita Constantini); St Photius, Letter to Boris-Michael of Bulgaria

branches.text: So I should speak to the caravans in their own words.
branches.text_ru: Значит, с караванщиками надо говорить их словами.

branches.text: And if they do not want to hear?
branches.text_ru: А если они не захотят слушать?

nodes.text: A seal is not lent. It says 'I stand behind this.' If I press it for your convenience, it no longer means anything, even when I need it for the truth. I was deposed twice and restored once; I know what a seal costs.
nodes.text_ru: Печать не дают взаймы. Она говорит: «Я за это ручаюсь». Если приложу её ради твоего удобства, она перестанет что-либо значить, даже когда понадобится для правды. Меня дважды низлагали и однажды вернули — я знаю цену печати.
nodes.meaning: Church office is service, not a tool for advantage; the cunning request gains a small skill but costs trust and opens no teaching.
nodes.source: 1 Peter 5:2-3; Synaxarion, February 6 (St Photius)

branches.text: I understand. Why did I want the seal so much?
branches.text_ru: Понимаю. Почему же мне так хотелось этой печати?

nodes.text: Not here at the reading lamp. What you carry belongs to the priest, before God, and it is written in no codex: no scribe copies it, no margin keeps it, no epitome is made of it. Go to your priest. This hall will not remember what you were about to say.
nodes.text_ru: Не здесь, не у светильника. То, что ты несёшь, принадлежит священнику, пред Богом, и не записывается ни в какой кодекс: никакой писец его не перепишет, никакие поля его не сохранят, никакой выписки из него не сделают. Иди к своему священнику. Этот зал не запомнит того, что ты хотел сказать.
nodes.meaning: Confession is a sacrament performed by a priest and is never a game mechanic; its secrecy is absolute. The game shows only the door: this choice stores no log, no text, no counter and gives no attribute.
nodes.source: James 5:16; 1 John 1:9; Extended Christian Catechism of St Philaret (on the Mystery of Repentance); Nomocanon in XIV Titles (recension of 883, traditionally linked to Photius)

branches.text: I will go to the priest.
branches.text_ru: Я пойду к священнику.
branches.narrativeEffect: NO_LOG: confession door. The choice is not stored, not sent to the server, not counted in analytics; the scene ends in silence

nodes.text: Watch your own margins. Vainglory in a reader shows itself so: you remember who heard you, not what you read; you hurry to correct others in company and forget to correct yourself alone; you quote to be admired; you want a seal on your letter more than truth in it. When the lamp is lit for an audience, it is already smoking.
nodes.text_ru: Следи за собственными полями. Тщеславие читателя выдаёт себя так: ты помнишь, кто тебя слушал, а не что ты прочёл; спешишь поправить других при людях и забываешь поправить себя наедине; цитируешь, чтобы тобой восхищались; хочешь печати на письме больше, чем правды в нём. Когда светильник зажжён для зрителей, он уже коптит.
nodes.meaning: Discernment cue for vainglory: learning or standing pursued for being seen; recognised by attention to the audience and to marks of approval rather than to truth.
nodes.source: St John Climacus, The Ladder, Step 22 (On vainglory); Matthew 6:1

branches.text: I will read for honey, not for the audience.
branches.text_ru: Буду читать ради мёда, а не ради слушателей.

nodes.text: The lamp is trimmed. A shepherd who reads all night and forgets the one sheep lost on the hill has read in vain. And if the sheep will not come, he does not drive it with the staff; he goes after it again, and carries it when it lets him. Close the codex gently and go.
nodes.text_ru: Фитиль подрезан. Пастырь, что читает всю ночь и забывает одну овцу, заблудившуюся на холме, читал напрасно. А если овца не идёт, он не гонит её посохом — он снова идёт за ней и несёт её, когда она позволит. Закрой кодекс бережно и ступай.
nodes.meaning: Knowledge is fulfilled in pastoral love; the scholar-bishop's model is the shepherd seeking the lost sheep, patiently and without coercion.
nodes.source: Luke 15:4-5; John 10:11

branches.text: I will close the codex and go.
branches.text_ru: Закрою кодекс и пойду.
branches.narrativeEffect: Meeting recorded; the reading lamp burns lower

decisions: bias: let the player 'confess' to Photius for a Faith bonus / counter (catechist, liturgist, operator request of this run): confession is a priest's sacrament, off-screen, and the user's words must not be stored / why: confession_door gives no attributes, is flagged NO_LOG in narrativeEffect so the engine must not persist the choice, text, counter or analytics event; declared in meaning. Dissent: game designer asked to at least count 'went to confession' for gate progress; rejected by catechist+patrologist+dogmatist majority: a counter turns the sacrament into a ritual metric (TABOO 0.35 r.16)

bias: Photius is a bishop and could himself hear confession in-scene / counter (dogmatist): in the game frame no sacrament is performed or simulated / why: he redirects to 'your priest', consistent with storyline 26 where the confession stays behind the door

bias: frame the Filioque node as polemic against Latins / counter (sceptic, historian): TABOO 0.37 requires non-Orthodox to be partners, not targets / why: creed_margin states the doctrine and the conciliar principle, names no people as enemies; source cites Ephesus canon 7 and the Mystagogy, not invented lines

bias: attribute the bee image to Photius / counter (patrologist): it is St Basil's Address to Young Men / why: source credits Basil and Photius now names Basil in his own speech; Photius's own claim is only the critical method of the Bibliotheca

bias: the seal request should be a hidden 'influence' path rewarding charisma / counter: office is not a tool (1 Peter 5:2-3) / why: cunning +1 only, no deeper teaching, cost stated in meaning; mention of his two depositions kept to the Synaxarion without invented speech
bias: exact chapter numbers for Mystagogy and Encyclical / counter (sceptic): not verified / why: works cited without chapter numbers

bias (patrologist review): keep Vita Constantini ch. 14 as 'the alphabet chapter' / counter (Aristotle-sceptic): the number was flagged unverified by the author himself / why: downgraded to the work title per contract; no fabricated numbers

bias: 'when my brother Tarasius went away' reads warmly / counter (patrologist, historian): the dedicatory letter says Photius left on an embassy and Tarasius asked for the books read in his absence / why: corrected; a false biographical detail in a saint's mouth is an invented testimony (TABOO 0.35 r.18)

bias: keep the Nomocanon of 883 as the sole source for the confession door / counter (patrologist): its attribution to Photius is traditional, not certain, and it is canon law rather than doctrine / why: kept with 'traditionally linked' wording, and Philaret's Catechism on the Mystery of Repentance added as the doctrinal ground

bias: keep 9 nodes, every one is good / counter (game designer of the Constitution): the contract fixes 6-8 / why: pagan_books and epitome_art merged into margin_art with no teaching lost; the erudition-5 entry keeps its higher bonus by depth. Dissent: dogmatist preferred cutting slavic_mission instead; rejected by majority, because the mission in the people's own tongue is the heart of Photius for a Semirechye caravan setting

bias: 'Then teach me something instead' after the seal refusal should lead back to the reading method / counter (Aristotle-sceptic): a cunning request would then be a side door to the erudition-8 Creed node / why: rerouted to vainglory_cue, which names the passion behind wanting a seal; cunning opens no deeper teaching

bias: the wisdom-6 question 'what if they do not want to hear?' is answered by the generic farewell / counter (sceptic): the NPC never answered it, so the +3 paid for nothing / why: library_end now gives the answer (the shepherd goes after the sheep again and does not use the staff to drive it, which also rules out coercion under TABOO 0.37 point 4); bonus lowered to +2

fixes: Node count was 9 and the contract allows 6-8. pagan_books and epitome_art are merged into one node, margin_art, which keeps both the bee image and the epitome method. Both start branches still lead there, with bonuses set by depth (unconditioned: wisdom 1; erudition >= 5: erudition 2, wisdom 1).

Historical error in the library node: in the dedicatory letter of the Bibliotheca it was Photius who was sent away on an embassy, and Tarasius asked for the books read while they were apart. The text is corrected in both English and Russian.

Confession source: the Nomocanon in XIV Titles (883) is only traditionally linked to Photius, so it is downgraded to that wording. The Extended Christian Catechism of St Philaret (on the Mystery of Repentance) is added as the doctrinal source.
Basil's Address to Young Men is cited by work only, with no chapter. The bee image is now openly credited to Basil in the NPC's own speech.
The Vita Constantini chapter number is removed. The chapter-14 attribution is not verified, so the work is cited by title only.

slavic_mission: the wisdom-6 question 'And if they do not want to hear?' got no answer. library_end now answers it: the shepherd goes after the sheep again and does not drive it with a stick, which also rules out pressure or forced conversion. The bonus is lowered from 3 to 2 because the answer is short.

seal_refusal follow-up now leads to vainglory_cue (seeking to be seen) instead of the reading method. The cunning path therefore lands on a discernment cue for the very passion behind the request and opens no deeper teaching.
idiom.images: 'the brother Tarasius' is a person, not an object of the craft, and is replaced with 'the ink-horn'.

theology: Lay Orthodox piety of the apostolic fishermen: honest labour, an empty net shown rather than hidden (Lk 5:5-8), repentance met by calling (Lk 5:10), stillness under the cold layer, the lake as creation and not a deity. Not a saint, no nimbus.

idiom.worldview: The lake gives what it gives; a man's part is to mend the net, cast at the right depth and never lie about the catch.
idiom.craft: Net fishing from a dugout boat on Issyk-Kul: reading wind, depth and the cold layer (thermocline), mending nets on the jetty.
metaphors: An empty net shown on the jetty is honester than a full one bought at market.
Mending comes before the catch.
The cell you hide tears wider.
Below the cold layer the water is still and sound carries far.
A small mesh holds, a wide mesh lets go.
idiom.silence: When a question is not his to answer, he starts mending the net, knot by knot, and speaks only when the knot is tied.

nodes.text: Mind the ropes, deacon. I came in with an empty net, and I lay it out on the jetty for all to see. An empty net shown is honester than a full one bought at market.
nodes.text_ru: Осторожно, дьякон, тут верёвки. Я вернулся с пустой сетью и раскладываю её на причале у всех на виду. Пустая сеть, которую показали, честнее полной, купленной на базаре.
nodes.meaning: Honesty about one's own emptiness is the beginning of repentance; Peter confessed a fruitless night before the miracle.
nodes.source: Lk 5:5

branches.text: Why lay out an empty net for everyone to see?
branches.text_ru: Зачем показывать всем пустую сеть?

branches.text: Teach me to read the water under the boat.
branches.text_ru: Научи меня читать воду под лодкой.

branches.text: Is the fish scratched on that pile a charm against drowning?
branches.text_ru: Рыба, процарапанная на свае, — оберег от утопления?

branches.text: Buy a full net at market and show it as yours. Nobody will know.
branches.text_ru: Купи полную сеть на базаре и выдай за свою. Никто не узнает.
branches.narrativeEffect: The fisherman stops coiling the rope and looks at the deacon for a long time.

nodes.text: There was a fisherman on another lake who toiled all night and caught nothing. At the Teacher's word he cast again, and the nets began to tear with fish. And the first thing he did was fall at the Teacher's knees and say he was a sinful man. The catch did not make him proud. It made him see his own hands.
nodes.text_ru: Был рыбак на другом озере: всю ночь трудился и ничего не поймал. По слову Учителя закинул снова, и сети стали рваться от рыбы. А первое, что он сделал, — припал к коленям Учителя и сказал, что он человек грешный. Улов не сделал его гордым. Улов показал ему его собственные руки.
nodes.meaning: Meeting God does not puff a man up but reveals his sinfulness; confession begins with seeing oneself in the light, not with a list of deeds.

branches.text: And what did the Teacher answer him?
branches.text_ru: А что ответил ему Учитель?

branches.text: So the full net showed the fisherman, not the fish.
branches.text_ru: Значит, полная сеть показала рыбака, а не рыбу.

nodes.text: He did not send him away. He told him not to be afraid, and that from now on he would be catching men. Do you see? He did not take the net from him. He gave him a wider sea.
nodes.text_ru: Он не прогнал его. Сказал: не бойся, отныне будешь ловить человеков. Видишь? Сеть у него не отняли. Ему дали море шире.
nodes.meaning: Repentance is answered by a calling, not by rejection; God does not destroy the person's craft but transfigures it into service.

branches.text: I will think about this on the shore.
branches.text_ru: Я подумаю об этом на берегу.

branches.text: Tell me how you mend a torn net.
branches.text_ru: Расскажи, как ты чинишь рваную сеть.

nodes.text: Mending comes before the catch. I pass every cell through my fingers in daylight, not in the dark, and I name each tear aloud to my brother in the boat. The cell you hide tears wider. At the end of the jetty there is a corner with a lectern and a lamp. There a man shows his torn cells to God, and the priest stands beside him like the second man in the boat who holds the lamp. Nobody writes it down. The lake does not keep what was let go.
nodes.text_ru: Починка — раньше улова. Каждую ячею я пропускаю через пальцы днём, не в темноте, и каждую прореху называю вслух брату в лодке. Спрятанная ячея рвётся шире. В конце причала есть угол: аналой и лампада. Там человек показывает Богу свои рваные ячеи, а священник стоит рядом, как второй в лодке, что держит лампу. Никто ничего не записывает. Озеро не держит того, что отпущено.
nodes.meaning: Sins that are named are healed, and hidden ones grow. In confession Christ Himself forgives: the priest is witness and minister, through whom the penitent receives the visible declaration of pardon and is invisibly loosed by Christ. What is forgiven is not archived and is not kept against the penitent.
nodes.source: 1 Jn 1:9; Jas 5:16; Jn 20:22-23; Extended Catechism of St Philaret, on the Mystery of Penance; Ladder, step 4

branches.text: What tears a net more than anything?
branches.text_ru: Что рвёт сеть сильнее всего?

branches.text: Then I will not wait for a full net to go to that corner.
branches.text_ru: Тогда я не буду ждать полной сети, чтобы пойти в тот угол.
branches.narrativeEffect: The fisherman nods and goes back to his knots without a word.

nodes.text: Greed tears it. The man who will not let the small fish through the cell. He weighs the catch before he gives thanks for it, counts at night instead of sleeping, and for him the net is never 'enough'. Here is the sign: you think of the scales before you think of the people waiting on the shore. And the word 'enough' has gone out of your mouth.
nodes.text_ru: Жадность рвёт. Человек, который не пропускает мелкую рыбу сквозь ячею. Он взвешивает улов раньше, чем поблагодарит за него, считает ночью вместо сна, и сети ему всегда «мало». Вот признак: ты думаешь о весах раньше, чем о людях, что ждут на берегу. И слово «довольно» ушло у тебя изо рта.
nodes.meaning: Discernment cue for the passion of avarice: gratitude and the sense of 'enough' disappear, things are counted before people are seen. It is healed by mercy and thankfulness, not by any object.
nodes.source: Ladder, steps 16-17; 1 Tim 6:6-10

branches.text: I will listen for the word 'enough' in my own mouth.
branches.text_ru: Я буду прислушиваться, звучит ли у меня во рту слово «довольно».

branches.text: Then I will let the small fish go and share my catch with the shore.
branches.text_ru: Тогда я отпущу мелочь и поделюсь уловом с берегом.

nodes.text: Out past the third float the water changes. On top it is warm and loud, the wind throws it about. Below, there is a cold layer, and under it the water is still. A sound goes far there; a knock on the hull comes back clean. The fish gather under that layer. The lake is no spirit to be fed with offerings; it is a work of the Maker, like my own hands. And a man has such a layer too: under all his talk, there is a still place where a voice carries.
nodes.text_ru: За третьим поплавком вода меняется. Сверху тёплая и шумная, её треплет ветер. Ниже — холодный слой, а под ним вода тихая. Звук там идёт далеко: стук по борту возвращается чистым. Рыба собирается под этим слоем. Озеро — не дух, которого надо кормить подношениями, оно дело рук Творца, как и мои руки. И в человеке есть такой слой: под всеми его разговорами — тихое место, где голос слышно далеко.
nodes.meaning: The lake is creation, not a deity. Stillness (hesychia) is the inner depth where God's word is heard; it is a gift of attention, not a technique that earns anything.

branches.text: So one must go down quietly, not shout from the surface.
branches.text_ru: Значит, надо тихо уходить вглубь, а не кричать с поверхности.

branches.text: Show me the net you came back with.
branches.text_ru: Покажи сеть, с которой ты вернулся.

nodes.text: That fish was scratched by the old people. Five letters: Jesus Christ, God's Son, Saviour. It is a confession of faith cut into wood, not a charm. Nail a hundred fish to the boat, and you still check every knot before going out.
nodes.text_ru: Эту рыбу процарапали старые люди. Пять букв: Иисус Христос, Божий Сын, Спаситель. Это исповедание веры, вырезанное на дереве, а не оберег. Прибей к лодке хоть сто рыб — узлы перед выходом всё равно проверяешь сам.
nodes.meaning: The ΙΧΘΥΣ sign is a confession of faith, not an amulet; faith does not replace sober human care and is never magic.
nodes.source: St Augustine, The City of God XVIII.23

branches.text: I will look for the other signs on the jetty.
branches.text_ru: Я поищу другие знаки на причале.

branches.text: And the empty net on the planks?
branches.text_ru: А пустая сеть на досках?

nodes.text: A bought net shown as mine? The lake would know. I would know. And tomorrow I would have to buy again, and the day after. A lie is a fish you have to feed every day, and it only grows.
nodes.text_ru: Купленную сеть выдать за свою? Озеро будет знать. Я буду знать. А завтра придётся покупать снова, и послезавтра. Ложь — это рыба, которую кормишь каждый день, и она только растёт.
nodes.meaning: Cunning seems to gain something but binds a man to repeated deceit; the small gain of cunning is paid for with the loss of freedom and honesty.
nodes.source: Prov 20:17

branches.text: You are right. Show me the empty net.
branches.text_ru: Ты прав. Покажи пустую сеть.

branches.text: I am going.
branches.text_ru: Я пойду.

decisions: bias: a fisherman is a quaint extra who only gives directions / counter: CLAUDE.md A requires every NPC to teach; the net is the Gospel's own image (Lk 5, Mt 4:19) / why: his whole teaching is carried by nets, depth and mending, so the Aesopian idiom and the doctrine coincide.

bias: the confession corner needs an explicit rite and a reward for confessing / counter: TABOO 0.4 rule 1 and 0.35 rule 16 forbid turning a mystery into a mechanic / why: the corner is only named in living speech (lectern, lamp, 'nobody writes it down'); no bonus is paid for confessing, bonuses go to understanding; the priest is a witness, as in the user's request 'no voice recording'.

bias: quote the rite of confession to make the corner feel authentic / counter: TABOO 0.2 p.7 and the task contract forbid quoting liturgical text / why: the fisherman paraphrases the idea (second man in the boat holding the lamp) and cites Scripture and Ladder step 4 instead.

bias: the ROV-diver voice should make the fisherman talk sonar / counter: he is a 14th-century lakeman / why: the thermocline appears as 'the cold layer' and 'a knock on the hull comes back clean' - physics true to the diver, words true to the fisherman.

bias: the cunning path could open a secret fishing spot / counter: TABOO 0.35 rule 14, Cunning opens nothing deeper / why: cunning +1 once, the node explains the cost (Prov 20:17) and leads back to the empty net or out.
bias: the ichthys sign could give luck at sea / counter: sign as amulet is magic (TABOO 0.2 p.4) / why: the fisherman says 'you still check every knot yourself'.

dissent kept (Aristotle-sceptic): Lk 5 has Peter at Gennesaret, not Issyk-Kul; the fisherman must say 'another lake' so the game never claims an apostle walked here (matrix storyline with Wisdom >= 5 refusal) - accepted.

catechist: bias: 'the priest is only a witness' is enough doctrine for a fisherman / counter: the Extended Catechism of St Philaret teaches that the penitent is invisibly loosed by Christ through the priest's ministry (Jn 20:22-23), so 'only a witness' would read as a Protestant reduction / why: the fisherman's image (the second man holding the lamp) stays, and the meaning and source now carry the full teaching for the theologian.

catechist: bias: deciding to go to confession deserves Faith points / counter: TABOO 0.35 rule 16 says rites are never paid as such / why: the branch keeps its Faith>=4 gate but pays Wisdom for understanding that naming heals.

catechist: bias: an ending button may be a bare question / counter: a question that closes the conversation leaves the passion lesson unanswered / why: the avarice buttons now voice the player's own recognition and the opposing virtue (mercy, sharing) in the first person, not orders to the NPC.

catechist: bias: a lakeman's awe of the deep is harmless colour / counter: the matrix (line 1057) requires 'the lake is creation, not a deity' and TABOO 0.4 p.6 forbids paganism as truth / why: one plain line about the Maker's work was added to cold_layer (Ps 103:24-25 LXX), inside his own idiom of offerings and hands.

fixes: mending.meaning/source: the priest is not only a witness. Per the Extended Catechism of St Philaret (the Mystery of Penance, under Article 10 of the Creed), the penitent receives from the priest the visible declaration of pardon and is invisibly loosed by Christ. Jn 20:22-23 and the Catechism are now cited, and the image of the second man in the boat holding the lamp is kept.

mending, branch 'Then I will not wait...': the bonus changed from faith+2/wisdom+1 to wisdom+2, keeping the gate faith>=4. The resolve to go to confession is not paid (TABOO 0.35 rule 16). Only the understanding that naming the torn cell heals is rewarded.
avarice, branch 1: the button asked a question and then ended the talk with no answer. It is rewritten as the player's recognition ('I will listen for the word enough in my own mouth').

avarice, branch 2: the player was giving the fisherman orders ('let the small fish go'). It is rewritten in the first person, so the virtue opposed to the passion (mercy and sharing) is the player's own choice.
cold_layer: added a line that the lake is the Maker's work and not a spirit to be fed (matrix storyline at line 1057; no paganism as truth). Ps 103:24-25 LXX is added to the source.
empty_net text_ru: 'упал Учителю в колени' is changed to 'припал к коленям Учителя', which is closer to Lk 5:8 and still a retelling.

Checked and left unchanged: the tree has 8 nodes, every nextNodeId resolves, and the start node has 2 unconditioned branches. It has 6 FORM-gated branches (con3, eru3, wis5, fai4, cha5, wis6). Cunning gives +1 once, opens nothing and its cost is stated. No forbidden words appear in the buttons. No liturgical text is quoted. Sources checked: Lk 5:4-10, Mt 4:19, 1 Jn 1:9, Jas 5:16, Ladder steps 4, 16-17 and 27, Ps 45:11 LXX, Mk 4:39, Prov 20:17, and Augustine, City of God XVIII.23 (ΙΧΘΥΣ acrostic).
dissent: Aristotle-sceptic: in the 14th century the Christians of Semirechye and Issyk-Kul were mostly of the Church of the East, not Byzantine Orthodox. The 'old people' who scratched the fish are therefore left unnamed as to confession. The game does not claim them for either Church. Kept open for the historian-ethnographer.

Aristotle-sceptic: the cold_layer branch 'Show me the net...' grants constitution+1 for a mere return to another node, which is weakly motivated. Left as the author's choice because it is small and deterministic.

theology: Hospitality against the love of money: the just scale, the stranger at the well, the open hand (Prov 11:1; Prov 19:17; Lk 12:15-21; Lk 19:8; Mt 25:35; Ladder, steps 16-17). An Armenian merchant drawn with dignity; his temptations are the honest human temptations of trade, and his turning is left to his own Church, not enacted by the game.

idiom.worldview: Every road is paid for twice, once in silver and once in the knees of the camels; the scale remembers everything.
idiom.craft: Caravan master (karavan-bashi) on the silk road from Semirechye to Tana: loading bales, keeping the ledger, weighing silver, choosing wells and halts.
metaphors: the scale remembers
one more bale breaks the camel at the pass
the well belongs to every caravan
a stranger at the well is a debt the road lends you
a road is paid in feet, not only in coin
idiom.silence: He stops counting, lays his palm flat on the scale pan so it cannot move, and waits until the other man speaks first.

nodes.text: Welcome, deacon, sit by the bales. Forty camels, eleven wells to Tana, and every well remembers who drank and who paid. What will you trade? Or have you come to count my sins in your ledger?
nodes.text_ru: Добро пожаловать, дьякон, садись у тюков. Сорок верблюдов, одиннадцать колодцев до Таны, и каждый колодец помнит, кто пил и кто платил. Что ты продаёшь? Или пришёл пересчитать мои грехи в своей книге?
nodes.meaning: The merchant greets through the measure of trade; the meeting opens to any guest without a test. His jibe about a 'ledger of sins' is his own misunderstanding: a deacon does not hear confession, and the game keeps no account of sins.
nodes.source: Heb 13:2

branches.text: I came to help build the guest-house on the shore.
branches.text_ru: Я пришёл помочь строить странноприимный двор на берегу.

branches.text: May I set your weights against the khan's standard?
branches.text_ru: Можно сверить твои гири с ханским эталоном?
branches.narrativeEffect: Sargis's hand pauses over the weight box.

branches.text: What does a caravan fear most on the road?
branches.text_ru: Чего караван боится больше всего в дороге?

nodes.text: Cells for travellers, bread at the gate for nothing. A good caravanserai fills the road, but free bread empties the purse. Still, my grandfather used to say: a stranger at the well is a debt the road lends you, and the road always comes to collect.
nodes.text_ru: Кельи для путников, хлеб у ворот даром. Хороший караван-сарай наполняет дорогу, но даровой хлеб опустошает кошель. И всё же дед мой говорил: чужак у колодца — это долг, который дорога даёт тебе взаймы, и дорога всегда приходит за своим.
nodes.meaning: The guest-house is built for hospitality, not influence: the stranger received is Christ received, and what is given to the poor is lent to the Lord, who repays; it is not lost.

branches.text: Then why should the gate open only for paying guests?
branches.text_ru: Тогда зачем открывать ворота только тем, кто платит?
branches.narrativeEffect: Sargis laughs, then stops counting.

branches.text: Tell me about the road first.
branches.text_ru: Сначала расскажи о дороге.

nodes.text: Not bandits. Overload. A camel carries its load to the pass and kneels there forever. Every year some merchant ties on one more bale, because silver is light in the mind and heavy on the knees.
nodes.text_ru: Не разбойников. Перегруза. Верблюд доносит груз до перевала и там ложится навсегда. Каждый год какой-нибудь купец приторачивает ещё один тюк: серебро лёгкое в уме и тяжёлое для колен.
nodes.meaning: Possessions heaped beyond need crush the one who carries them; life does not consist in the abundance of goods, as the parable of the rich fool teaches.
nodes.source: Lk 12:15-21; St Basil the Great, Homily on the words 'I will pull down my barns'

branches.text: And you, how many bales are enough?
branches.text_ru: А тебе сколько тюков довольно?

branches.text: That is good road-sense.
branches.text_ru: Это добрая дорожная мудрость.

nodes.text: You have a scribe's eye. This stone is the khan's standard, this one is mine, lighter by a grain. Everyone on the road shaves a grain. The road is long and the grain is short.
nodes.text_ru: Глаз у тебя писцовый. Этот камень — ханский эталон, а этот мой, легче на зерно. Все на дороге сбривают зерно. Дорога длинная, а зерно короткое.
nodes.meaning: A false balance is an abomination; small, habitual injustice in measure is still injustice, and 'everyone does it' is no excuse.

branches.text: A grain a day is a bale a year. Let us give your weight its grain back, against the khan's stone.
branches.text_ru: Зерно в день — это тюк в год. Давай вернём твоей гире её зерно — по ханскому камню.
branches.narrativeEffect: The two stones balance on the scale.

branches.text: Shave two grains, and give the profit to the guest-house.
branches.text_ru: Сбрей два зерна, а выгоду отдай странноприимному двору.
branches.narrativeEffect: Sargis grins, and moves your bread onto his scale.

nodes.text: Ha, you learn quickly. But now I will weigh your bread too, deacon. A partner who shaves for me today shaves from me tomorrow.
nodes.text_ru: Ха, быстро учишься. Только теперь я и твой хлеб буду взвешивать, дьякон. Компаньон, что сегодня сбривает для меня, завтра сбреет у меня.
nodes.meaning: Fraud 'for a good cause' corrupts the good it claims to serve and destroys trust; evil is not done that good may come. The cunning path costs trust and opens no deeper teaching.
nodes.source: Rom 3:8

branches.text: You are right. How does a man know the scale has got into him?
branches.text_ru: Ты прав. Как понять, что весы забрались в тебя самого?

nodes.text: Shall I tell you how a merchant learns he is sick? He counts bales at night when there is no caravan to load. He greets a guest by the weight of his saddlebags before he sees his face. He gives, and then remembers the gift for a week. And the bells of his camels ring in his sleep.
nodes.text_ru: Сказать тебе, как купец узнаёт, что болен? Он пересчитывает тюки ночью, когда нечего грузить. Встречает гостя по весу перемётных сум, прежде чем увидит лицо. Даёт — и неделю помнит о данном. А бубенцы его верблюдов звенят у него во сне.
nodes.meaning: Discernment cue for the passion of love of money (avarice): anxious counting without need, measuring persons by their purse, and regret after giving. It is recognised by these signs, not fought with a holy object; its opposite is non-possessiveness and mercy.
nodes.source: Ladder, step 16 (on love of money); St John Cassian, Institutes, Book 7 (on the spirit of covetousness); 1 Tim 6:10

branches.text: What cures the night counting?
branches.text_ru: Чем лечится ночной счёт?

branches.text: I will watch for the night counting in myself.
branches.text_ru: Я буду следить за ночным счётом в себе.

nodes.text: Here is a better trade. Pilgrims pay for wonders. Say an icon wept at your gate: pilgrims bring silver, silver builds cells. Who is harmed?
nodes.text_ru: Вот торг получше. Паломники платят за чудеса. Скажи, что у ваших ворот заплакала икона: паломники принесут серебро, серебро построит кельи. Кому от этого вред?
nodes.meaning: The temptation to invent a miracle for profit: a lie told 'for God' is still a lie, and putting a price on a gift of God is the sin of Simon Magus. Its recognition cue is the price attached to the wonder. The icon remains an object of veneration, never a tool of trade. The honest answer follows the Dialogist's practice of naming the witnesses for each account.
nodes.source: Job 13:7; Acts 8:18-20; St Gregory the Dialogist, Dialogues

branches.text: A wonder with a price on it is a false coin. We will write down only what witnesses saw.
branches.text_ru: Чудо с ценником — фальшивая монета. Запишем только то, что видели свидетели.

branches.text: The truth does not need hired mourners, Sargis.
branches.text_ru: Правде не нужны наёмные плакальщики, Саргис.
branches.narrativeEffect: Sargis lays his palm flat on the scale and is silent a long while.

nodes.text: My mother, whose people came from Ani, lit candles in our church. She said: the hand that holds the scale must also know how to open. In the Gospel there was a tax-gatherer who gave half away and repaid fourfold; he climbed a tree to see and came down lighter. I will set true weights at the guest-house gate. As for the grains I have shaved, that I will carry to a priest of my own Church, not to your ledger.
nodes.text_ru: Мать моя, чей род из Ани, ставила свечи в нашей церкви. Она говорила: рука, что держит весы, должна уметь и раскрыться. В Евангелии был мытарь, что отдал половину и вернул вчетверо: влез на дерево, чтобы увидеть, а слез легче. Я поставлю верные гири у ворот странноприимного двора. А за сбритые зёрна я понесу ответ священнику своей Церкви, а не в твою книгу.
nodes.meaning: The remedy of avarice is mercy and restitution, as with Zacchaeus. Repentance belongs to the Church's own mystery and is heard by a priest, not a deacon; the game does not enact it, so the merchant takes it outward to a priest of his own Church rather than to the deacon's ledger.
nodes.source: Lk 19:1-10; Lk 16:9; Ladder, step 17 (on non-possessiveness)

branches.text: Let the true weights stand at the gate.
branches.text_ru: Пусть верные гири стоят у ворот.
branches.narrativeEffect: The standard weights are placed at the guest-house gate for all to check.

decisions: bias: the matrix calls Sargis 'the tempter by profit', so he should be a villain / counter: TABOO 0.37 p.4 and TABOO 0.4 p.5, a temptation must be recognisable, and a merchant is a person, not a passion / why: his temptations (shaved grain, invented wonder) come from his honest trade idiom, he names the signs of avarice himself, and he turns by his own choice, which keeps him a partner rather than a target.

bias: Sargis is Armenian, so the tree should settle the Chalcedonian question or push him toward Orthodoxy / counter: brief rule 4 forbids pressure or forced conversion; the chorus does not stage dogmatic dispute in a trade scene / why: he speaks of his mother's church with dignity and refers his conscience to a priest of his own Church. Dissent (dogmatist): a later node may need to state plainly that the game's truth is Orthodox; kept open, not decided here.

bias: the deacon could hear Sargis's confession and give absolution in the dialogue / counter: operator's relayed note: the game does not perform the sacraments; confession is often shown on sites, but the game must not simulate it, and the Eucharist likewise is never a mechanic / why: open_hand refers repentance outward ('to a priest, not to your ledger'); no attribute or bonus is tied to any sacrament.

bias: an invented 'weeping icon' legend is harmless marketing for pilgrims / counter: Job 13:7, a lie for God is still a lie; TABOO 0.4 p.1, an icon is never a tool of trade / why: legend_offer is kept as a temptation with a price-tag recognition cue; neither player choice accepts it, and the scene continues with honest witness (mission 22).

bias: the cunning 'shave two grains for a good cause' choice should be rewarded as clever charity / counter: Rom 3:8 and TABOO 0.35 rule 14, Cunning never opens deeper teaching / why: it pays at most cunning +1, costs trust (Sargis weighs your bread), and rejoins the same lesson on avarice.

bias: Zacchaeus should be quoted directly for weight / counter: no invented or forced quotations; Scripture referred to in living speech with source / why: Sargis paraphrases the story in his own road idiom (climbed to see, came down lighter), cited Lk 19:1-10.

bias (catechist): 'let us file the weight true' reads well / counter: Sargis's stone is already a grain light, so filing makes it more false; the scale-idiom must be physically right or it teaches nothing / why: the honest branch now restores the grain against the khan's standard.

bias (catechist): 'your Gospel' marks the deacon's faith as distinct / counter: Armenian Christians confess the same Gospel; the phrase would place Sargis outside Christianity and fail the dignity rule / why: changed to 'in the Gospel'. Dissent (Aristotle-skeptic): the distinction of Churches is real, but it lies in dogma and communion, not in the Gospel book; kept for a later scene.

bias (historian-ethnographer): 'our church at Ani' gives colour / counter: Ani was largely abandoned after the 1319 earthquake, before a 14th-c. merchant's mother could light candles there / why: changed to 'my mother, whose people came from Ani'.

bias (patrologist): the Dialogues of St Gregory are a book of miracles, so citing them against an invented miracle is odd / counter: Gregory names his witnesses for each account, which is exactly the player's answer 'write down only what witnesses saw' / why: kept at work level without a chapter number, with Acts 8:18-20 added for the price on a gift of God.

fixes: false_weights, honest branch: the logic was backwards. Sargis's weight is already a grain light, so filing it would make it lighter and more false. The branch now restores the missing grain to the weight, checked against the khan's standard ('let the scale weigh what it says'). EN and RU changed together.

open_hand: 'in your Gospel' changed to 'in the Gospel'. Sargis is an Armenian Christian and the Gospel is his too. Calling it the deacon's Gospel pushed him outside Christianity, which cuts against the dignity rule (brief rule 4).

open_hand: Ani was mostly abandoned after the 1319 earthquake, so a 14th-century merchant cannot plausibly have a mother lighting candles there. The line now says 'my mother, whose people came from Ani, lit candles in our church'.

guesthouse: Prov 19:17 added to the source. His grandfather's metaphor ('a stranger at the well is a debt the road lends you') now rests on real Scripture ('He that hath pity upon the poor lendeth unto the LORD'), not on a transactional saying. The meaning now names this.

legend_offer: the sources are now Job 13:7 and Acts 8:18-20 (Simon Magus, a price put on a gift of God). The citation of St Gregory the Dialogist's Dialogues stays at work level with no book or chapter, and the meaning now explains it: Gregory names his witnesses for each account (mission 22 links him to this scene).
avarice_cue: Cassian, Institutes, Book 7 (on philargyria) added at work/book level. The meaning now says plainly that the opposite of avarice is non-possessiveness and mercy (Ladder, steps 16-17).

scales_greeting and open_hand: the meaning now states that a deacon does not hear confession. Sargis's jibe about the deacon's 'ledger of sins' is his own misunderstanding, and open_hand corrects it by sending repentance to a priest.

Checked with no change needed: 8 nodes; every nextNodeId resolves or is null; the start node has an unconditioned branch; there are 6 FORM-gated branches (erudition 4, wisdom 5/6/7, charisma 4, faith 5); Cunning is +1 only, carries a cost, and rejoins the shared avarice lesson without opening deeper teaching; all bonuses are integers from 1 to 5; no forbidden words appear in player choices; nothing liturgical is quoted; Ladder step 16 is on love of money and step 17 on non-possessiveness.
dissent: Dogmatist (kept open from the author): a later Sargis scene may need to say plainly that the game's truth is Orthodox, without pressure. This trade scene does not decide it.

Aristotle-skeptic: legend_offer puts a 'weeping icon' in the mouth of a tempter. That is allowed only because no player choice accepts it and the price-tag cue is taught. If a future edit lets the player accept, the node must be removed.

Aristotle-skeptic: the cunning_cost branch pays nothing ({}). This is kept on purpose as the cost, but a validator that requires a bonus of at least 1 on every branch would flag it. The fix is to relax the validator, not to pay the Cunning path.

theology: Mystical theology as synergy: deification is a gift of God's uncreated energy received by one who keeps watch, never an achievement; discernment of false lights (St Gregory Palamas, Triads; St Gregory of Nyssa, Life of Moses; the Ladder, steps 3 and 22).

idiom.worldview: Wax does not light itself: all that a person can do is keep the wick trimmed and stand near the flame, and the light comes as a gift.
idiom.craft: Nun, beekeeper and candle-maker of the monastery; she tends the hives by the wall, renders the comb and pours candles in the dark workshop.
metaphors: wax does not light itself
a candle gives light by being spent
the bees build best in the dark hive
a flame held to the face blinds
the bee takes from the flower and leaves it whole
idiom.silence: She lowers the smoker, works a lump of wax warm in her palms and does not answer; if pressed about visions or rewards, she pinches out the lantern and returns to the hives.

nodes.text: Step slowly. The hive hears a hurried heart before it hears your feet. I am rendering comb today: the honey goes to the refectory, the wax goes to the candles. What have you come for?
nodes.text_ru: Ступай тише. Улей слышит торопливое сердце раньше, чем шаги. Я сегодня перетапливаю соты: мёд пойдёт в трапезную, воск в свечи. С чем ты ко мне?
nodes.meaning: The contemplative way begins with quieting the heart; haste is the first obstacle. A first meeting is open to anyone.
nodes.source: The Ladder of Divine Ascent, step 27 (on stillness); Psalm 46:10 (45:11 LXX)

branches.text: What becomes of the wax?
branches.text_ru: Что становится с воском?
branches.narrativeEffect: She hands you the strainer. The wax is warm and smells of summer.

branches.text: Is there a faster way to the light?
branches.text_ru: Есть ли более быстрый путь к свету?
branches.narrativeEffect: She smiles and puts one more frame back into the hive, unhurried.

branches.text: I saw a bright light in my sleep. Is it a sign?
branches.text_ru: Мне во сне явился яркий свет. Это знак?

branches.text: How does dark wax become light?
branches.text_ru: Как тёмный воск становится светом?
branches.narrativeEffect: She sets the strainer down. For a while she says nothing at all.

nodes.text: Wax does not light itself. I can pour the best candle in the valley, straight, clean, the wick centred, and it stays dark on the shelf until someone brings it a flame. And once it is lit, it gives light by being spent. That is all the candle knows.
nodes.text_ru: Воск сам не загорается. Я могу отлить лучшую свечу в долине, ровную, чистую, фитиль по центру, и она будет стоять тёмной на полке, пока кто-нибудь не поднесёт огонь. А зажжённая, она светит, сгорая. Больше свеча ничего не знает.
nodes.meaning: Human effort prepares, but illumination and deification are God's gift, not the product of technique; the one who receives it gives himself away in love. This is synergy: the will cooperates, God gives.
nodes.source: Ephesians 2:8-10; Extended Christian Catechism of St Philaret

branches.text: Then what is the candle-maker's part?
branches.text_ru: Тогда в чём дело свечника?

branches.text: And the flame, where does it come from?
branches.text_ru: А огонь откуда берётся?

branches.text: And when a candle burns well, whose is the credit?
branches.text_ru: А когда свеча горит хорошо, чья это заслуга?

nodes.text: No bee builds a comb in one flight. Cell by cell, wax from its own body, all summer long, and in autumn there is enough for the winter. Those who wanted the honey by midsummer took the frames too early, and the hive died in the frost. The fruit comes in patience.
nodes.text_ru: Ни одна пчела не строит сот за один вылет. Ячейка за ячейкой, воском из собственного тела, всё лето, и к осени хватает на зиму. Кто хотел мёда к середине лета, вынимал рамки раньше срока, и улей погибал в мороз. Плод приходит в терпении.
nodes.meaning: There is no shortcut in the spiritual life; the ascent is gradual, and haste for experiences destroys what patience would have built.
nodes.source: Luke 8:15; The Ladder of Divine Ascent, step 1 (on renunciation and beginning)

branches.text: So the wax matters more than the hurry.
branches.text_ru: Значит, воск важнее спешки.

nodes.text: The bee visits every flower and harms none; it takes only what makes honey and leaves the rest. The great teacher of Caesarea told young men to read that way, like bees, not like those who pick the whole blossom. So gather from every teacher you meet, and let what does not feed the hive stay in the field.
nodes.text_ru: Пчела садится на каждый цветок и ни одному не вредит; берёт лишь то, из чего будет мёд, остальное оставляет. Великий учитель Кесарии советовал юношам читать именно так, по-пчелиному, а не обрывать цветок целиком. Так и ты собирай у каждого наставника, а что не кормит улей, пусть остаётся в поле.
nodes.meaning: The contemplative learns with discernment: receiving what is true and useful, leaving aside the rest, without contempt for the source. Knowledge serves the soul's growth, not curiosity.
nodes.source: St Basil the Great, Address to Young Men on the Right Use of Greek Literature, chapter 4

branches.text: And where does the bee do its real work?
branches.text_ru: А где пчела делает главную работу?

branches.text: I will gather slowly, flower by flower.
branches.text_ru: Буду собирать медленно, цветок за цветком.

nodes.text: Listen to how the light spoke to you. Did it say you were chosen, more than the brothers? Did it hurry you? Do you burn to tell someone about it? A flame held right up to the face does not light the road, it blinds. The light that flatters, hurries and wants to be seen is not from the hive; it is the old smoke of vainglory. The true one leaves you quieter and smaller, and you forget to tell.
nodes.text_ru: Прислушайся, как этот свет говорил с тобой. Сказал ли, что ты избран больше братии? Торопил ли? Хочется ли тебе поскорее кому-то рассказать? Огонь, поднесённый к самому лицу, не освещает дорогу, а слепит. Свет, который льстит, торопит и хочет, чтобы его увидели, не из улья: это старый дым тщеславия. Истинный оставляет тебя тише и меньше, и рассказать ты забываешь.
nodes.meaning: Discernment cue for vainglory and its fruit, spiritual delusion (prelest): an experience that flatters, singles one out above others, breeds haste and the desire to be seen is to be distrusted; the enemy can disguise himself as an angel of light. One does not chase visions but brings them to one's elder.
nodes.source: 2 Corinthians 11:14; The Ladder of Divine Ascent, step 3 (on dreams) and step 22 (on vainglory)

branches.text: Then I will tell it only to my elder, and not seek it again.
branches.text_ru: Тогда расскажу только старцу и не стану искать этого снова.
branches.narrativeEffect: She lets the smoker drift over the hive; the bees settle.

branches.text: But surely such a light means I am close.
branches.text_ru: Но ведь такой свет значит, что я уже близко.
branches.narrativeEffect: Sister Catherine does not argue. She lifts the lid of a hive that was opened too early; it is empty.

nodes.text: After a good day in the workshop there is a voice that comes softly: "See what a straight candle you poured. This was your own doing." It sounds like honest pleasure in work, so no one guards against it. But it speaks as if the wax had lit itself. The wax came from the bees, the flame from another hand, and the hands themselves were given. When I hear that voice I ask the candle: what have you that you did not receive? It never has an answer.
nodes.text_ru: После удачного дня в мастерской приходит тихий голос: «Смотри, какую ровную свечу ты отлила. Это твоё собственное дело». Он звучит как честная радость от работы, поэтому его никто не стережётся. Но говорит он так, будто воск загорелся сам. Воск дали пчёлы, огонь поднесла чужая рука, да и сами руки даны. Когда я слышу этот голос, я спрашиваю свечу: что у тебя есть, чего бы ты не получила? Ответа у неё не бывает.
nodes.meaning: Discernment cue for pride, the eighth passion: the thought that ascribes one's good deeds and progress to oneself ("this was your own doing"). St John Climacus calls pride a denial of God and the ascription of one's achievements to oneself; the remedy is humility, remembering that every good is received. The mentor teaches the sign, not a weapon: the passion is cut by recognising it and giving thanks.
nodes.source: The Ladder of Divine Ascent, step 23 (on pride); 1 Corinthians 4:7

branches.text: Then I will thank the hand that brought the flame.
branches.text_ru: Тогда я поблагодарю руку, что поднесла огонь.
branches.narrativeEffect: She nods once and trims a wick with her thumbnail.

branches.text: But I did pour it well.
branches.text_ru: Но ведь я и правда хорошо её отлил.
branches.narrativeEffect: Sister Catherine sets the candle on the shelf. In the dark it is only wax.

nodes.text: The bees build their best comb in the dark; open the hive at noon and they stop working. The one who wrote the life of Moses said the lawgiver first saw God in light, in the burning bush, then in the cloud, and last in the darkness on the mountain, where seeing stops. The higher he went, the less his eyes could hold. When my lantern goes out in the workshop, my hands still know the mould.
nodes.text_ru: Лучшие соты пчёлы строят в темноте; открой улей в полдень, и работа встанет. Тот, кто написал житие Моисея, говорил: сначала законодатель увидел Бога в свете, в горящей купине, потом в облаке, а под конец во мраке на горе, где кончается зрение. Чем выше он шёл, тем меньше вмещали глаза. Когда в мастерской гаснет мой фонарь, руки всё равно знают форму.
nodes.meaning: God surpasses all concepts; the higher ascent is into the 'divine darkness' where the mind ceases to grasp and simply abides in faith. Stillness is not emptiness but the place of meeting.
nodes.source: Exodus 3:2 and 20:21; St Gregory of Nyssa, The Life of Moses, book II; Dionysius the Areopagite, The Mystical Theology, chapter 1

branches.text: Then I will not ask for more light than I can bear.
branches.text_ru: Тогда не стану просить больше света, чем могу вынести.

branches.text: And if the flame does come into the dark?
branches.text_ru: А если огонь всё-таки придёт в темноту?

nodes.text: I cannot give you the flame. No one lights himself; he is lit. The teacher of Thessalonica defended the monks who said the light they saw was not made, not the sun's and not their own, but God Himself giving Himself. He taught that it is shown to hearts made clean, and always as a gift. So I keep the wick trimmed; I do not light it. Remember the wise virgins with their lamps: they did not make the bridegroom come. They were ready when He came.
nodes.text_ru: Огня я тебе дать не могу. Никто не зажигается сам: его зажигают. Фессалоникийский учитель защищал монахов, говоривших, что свет, который они видели, не сотворён, не от солнца и не от них самих, а Сам Бог, подающий Себя. Он учил, что этот свет открывается очищенному сердцу, и всегда как дар. Вот я и держу фитиль подрезанным, а зажигать его не мне. Вспомни мудрых дев со светильниками: не они заставили жениха прийти. Они были готовы, когда он пришёл.
nodes.meaning: The uncreated light is God's own energy, given freely to the pure in heart; deification is gift, not wage. Human watchfulness and stillness are necessary but never sufficient: this is why the mystical gate is a gift that requires an act of humility and cannot be bought with counted minutes.
nodes.source: St Gregory Palamas, Triads in Defence of the Holy Hesychasts (on the divine light); Matthew 5:8; Matthew 25:1-13

branches.text: I will keep the wick trimmed and wait.
branches.text_ru: Буду держать фитиль подрезанным и ждать.
branches.narrativeEffect: She takes a new, unlit candle from the shelf and turns it slowly in her hands.

branches.text: But my minutes of stillness have earned it, surely.
branches.text_ru: Но ведь мои минуты тишины уже это заработали.
branches.narrativeEffect: Sister Catherine pinches out her lantern. In the dark she says only: 'Listen to how that sounded.'

nodes.text: (She puts the unlit candle into your hands, closes your fingers over it, and goes back to the hives without a word. Behind the wall the lake is so still that you can hear the reeds.)
nodes.text_ru: (Она вкладывает тебе в руки незажжённую свечу, сжимает твои пальцы вокруг неё и молча возвращается к ульям. За стеной озеро так тихо, что слышно тростник.)
nodes.meaning: The mentor's final answer is silence: the teaching of the mystical way cannot be handed over as a formula. The unlit candle signifies readiness and expectation; the light is God's to give, in His time.
nodes.source: 1 Kings 19:11-12 (3 Kingdoms LXX); The Ladder of Divine Ascent, step 27 (on stillness)

branches.text: Stand still and listen to the reeds.
branches.text_ru: Постоять и послушать тростник.
branches.narrativeEffect: The HUD fades. Room tone and breathing remain; no counter appears.

decisions: bias: Sister Catherine is Catherine of Alexandria and should argue with philosophers / counter: the roster portrait (npc-sister-catherine.svg) shows a nun in an apostolnik under descending light, the mentor of the mystical gate, while Catherine of Alexandria is a separate saint row in NPC_DIALOGUE_SYSTEM.md section 3 / why: she is drawn as a living nun of the monastery, not a saint, so her own lines are voice 'own' and only the nodes retelling Basil, Gregory of Nyssa and Palamas are 'paraphrase'. Dissent kept: the playwright proposed merging her with the saint; the patrologist refused, since that would put invented speech in a saint's mouth.

bias: the old tree told the player 'You are ready for theosis' at wisdom 8 and faith 8 / counter: the dogmatist and TABOO 0.35 rule 14 say deification is synergy and gift, never a threshold reward / why: the high-FORM branch now leads to 'wick_waits', where she says she cannot give the flame, and the 'I earned it' branch is sent back to the false-light cue with no bonus.

bias: a mystic should speak about light directly, with a glowing effect / counter: TABOO 0.2 rule 2 and TABOO 0.25 forbid the nimbus and rings, and TABOO 0.4 forbids the sacred as a visual power-up / why: light is spoken of through wax, wick and lantern (1900-2500 K human work); at the end the HUD fades to room tone and breathing, and no counter or reward appears.

bias: the passion node should frighten the player with a demon / counter: TABOO 0.2 rule 8 requires prelest to be recognisable, not a monster / why: the false-light node gives concrete cues (flattery, being singled out, haste, the urge to tell) with Ladder steps 3 and 22 and 2 Cor 11:14 as sources. It is vainglory, one of the eight.

bias: minutes of stillness should give faith points / counter: TABOO 0.35 rule 16 says stillness is never paid in attributes / why: bonuses in 'wick_waits' reward the understanding of gift and waiting; the gate itself keeps its separate rite counter and gift flag.

bias: the shortcut question is Cunning and should be gated by cunning / counter: Cunning never opens a deeper teaching / why: 'Is there a faster way' is open to all, gives no bonus, and leads to the patience node; Cunning appears in no condition and no bonus in this tree. Skeptic's objection kept: a zero-bonus branch may feel like a trap; answered: it leads to a real teaching and back to the main path.

bias: cite exact chapters for Palamas and Nyssa / counter: the no-fabrication rule / why: only the work and book are given (Triads; Life of Moses book II), where the chapter numbering was not verified; exact verses are given only for Scripture and for Basil's Address chapter 4.

bias (dogmatist): the Palamas paraphrase may add a vivid line of our own, 'not to those who reach for it' / counter: TABOO 0.35 rule 18 and 0.37 forbid putting invented teaching in a saint's mouth / why: the saint's part is limited to what the Triads actually defend (the light is uncreated, shown to the pure in heart, a gift; Mt 5:8), and the wick image is moved into Catherine's own voice ('So I keep the wick trimmed'). The source is downgraded from 'Triads III' to the work, because the exact treatise was not verified.

bias (dogmatist): 'God met Moses not in the bright plain but in the cloud' is close enough / counter: Life of Moses II presents three stages, light at the bush, then cloud, then darkness, and dropping the first stage misstates Nyssa / why: the paraphrase now keeps all three stages, and Exodus 3:2 is added as a source.

bias: the closing 'listen to the reeds' may keep +1 wisdom for the insight / counter: the branch text is the act of standing still itself, and TABOO 0.35 rule 16 does not pay stillness / why (dogmatist): the bonus is removed; the meeting is still recorded, and understanding was already rewarded in wick_waits. Author's view kept as dissent: the catechist wanted +1 as a mark of attention.

bias: Russian choice texts may use the masculine 'пришёл' / counter: players of both sexes meet the mentor who opens the gate / why: the greeting is made gender-neutral ('С чем ты ко мне?'); the English is unchanged.

fixes: wick_waits: the Palamas paraphrase said the light comes 'not to those who reach for it'. That is not his wording or a close retelling of him. It now follows the Triads' own claim that the light is shown to the pure in heart as a gift (Mt 5:8). The wick image is now clearly Catherine's own line. Source changed to 'Triads (on the divine light)' plus Matthew 5:8 and 25:1-13, because 'Triads III' was not verified as the place for this claim.
wick_waits: 'the wise girls' changed to 'the wise virgins' (Mt 25). The Russian text already had 'мудрые девы'.

dark_hive: the Nyssa paraphrase said Moses met God 'not in the bright plain'. Life of Moses II describes three steps: light at the bush, then the cloud, then darkness. The text now follows that order.

quiet_candle: the final 'Stand still and listen to the reeds' branch gave +1 wisdom. It now gives {}, because TABOO 0.35 rule 16 says stillness is never paid in attributes. The earlier branches already pay for the understanding.
greeting text_ru: the masculine 'С чем пришёл?' is now the gender-neutral 'С чем ты ко мне?', so the first meeting reads right for any player.
wax_and_flame source: removed the vague parenthetical after St Philaret's Catechism. It now cites the work only.
dissent: Skeptic: wick_waits can be reached three ways with inconsistent thresholds: greeting at wisdom 8 + faith 8, wax_and_flame at faith 6, dark_hive at wisdom 12. The wisdom-12 route is almost never the one a player uses. Kept, because the dialogue route is not the gate. The mystical gate is still checked separately in ludus-actions.js (wisdom 12, the mentor sister_catherine, 30 minutes of stillness, gift flag). Game designer to review.
Skeptic: a branch with an empty bonus may read to players as a trap. The author's answer is kept: each such branch leads to a real teaching.

theology: Watchfulness without wrath. The soldier's duty is not condemned (Lk 3:14; Mt 8:5-13), but the clergy do not take the sword (Mt 26:52; Is 2:4; Apostolic Canon 83), and anger is recognised before it strikes (Ladder, steps 8-9). The guard is a non-Orthodox man of the Yasa, drawn with dignity as a partner in dialogue.

idiom.worldview: The world holds together by the oath, the watch and the Yasa; a gate without a man is an invitation.
idiom.craft: Night-guard of the khan's camp (kesikten): keeping the gate, the watch-fire and the bow through the hours of dark.
metaphors: the hand leaves before the arrow does
the lowest fire is the hour before dawn
a bolting horse is not courage
a gate without a man is an invitation
the lead wolf falls and the pack scatters
idiom.silence: He turns his back to the fire and watches the dark; he answers by laying on another log, not by a word.

nodes.text: The fire at the gate burns all night. I count who comes by its light, not by the dark behind them. Name your road, deacon.
nodes.text_ru: Костёр у ворот горит всю ночь. Я считаю входящих по его свету, а не по тьме за их спиной. Назови свою дорогу, дьякон.
nodes.meaning: Vigilance is a real virtue of service: a man must see what approaches before he judges it. The meeting opens without any test.

branches.text: I come in peace, and I carry no weapon.
branches.text_ru: Я пришёл с миром и без оружия.
branches.narrativeEffect: The guard looks at the empty hands a long time.

branches.text: Among my people a song says the watchman keeps awake in vain unless the Lord keeps the city. Have you heard it?
branches.text_ru: У моего народа есть песнь: напрасно не спит сторож, если город не хранит Господь. Ты слышал её?
branches.narrativeEffect: The guard repeats the line under his breath, testing it like a bowstring.

branches.text: Your eyes are tired. What do you watch for?
branches.text_ru: У тебя усталые глаза. Чего ты ждёшь в темноте?

nodes.text: A man with no blade at night is either a fool, or a man who trusts another's bowstring. Which are you?
nodes.text_ru: Человек без клинка ночью — либо глупец, либо тот, кто верит чужой тетиве. Кто из них ты?
nodes.meaning: The soldier reads defencelessness as folly or dependence. The deacon's refusal of the sword is not weakness: it is obedience to Christ's word to Peter and to the canon that forbids clergy to bear arms.
nodes.source: Mt 26:52; Apostolic Canon 83

branches.text: I trust the word that whoever takes up the sword falls by it.
branches.text_ru: Я верю слову: кто поднимает меч, от меча и падёт.

branches.text: Let us speak of your watch instead.
branches.text_ru: Лучше расскажи о своей страже.

nodes.text: In vain? Then why do I stand here? I will tell you why: because a gate without a man is an invitation. Perhaps your song means the watchman should not think the city lives by his eyes alone.
nodes.text_ru: Напрасно? Зачем же я тогда стою? Скажу зачем: ворота без человека — приглашение. Может, твоя песнь о том, что страж не должен думать, будто город живёт одними его глазами.
nodes.meaning: The psalm does not abolish the watch; it removes the watchman's pride. Human labour is real, but the keeping of the city belongs to God.
nodes.source: Ps 126:1 (LXX; Ps 127:1 Hebrew)

branches.text: Yes: keep the gate, but do not carry the whole night on your shoulders.
branches.text_ru: Да: стереги ворота, но не неси всю ночь на своих плечах.

nodes.text: I watch for the hour before dawn. Then the fire is lowest, and a man's heart is lowest with it. The watchman who dozes in that hour loses all the night had kept for him.
nodes.text_ru: Я жду часа перед рассветом. Тогда огонь ниже всего, и сердце человека вместе с ним. Страж, задремавший в этот час, теряет всё, что ночь ему сберегла.
nodes.meaning: The hour of lowest strength is the hour of despondency. Watchfulness (nepsis) is most needed when the heart is weakest, and the soul waits for the morning as watchmen do.
nodes.source: Ps 129:6 (LXX; Ps 130:6 Hebrew); Ladder, step 13 (on despondency)

branches.text: And tonight? Something moves on the road.
branches.text_ru: А сегодня? На дороге что-то движется.
branches.narrativeEffect: Torches appear on the road below the wall.

nodes.text: Torches under the wall. They shout that your mixed house must go. Say one word and my arrows will thin them. When the lead wolf falls, the pack scatters.
nodes.text_ru: Факелы под стеной. Кричат, что ваш смешанный двор должен уйти. Скажи одно слово — и мои стрелы их проредят. Падёт вожак — стая разбежится.
nodes.meaning: This is the temptation of force presented as protection. The men under the wall are people driven by fear and grievance, not wolves. Christ commands love of enemies, and evil is overcome with good: the Church answers a crowd with meekness and truth, not with arrows.

branches.text: Hold your bow. Let me go out to them with open hands.
branches.text_ru: Опусти лук. Дай мне выйти к ним с открытыми руками.
branches.narrativeEffect: The guard lowers the bow but keeps the arrow on the string.

branches.text: They are not wolves; they are afraid. Let me speak to them from the gate.
branches.text_ru: Это не волки, это испуганные люди. Дай мне сказать им слово от ворот.
branches.narrativeEffect: The shouting falters when a voice answers without a threat.

branches.text: Close the gate and keep the fire burning.
branches.text_ru: Закрой ворота и не дай огню погаснуть.

branches.text: Shoot over their heads, just to frighten them.
branches.text_ru: Пусти стрелы над головами — только припугнуть.
branches.narrativeEffect: The crowd scatters, and then returns louder.

nodes.text: Arrows over heads teach a crowd only where to aim next time. The trick buys one night and sells the next ten.
nodes.text_ru: Стрела над головой учит толпу лишь одному — куда целиться в следующий раз. Хитрость покупает одну ночь и продаёт следующие десять.
nodes.meaning: A ruse of fear does not quench anger; it feeds it. Cunning wins an hour and costs the peace, while a soft answer turns wrath away.
nodes.source: Prov 15:1

branches.text: Then how does a man stop the anger itself?
branches.text_ru: Как же тогда остановить сам гнев?

nodes.text: Old riders say: before the arrow leaves, the hand has already left. When the jaw sets hard, when you tell the insult over again at the fire, when you want the gate opened only to strike, that heat is not courage. It is the horse bolting with you on its back.
nodes.text_ru: Старые всадники говорят: прежде стрелы уходит рука. Когда челюсть сжата, когда у костра снова пересказываешь обиду, когда хочешь открыть ворота только чтобы ударить, — этот жар не храбрость. Это конь понёс, а ты у него на спине.
nodes.meaning: This is the discernment cue for the passion of anger. Bodily heat, rumination on the offence (remembrance of wrongs) and the haste to strike come before the deed, and they can be recognised in time. Anger is overcome by meekness and stillness, not by a weapon, holy or otherwise.
nodes.source: Ladder, step 8 (on freedom from anger and meekness) and step 9 (on remembrance of wrongs); Evagrius, Praktikos (chapters on anger); Apophthegmata Patrum, alphabetical collection, Abba Moses

branches.text: How does your horse stop, then?
branches.text_ru: А как останавливают такого коня?

branches.text: I will remember the set jaw.
branches.text_ru: Я запомню сжатую челюсть.

nodes.text: You stop it by the rein, not by the whip. A priest of yours once told me that your desert preacher said to soldiers: do not extort, do not accuse falsely, be content with your pay. He did not tell them to break the bow. So I keep my gate. And you keep your word, whatever it is you keep at night.
nodes.text_ru: Останавливают поводом, а не плетью. Ваш священник как-то сказал мне: ваш пустынный проповедник велел воинам — никого не обижайте, не клевещите, довольствуйтесь жалованьем. Ломать лук он не велел. Вот я и стерегу ворота. А ты храни своё слово, что бы ты там ни хранил по ночам.
nodes.meaning: Scripture does not condemn the soldier's service as such (the Baptist's counsel, the centurion's faith), but it forbids violence and extortion. The guard keeps his duty and the Church keeps its refusal of the sword; neither is forced onto the other's path.

branches.text: Keep the gate honestly; I will keep watch in my own way.
branches.text_ru: Стереги ворота честно, а я буду бодрствовать по-своему.
branches.narrativeEffect: The guard adds a log to the fire without a word.

decisions: bias: the guard is a Mongol soldier, so he should be an enemy or a zealot to convert / counter: TABOO 0.37 p.4 requires non-Orthodox characters as dignified partners; Lk 3:14 and the centurion (Mt 8) show Scripture addressing soldiers without contempt / why: he keeps his duty and his Yasa idiom; the Orthodox line is carried by the deacon's choices, with no pressure or mockery.

bias: the guard's world should include the Eternal Blue Sky as a colour of faith / counter: TABOO 0.4 p.6 forbids showing paganism as true or rewarded / why: his worldview is expressed through oath, watch and Yasa only; no Tengri invocation is voiced, so nothing pagan is validated. Dissent (historian-ethnographer): a kesikten without any sky-oath is thinner historically; kept as an open note for a later node, never rewarded.

bias (patrologist, added): give the guard a Tengrist or Islamic voice for colour / counter (historian): the Chagatai khans in Semirechye had become Muslim by the 1350s, so a Tengrist kesikten is uncertain and an Islamic formula risks caricature / why: his faith stays unvoiced; he is a man of the oath, and that keeps his dignity without deciding a doubtful fact.

bias: the cunning 'arrows over heads' option is harmless and should pay well / counter: TABOO 0.35 rule 14 and the brief say Cunning never opens deeper teaching / why: it pays at most cunning +1, leads to the cost node (Prov 15:1) and rejoins the same lesson; the crowd returns louder.
