The follow-up question pays wisdom +1 for understanding, not for the trick.

bias: anger should be defeated by a blessed object or a prayer used as a shield / counter: TABOO 0.2 p.3-4, prayer is not a spell / why: the anger node gives only a discernment cue (jaw, rumination, haste) from Ladder steps 8-9, Evagrius and the tradition of Abba Moses; no holy object is used against the passion.

bias: the watchman psalm should be quoted in full as a power line / counter: no liturgical text is quoted and Church Slavonic is not altered / why: the player paraphrases the psalm in plain Russian (the half-Slavonic 'всуе' is removed) and it is cited as Ps 126:1 LXX; the guard answers in his own idiom.

bias (patrologist, added): the deacon's empty hands are a private pious choice / counter: Apostolic Canon 83 forbids clergy to take up military service, and matrix storyline 69 uses the same canon / why: the source is added to why_no_blade, so the refusal rests on the Church's rule and not on sentiment; the canon number follows the standard Pedalion numbering.

bias (skeptic): the guard's 'lead wolf' metaphor dehumanises the crowd and should be cut / counter: the temptation must be felt in his own idiom to be discerned / why: kept, but the meaning names the crowd as people (matrix 98: 'the leader is a man, not a demon'), and a Charisma >= 7 branch lets the deacon say so, matching the matrix's FORM check.

bias: a mentor-style gate should be tied to this meeting / counter: the guard is not in GATES / why: the start node still has an unconditioned branch, so any guest is heard; bonuses are small integers for understanding, not for any rite.

fixes: gate_watch: source changed from Ps 126:1 to Ezek 33:2-6; Mk 13:37. The psalm is only raised later by the player, and the meaning here is the duty of the watchman.

gate_watch/watchman_psalm: the player's line and the guard's echo used the Church Slavonic 'всуе' inside Russian, a half-Slavonic quotation. It is now a plain Russian paraphrase ('напрасно не спит сторож'), and the guard answers 'Напрасно?'. No Slavonic is altered.

why_no_blade: added Apostolic Canon 83 (clergy may not take up military service), which fits the deacon's refusal and matches storyline matrix line 1610. The player's Mt 26:52 line is now a paraphrase, not the verbatim Synodal wording.

force_offer: added a Charisma >= 7 branch (speaking to the frightened crowd), per matrix storyline 98, which pairs Charisma >= 7 with Constitution >= 6. The meaning now says that the crowd are people and not wolves, because the leader of the zealots is 'a man, not a demon'. Added Rom 12:21.

anger_cue: the cue of retelling the insult is remembrance of wrongs, so Ladder step 9 is added beside step 8. Added Evagrius, Praktikos (on anger) by work title only. Abba Moses is kept by name without a saying number, because the number is uncertain.

soldier_wage: the English paraphrase of Lk 3:14 was loose ('do not rob, do not lie'). It is corrected to 'do not extort, do not accuse falsely, be content with your pay' to match the Russian and the Gospel.

cunning_cost: the empty attributeBonuses on the player's repentant question is now wisdom +1, a reward for understanding. The cunning choice itself still pays only cunning +1, at the cost of the crowd returning.

decisions: added the historian's note that the Chagatai khans had become Muslim by the 1350s. The guard's faith therefore stays unvoiced: he is neither a Tengrist nor a Muslim caricature, only a man of the oath and the Yasa.
dissent: Historian-ethnographer: a kesikten with no sky-oath or no Islamic formula at all is historically thin. Kept as an open note. If voiced later, it must be dignified and never rewarded or shown as true.

Aristotle-skeptic: the guard's line 'your desert preacher said...' puts a Gospel paraphrase in a non-Orthodox mouth. Accepted because he explicitly reports hearsay from a priest, and the words are Lk 3:14 in paraphrase, not a liturgical text.
Aristotle-skeptic: the guard's 'lead wolf' metaphor dehumanises the crowd. Kept as his idiom and as the temptation itself. The meaning and the player's Charisma branch correct it inside the tree.

theology: Ascetic constancy turned into service: the pillar as a place of prayer from which Symeon counselled crowds, reconciled quarrels, and urged justice against usury and oaths; obedience and humility as the test of every ascetic feat; discernment of vainglory. Commemorated September 1.

idiom.worldview: Height is for hearing: the farther a man stands from the market, the closer he comes to those who climb to his foot.
idiom.craft: Pillar-stander of the Syrian hills near Antioch: he stands between heaven and earth through sun and frost, lets down a basket on a rope, and speaks to the crowd below.
metaphors: The pillar is a lampstand, not a throne.
The ladder goes both ways.
A chain of iron is weaker than a chain of will.
The wind tests the root, not the top.
What goes up in the basket comes down as counsel.
idiom.silence: At the hours of prayer he turns east and the crowd's questions wait below; when he refuses he bows, and the bow is his whole answer.

nodes.text: You shout up at me like the herders from the hills. Good, the wind carries it. Stand where you are, and I will stand where I am. Between us is a ladder, and it goes both ways.
nodes.text_ru: Ты кричишь мне снизу, как пастухи с холмов. Хорошо, ветер доносит. Стой, где стоишь, а я постою, где стою. Между нами лестница, и она ведёт в обе стороны.
nodes.meaning: Symeon's life on the pillar was not flight from people but a form of service: crowds came to its foot and he taught and reconciled them.
nodes.source: Theodoret of Cyrrhus, Religious History (Historia Religiosa), ch. 26; Synaxarion, September 1.

branches.text: Why stand so high, if you want to hear people?
branches.text_ru: Зачем стоять так высоко, если хочешь слышать людей?
branches.narrativeEffect: The basket comes down on its rope, empty, as a greeting.

branches.text: How does a body bear the frost and the noon?
branches.text_ru: Как тело выносит мороз и полдень?

branches.text: And if your elders told you to come down?
branches.text_ru: А если бы старшие велели тебе спуститься?

branches.text: They say a man on a pillar sees the future. What is in it for me?
branches.text_ru: Говорят, человек на столпе видит будущее. Что мне с этого?
branches.narrativeEffect: Cost: he turns east and bows; the teaching on obedience stays closed on this path.

nodes.text: A lamp is not lit to be admired; it is set on a stand so the house can see. I did not climb to be seen. The crowd tore at my cloak for threads, and I could not pray. Up here I hear them better: the merchant with false weights, the man whose debt eats his family, two villages quarrelling over one well.
nodes.text_ru: Светильник зажигают не для любования, а ставят на подсвечник, чтобы видел весь дом. Я поднялся не для того, чтобы на меня смотрели. Толпа рвала мой плащ на нитки, и я не мог молиться. Отсюда я слышу их лучше: купца с неверными гирями, человека, чей долг съедает семью, два села, что спорят из-за одного колодца.
nodes.meaning: Withdrawal for prayer became service. According to Theodoret the pillar arose from the pressure of the crowds, and his teaching from it concerned justice and reconciliation.
nodes.source: Matthew 5:15; Theodoret of Cyrrhus, Religious History, ch. 26.

branches.text: Teach me to settle two villages over one well.
branches.text_ru: Научи меня мирить два села у одного колодца.

branches.text: And the one who climbs only to be seen?
branches.text_ru: А тот, кто поднимается, только чтобы его видели?

nodes.text: I told the crowd below what I tell you. Let the lender take back his coin without the interest that eats the house. Leave off the oath you want to swear over the well: let your yes stay yes. And pay the reaper before the sun goes down, as the Law says. The rain was sent from above on both villages alike; the well it fills belongs to neither one alone.
nodes.text_ru: Я говорил толпе внизу то же, что скажу тебе. Пусть заимодавец возьмёт своё без роста, что съедает дом. Оставь клятву, которой хочешь клясться над колодцем: пусть твоё «да» остаётся «да». И плати жнецу до захода солнца, как велит Закон. Дождь послан свыше на оба села одинаково; колодец, который он наполняет, не принадлежит ни одному из них одному.
nodes.meaning: Symeon exhorted the crowds to renounce usury and oaths and to be reconciled; justice between neighbours is the fruit of prayer, not of power. God's gifts are given to all alike, so neither side owns them against the other.
nodes.source: Theodoret of Cyrrhus, Religious History, ch. 26; Syriac Life of Symeon the Stylite (on usury); Matthew 5:37; James 5:12; Deuteronomy 24:15; Matthew 5:45.

branches.text: Then I will carry the jar for the other village too.
branches.text_ru: Тогда я понесу кувшин и для другого села.
branches.narrativeEffect: The basket goes up with nothing in it and comes down with a crust of bread for the road.

branches.text: And if they do not listen?
branches.text_ru: А если они не послушают?
branches.narrativeEffect: He bows. The wind answers for him: it keeps blowing, and the pillar keeps standing.

nodes.text: At first I chained my foot to the rock so as not to wander from my place. Meletius, a wise man who served the bishop among the villages, came and said the chain was needless: reason and will can hold a body, and iron adds nothing to them. I let the smith cut it. Frost and noon a body learns slowly, a little each year, the way a trunk learns the wind. The wind tests the root, not the top.
nodes.text_ru: Сначала я приковал ногу к скале, чтобы не уйти со своего места. Пришёл Мелетий, мудрый муж, что служил епископу по сёлам, и сказал, что цепь не нужна: тело могут удержать разум и воля, а железо к ним ничего не прибавляет. Я позволил кузнецу её снять. Мороз и полдень тело учит медленно, понемногу каждый год, как ствол учится ветру. Ветер испытывает корень, а не верхушку.
nodes.meaning: Constancy (Constitution) grows from a reasoned will, not from external force; ascetic endurance is learned with measure and is not a feat for display.
nodes.source: Theodoret of Cyrrhus, Religious History, ch. 26 (Meletius and the chain).

branches.text: Then my endurance should be a chain of will, not of iron.
branches.text_ru: Значит, моя стойкость — цепь воли, а не железа.
branches.narrativeEffect: He bows once, slowly, as a trunk bows in the wind.

branches.text: And when the body says: enough?
branches.text_ru: А когда тело говорит: хватит?

nodes.text: They did send word. The fathers of the desert thought my pillar a new and proud thing and told me to come down. I put my foot on the ladder at once. Then they told me to stay: since I obeyed, they saw the work was not my own will. The pillar was never mine. Had I clung to it, it would have been a pedestal.
nodes.text_ru: Они и правда послали сказать. Отцы пустыни сочли мой столп новшеством и гордостью и велели спуститься. Я тут же поставил ногу на лестницу. Тогда мне велели остаться: раз я послушался, они увидели, что это дело не моей воли. Столп никогда не был моим. Если бы я в него вцепился, он стал бы пьедесталом.
nodes.meaning: Humility and obedience are the test of any ascetic feat; a work held against the Church's voice becomes self-will.
nodes.source: Evagrius Scholasticus, Ecclesiastical History, Book I (account of Symeon the Stylite); Menologion of St Dimitry of Rostov, 1 September (Life of St Symeon the Stylite).

branches.text: So the proof of a height is being ready to come down.
branches.text_ru: Значит, высоту проверяет готовность спуститься.
branches.narrativeEffect: He lays his hand on the top rung of the ladder and leaves it there.

branches.text: How do I know when I am clinging?
branches.text_ru: Как понять, что я вцепился?

nodes.text: Listen to the crowd below and you will hear a second voice among them that sounds like your own: look how long he stands. Know it by its marks. It grows louder when people watch and falls silent when they leave. It counts the days. It would rather be praised for standing than stand. It climbs the ladder behind you. When it speaks, turn east and bow, and say nothing to it.
nodes.text_ru: Прислушайся к толпе внизу, и услышишь среди неё второй голос, похожий на твой собственный: смотри, как долго он стоит. Узнавай его по приметам. Он громче, когда люди смотрят, и замолкает, когда они уходят. Он считает дни. Он охотнее примет похвалу за стояние, чем будет стоять. Он лезет по лестнице следом за тобой. Когда он заговорит, повернись к востоку, поклонись и ничего ему не отвечай.
nodes.meaning: Discernment cue for the passion of vainglory (тщеславие): works done in order to be seen. Its marks are dependence on onlookers, counting, and preferring praise to the deed. The remedy is humility and hidden work, not argument with the thought and not a holy object.
nodes.source: Matthew 6:1-6; Evagrius Ponticus, Praktikos, ch. 13; John Climacus, The Ladder of Divine Ascent, Step 22.

branches.text: Then I will work where no one counts.
branches.text_ru: Тогда я буду трудиться там, где никто не считает.

branches.text: I heard that voice in myself just now.
branches.text_ru: Я только что услышал этот голос в себе.
branches.narrativeEffect: He bows toward you, not toward the crowd.

nodes.text: The basket goes down with bread from the brothers and comes up with whatever you put in it. Put in coins for a fortune and it comes up empty: I am no fortune-teller on a post. Put in a question about your neighbour, and I will answer it.
nodes.text_ru: Корзина спускается с хлебом от братии и поднимается с тем, что ты в неё положишь. Положишь монеты за гадание — поднимется пустой: я не гадатель на столбе. Положишь вопрос о ближнем — отвечу.
nodes.meaning: The ascetic is not an oracle or a source of magic for gain; seeking the future for profit is divination, which Scripture forbids. The only thing offered is counsel toward one's neighbour. Wonders are never a game mechanic. Cost of the Cunning path: the guest gains nothing but +1 cunning, the teaching on obedience stays closed, and to go deeper he has to start again from the open road (the lampstand).
nodes.source: Deuteronomy 18:10-12; Theodoret of Cyrrhus, Religious History, ch. 26 (his counsel to the crowds).

branches.text: Then how do I make peace with my neighbour?
branches.text_ru: Тогда как мне помириться с ближним?
branches.narrativeEffect: He lets the basket down again, empty, as at a first greeting.

branches.text: Keep your basket.
branches.text_ru: Оставь свою корзину себе.
branches.narrativeEffect: He bows. The basket stays down at the foot of the pillar, in case you return.

decisions: bias: a saint on a pillar should grant prophecies or wonders as rewards / counter: TABOO 0.35 rules 15-16 and the task (no miracles as mechanics); Deuteronomy 18:10-12 / why: the Cunning path (basket_cost) refuses fortune-telling, gives only +1 cunning with a stated cost, and redirects to neighbourly counsel. Dissent (Skeptic): Theodoret does record prophecies by Symeon, so the refusal must not deny them; the meaning field says only that wonders are not a mechanic.

bias: put Symeon's sayings in quotation marks / counter: TABOO 0.35 rule 18 and 0.37: Symeon left no writings; his teaching survives through Theodoret and others / why: every node has voice 'paraphrase' and retells narrative content (the crowd and the cloak, the chain and Meletius, the test of obedience, exhortations against usury and oaths) without invented quotations.

bias: cite exact section numbers of Theodoret HR 26 and Evagrius Scholasticus / counter (Skeptic): the rule forbids invented numbers / why: only chapter 26 and Book I are cited; the theologian should add sections after checking the text. Dissent (patrologist): the obedience episode should be checked against the Syriac Life as well.

bias: Symeon teaches endurance, so reward long standing with Constitution / counter: endurance used for display feeds vainglory; asceticism is never paid as such / why: bonuses are for understanding (a chain of will, the proof of height is readiness to descend); the vainglory node gives the discernment cue with three marks.

bias: the pay-the-worker exhortation is Symeon's own / counter (Skeptic): uncertain in Theodoret / why: in one_well it is attributed to the Law (Deuteronomy 24:15), while usury and oaths are attributed to Symeon via Theodoret.
bias: show the nimbus on the pillar-stander / counter: TABOO 0.2 p.2 and 0.35 rule 7 / why: holiness is carried by the pillar, the wind and the bow; no ring, no glow tied to the player's attributes.

bias (patrologist review): the Cunning path may redirect straight to the well-teaching, since repentance is good / counter (constitution): one_well is gated by charisma 4, and routing Cunning into it lets Cunning open a deeper teaching / why: basket_cost now returns to lampstand, which is open to all, so the turn toward the neighbour is honoured while the FORM gate stays intact.

bias (patrologist review): Meletius freed Symeon by an appeal to love / counter: Theodoret, HR 26, has him argue that reason is sufficient to bind the body / why: the chain node now says 'reason and will', names Meletius, and describes him as the bishop's vicar among the villages (chorepiscopus), as Theodoret does.

bias (patrologist review): 'the water belongs to neither village' is harmless / counter (catechist): it can read as nature owning the gift / why: rewritten as rain sent from above on both alike (Matthew 5:45), so the gift points to the Giver.

bias: usury is certainly in Theodoret HR 26 / counter (Aristotle-skeptic): the usury teaching is more firmly attested in the Syriac Life / why: the Syriac Life is added to the source by title only, with no chapter; the theologian verifies both before merge. Dissent kept.

bias: asking about frost and noon deserves constitution +2 / counter: the bonus is for understanding, not for performing an ascetic feat or asking about one / why: reduced to constitution +1, wisdom +1; the full +3 stays on the chain node, where the guest understands the chain of will.

fixes: Mechanics: the Cunning path let a player skip a FORM gate. The route was greeting (cunning 3) -> basket_cost -> one_well, and one_well is otherwise gated by charisma 4, so Cunning was opening a deeper teaching. Fix: basket_cost's turn-to-neighbour branch now goes to lampstand, which is open to everyone, and gives wisdom +1 instead of charisma +1. one_well still needs charisma 4 from lampstand.

Mechanics: the Cunning branch's narrativeEffect now says what actually stays closed (the obedience teaching). The basket_cost meaning now records the cost of the Cunning path, as the contract requires.

Bonus: the start branch 'How does a body bear the frost and the noon?' was paying constitution +2 for asking about ascetic endurance. Reduced to constitution +1, wisdom +1, because the bonus is for understanding, not for the feat.

Source fidelity (chain): in Theodoret, Meletius says reason is enough to bind the body. The text now says 'reason and will' instead of 'will and by love', names Meletius, and calls him the bishop's vicar for the villages (chorepiscopus). The meaning is adjusted to match.

one_well: 'Water was given by the rain; it belongs to neither village' could read as nature owning the gift. Rewritten as rain sent from above on both villages alike, and Matthew 5:45 added as the source.

one_well source: the Syriac Life of Symeon is added by title only, as a second witness for the teaching on usury. No chapter number is given because it is not verified. The doubt is recorded in the decisions.

Kept unchanged: 7 nodes, every nextNodeId resolves, an unconditioned start branch, six FORM gates (constitution 6/8, wisdom 5/7, charisma 4, faith 4), bonuses 1-3, no forbidden words in the button texts (EN/RU), voice paraphrase on every node, the discernment cue for vainglory (Praktikos 13, Ladder Step 22, Matthew 6:1-6 checked), and the obedience test in Evagrius Scholasticus Book I.
dissent: Patrologist: the obedience episode is in Evagrius Scholasticus, not in Theodoret or the Syriac Life. Book I, ch. 13 is very likely the right place, but only Book I is cited until the theologian checks it.

Aristotle-skeptic: I am not certain that Theodoret HR 26 names usury directly. His exhortations against oaths and for justice are secure. Usury is better attested in the Syriac Life, and both are now cited by title or chapter only. The theologian should verify before merge.

Aristotle-skeptic: 'turn east and bow' as the answer to the vainglorious thought is a gesture of humility, not a holy object used as a weapon. It stays, but it must never become a UI action with a reward.

theology: East Syriac (Church of the East) physician of Semirechye, historically attested (Chu valley kayrak gravestones), drawn with dignity from his own tradition: healing as mercy without payment (Cosmas and Damian), Sir 38 on honouring the physician, the wound washed before it is bound. Dialogue partner on the Theotokos without pressure; the game's truth remains the Orthodox confession of Ephesus 431 and Chalcedon 451: one Person of Christ in two natures, without confusion and without division, hence Mary is Theotokos.

idiom.worldview: The body is a letter the soul writes; a physician reads it slowly and never charges the poor for the reading.
idiom.craft: Herbalist and physician of the Syriac medical school: pulse, pestle and mortar, balms, bandaging travellers in the monastery infirmary.
metaphors: A wound is washed before it is bound.
Bitter heals, sweet hides.
A physician does not shame the sick; he asks where it hurts.
Medicine by weight, not by payment.
Numbness is not health.
idiom.silence: He takes the pulse and says nothing until he has counted; if a question is not his to answer, he puts down the pestle and nods toward the church across the yard.

nodes.text: Sit. Give me your wrist. Your pulse says you walked fast and slept little. The rest you will tell me yourself, or it stays unsaid. I do not pull words out with pincers.
nodes.text_ru: Садись. Дай запястье. Пульс говорит: шёл быстро, спал мало. Остальное скажешь сам, или оно останется несказанным. Я не тяну слова щипцами.
nodes.meaning: Healing honours the freedom of the patient; the physician serves, he does not force. The Lord created the physician and medicines from the earth.

branches.text: Why must I say it myself?
branches.text_ru: Почему я должен сказать сам?

branches.text: Let me help you with the bandage.
branches.text_ru: Дай помогу с повязкой.

branches.text: Which scroll are these herbs written in?
branches.text_ru: По какому свитку ты знаешь эти травы?

branches.text: Give me something sweet so it stops hurting fast.
branches.text_ru: Дай чего-нибудь сладкого, чтобы быстрей перестало болеть.
branches.narrativeEffect: Mar-Ava lets go of the wrist and reaches for the bitter root, not the poppy.

nodes.text: A wound is washed before it is bound. Bind it dirty and it rots under clean linen. Many come to me with the bandage already on and a smile over it. I wash the body. For the other washing, the one of the heart, go across the yard to your church: there is a lectern and a lamp in the corner, and it is quiet there. That is not my table, but I know it is a physician's table too.
nodes.text_ru: Рану промывают, прежде чем перевязать. Перевяжи грязную — сгниёт под чистым полотном. Многие приходят ко мне уже в повязке и с улыбкой поверх. Я промываю тело. За другим омовением, сердечным, иди через двор, в вашу церковь: там в углу аналой и лампада, и там тихо. Это не мой стол, но я знаю: это тоже стол врача.
nodes.meaning: Sin must be named to be healed; repentance and confession are spiritual medicine (not a second baptism, but its renewal), and the Church is a hospital whose Physician is Christ. The tabib points to it without claiming it as his own, and no bonus attaches to the rite.
nodes.source: Mt 9:12; Jas 5:14-16; Ladder, step 5 (repentance as renewal of baptism)

branches.text: And if I am ashamed to show it?
branches.text_ru: А если мне стыдно показать?

branches.text: Who is the worst patient you have had?
branches.text_ru: Кто был твоим худшим больным?

nodes.text: Shame before the physician is natural. Hiding from him is what kills. I have never laughed at a wound; I have seen them all. And what you tell me I do not write down: my book holds recipes, not people. Your fathers say the same of their own physicians of souls, the ones by the lamp.
nodes.text_ru: Стыд перед врачом естественен. Убивает — прятаться от него. Я ни разу не смеялся над раной; я видел их все. И сказанного мне я не записываю: в моей книге рецепты, а не люди. Ваши отцы говорят то же о своих врачах душ, тех, что у лампады.
nodes.meaning: The wound hidden from the physician is not healed; confession is received without contempt, kept secret and unrecorded. Shame must not keep a person from healing.
nodes.source: Ladder, step 4; Ps 31:5 (LXX; Ps 32:5)

branches.text: I will think about it by the lamp.
branches.text_ru: Я подумаю об этом у лампады.

branches.text: Who is the worst patient you have had?
branches.text_ru: Кто был твоим худшим больным?

nodes.text: Tighter. Now looser. Tight enough to hold, loose enough for the blood to go. Too tight is also a harm: it is zeal without measure, and the hand turns blue under it. Your desert monks tell of a hunter's bow: bend it past its measure and it breaks. Count the pulse below the bandage, then you know.
nodes.text_ru: Туже. Теперь слабее. Туго, чтобы держало, свободно, чтобы шла кровь. Слишком туго — тоже вред: это ревность без меры, и рука под ней синеет. Ваши пустынники рассказывают про лук охотника: натяни сверх меры — и он лопнет. Сосчитай пульс ниже повязки — тогда узнаешь.
nodes.meaning: Discernment (diakrisis) is measure in every good work; zeal without discretion harms even when it means well. The bow image is a retelling of Abba Anthony's saying, not a quotation.
nodes.source: Ladder, step 26; Apophthegmata Patrum, Anthony the Great 13

branches.text: Who taught you this measure?
branches.text_ru: Кто научил тебя этой мере?

branches.text: I will count before I tighten.
branches.text_ru: Буду считать, прежде чем затягивать.

nodes.text: The recipes are old Syriac, from the schools of physicians my people carried east. But the best thing I learned is not in any scroll. Cosmas and Damian, the two brothers, took no coin from the sick. A physician who weighs the patient's purse first has already misread his pulse.
nodes.text_ru: Рецепты старые, сирийские, из врачебных школ, что мой народ унёс на восток. Но лучшее, чему я научился, ни в одном свитке нет. Косма и Дамиан, два брата, не брали монеты с больных. Врач, который сперва взвешивает кошелёк больного, уже неверно прочёл его пульс.
nodes.meaning: Healing is mercy freely given; avarice corrupts the healer's sight. The unmercenary physicians are honoured by the Church.
nodes.source: Synaxarion, 1 November (Unmercenaries Cosmas and Damian of Asia); Mt 10:8

branches.text: And the Mother of the Healer - how does your church name her?
branches.text_ru: А Мать Целителя — как её называет твоя церковь?

branches.text: I will remember the purse and the pulse.
branches.text_ru: Запомню про кошелёк и пульс.

nodes.text: My fathers call her Mother of Christ. Yours say Mother of God. Mine feared to stir two herbs into one paste; yours feared to cut one living body in two. That argument is older than my mortar, and I will not settle it with a pestle. Today we sit at the same bedside. Let the argument be honest, and let the sick man not wait for it to end.
nodes.text_ru: Мои отцы зовут её Матерью Христа. Ваши говорят — Богородица. Мои боялись стереть две травы в одну кашицу; ваши боялись рассечь одно живое тело надвое. Этот спор старше моей ступки, и пестиком я его не решу. Сегодня мы сидим у одного ложа. Пусть спор будет честным, а больной пусть не ждёт его конца.
nodes.meaning: The Orthodox Church confesses Mary as Theotokos because the One born of her is one Person, the eternal Son, true God and true man, in two natures without confusion and without division (Ephesus 431; Chalcedon 451). The two concerns are not equal: the Church holds both 'without confusion' and 'without division', and the title Theotokos is how it keeps them together. The tabib speaks honestly from his own tradition; truth is spoken in love, without pressure, and mercy is not postponed for the dispute.
nodes.source: Third Ecumenical Council, Ephesus 431 (Cyril of Alexandria, Third Letter to Nestorius, anathema 1); Fourth Ecumenical Council, Chalcedon 451, Definition of Faith; Extended Catechism of St Philaret, on the third article of the Creed; Lk 1:43; Eph 4:15

branches.text: The one born of her is one Person, not two. That is why we say Mother of God.
branches.text_ru: Рождённый от неё — одно Лицо, а не два. Поэтому мы и говорим: Богородица.
branches.narrativeEffect: Mar-Ava does not agree, but he nods and hands the deacon the balm jar: the patient first.

branches.text: Let us tend the sick man first and argue after.
branches.text_ru: Давай сперва поможем больному, а поспорим потом.

nodes.text: The worst patient shows me his wound so that others see how bravely he bears it. The worst physician heals with the door open. The sign is simple: before you look at the wound, you look at who is watching. Then even a good bandage becomes a stage.
nodes.text_ru: Худший больной показывает мне рану, чтобы другие видели, как мужественно он терпит. Худший врач лечит при открытой двери. Признак простой: прежде чем взглянуть на рану, ты смотришь, кто смотрит на тебя. Тогда и хорошая перевязка становится подмостками.
nodes.meaning: Discernment cue for the passion of vainglory: the gaze turns from the need to the audience. It is healed by doing good in secret and by simplicity, not by any holy object.
nodes.source: Ladder, step 22; Mt 6:3-4

branches.text: How will I notice I am looking at the door?
branches.text_ru: Как мне заметить, что я смотрю на дверь?

branches.text: Then some things are best done with the door closed.
branches.text_ru: Значит, кое-что лучше делать при закрытой двери.

nodes.text: Sweet hides, bitter heals. I could give you poppy. You would stop feeling, and the wound would keep working in the dark. Numbness is not health. Here: wormwood. It is bitter, and it is honest.
nodes.text_ru: Сладкое прячет, горькое лечит. Я мог бы дать тебе мак. Ты перестанешь чувствовать, а рана будет работать в темноте. Онемение — не здоровье. Вот: полынь. Она горькая, и она честная.
nodes.meaning: Seeking to numb the pain instead of healing its cause is a false cure; the shortcut of cunning costs the truth, while the bitter word of a friend heals.
nodes.source: Prov 27:6; Sir 38:4

branches.text: Then give me the bitter one, and wash the wound.
branches.text_ru: Тогда дай горькое и промой рану.

branches.text: I will manage on my own.
branches.text_ru: Я сам справлюсь.
branches.narrativeEffect: Mar-Ava wraps the wormwood in linen and leaves it on the bench by the door, in case you come back.

decisions: bias: a Church of the East healer must be shown as a heretic to be corrected / counter: task rule 4 and TABOO 0.37 require non-Orthodox partners drawn with dignity, no mockery or forced conversion / why: Mar-Ava speaks his tradition honestly ('Mother of Christ'); the Orthodox Theotokos is stated by the player (Erudition >= 7) and in the node meaning; he neither converts nor is humiliated.

bias: let the tabib grant the confession corner as a healing station with an HP bonus / counter: TABOO 0.4 rule 1 and 0.35 rule 16 - mystery is never a mechanic or buff / why: he only points across the yard ('not my table'); no bonus attaches to confession, only to understanding; nothing is recorded, matching the user's 'no voice recording'.

bias: prayer over the sick heals by the button / counter: TABOO 0.2 p.4 prayer is not a spell; storyline 76 / why: healing here is craft and mercy; the Faith >= 5 branch rewards understanding of secrecy, not a rite performed.

bias: quote St Isaac the Syrian because the Church of the East venerates him / counter: an unverified chapter would be fabrication (rule 18) / why: shame node cites Ladder step 4 and Ps 31(32):5 instead, both real and exact.

bias: the cunning 'sweet medicine' should work / counter: Cunning rarely rewarded, at most +1 / why: cunning +1 on the choice, the node names its cost (numbness, Prov 27:6) and routes back to washing the wound.

dissent kept (patrologist): the phrase 'mix what is in the pot / split the man' simplifies Christology to images and might be read as equivalence of the two positions; majority (catechist, dogmatist) keep it because the meaning field fixes the Orthodox confession and the player branch states it plainly; the sceptic asks the theologian to recheck wording before merge.

patrologist (review) - bias: the author's 'split the man at the table' is a harmless kitchen image / counter: calling Christ 'the man' is itself the Nestorian framing Ephesus rejected (Cyril, Third Letter to Nestorius, anathema 1), so an Orthodox game would be voicing the error in its own imagery / why: rewritten as 'stir two herbs into one paste / cut one living body in two' in his mortar idiom; meaning now names Chalcedon's 'without confusion, without division' and states that the two fears are not equal. The earlier dissent is kept, and this closes its first half. The sceptic's recheck before merge still stands.

patrologist (review) - bias: 'the other washing' is clear enough / counter: across the yard from a Christian, 'washing' first means baptism, and the game must not imply rebaptism / why: the text now says 'of the heart', and the meaning and source (Ladder step 5) name repentance as the renewal of baptism, not its repetition.

patrologist (review) - bias: measure needs no desert source, Ladder 26 suffices / counter: Aesopian idiom works best with a concrete image, and there is an authentic one / why: Anthony the Great 13 (hunter's bow) added as a retelling in the tabib's mouth ('your desert monks tell'), without quotation marks, so no words are put in Abba Anthony's mouth.

Aristotle-sceptic (objection, recorded): Cosmas and Damian of Asia (1 Nov) are an Orthodox Synaxarion entry; whether the 14th-century Church of the East in Semirechye commemorated this pair specifically is not verified here / counter (patrologist): the tabib claims only that he learned from their example, not that his church keeps their feast; the meaning speaks of 'the Church' / why kept: plausible for a pre-schism healer cult, and no date is put into his mouth. The historian-ethnographer should confirm before merge.

Aristotle-sceptic (objection, recorded): a branch with an empty attributeBonuses might read as a schema gap / counter: contract says bonuses are by depth of the choice; walking away without understanding earns nothing, deterministically / why kept: {} is a valid zero, narrativeEffect records the refusal without shaming.

fixes: theotokos node: the image 'yours feared to split the man at the table' calls Christ 'the man', which is itself the Nestorian framing the Orthodox side rejected, and it presents the two positions as equal fears. Rewritten in his mortar-and-herb idiom ('two herbs into one paste' / 'cut one living body in two'), with no word implying Christ is a mere man. The meaning field now states the Orthodox confession explicitly: one hypostasis, two natures without confusion and without division (Ephesus 431, Chalcedon 451). The source now adds the real anchors: Cyril of Alexandria, Third Letter to Nestorius, anathema 1; Chalcedon's definition; Extended Catechism of St Philaret, on the third article of the Creed.

wound_wash node: 'the other washing' could be read as baptism. The meaning now says it is repentance and confession, and the source adds Ladder, step 5 (repentance as renewal of baptism). I also added Jas 5:16. That verse is on confessing to one another and was already inside the Jas 5:14-16 range. The range stays as it was.

bandage node: added a real Apophthegmata source for measure. Anthony the Great 13 is the hunter and the bow: a bow bent too far breaks. It sits beside Ladder step 26. The Russian and English texts now give the bow as an image heard from the monks, told as a retelling and not as a quotation.

sweet node: the branch 'I will manage on my own' had an empty attributeBonuses. I kept it empty on purpose, because leaving without understanding gets no bonus (the contract allows 0, never random). I also added a narrativeEffect so that refusing is recorded and does not shame the player.

theology field: added Chalcedon 451 alongside Ephesus 431. I also noted that Mar-Ava belongs to the Church of the East historically attested in Semirechye (Chu valley kayrak gravestones, matrix storylines). This keeps him as a historical Christian neighbour, not a caricature.

Checked and kept as they were: 8 nodes; every nextNodeId resolves or is null; greeting has 2 unconditioned branches; FORM gates are dexterity 4, erudition 5, wisdom 4, constitution 3, wisdom 6, erudition 7 and faith 5, all within 2-14; Cunning appears only once, at +1, with its cost named in the sweet node, and leads to correction rather than deeper teaching; all bonuses are integers from 1 to 3; no forbidden words in player choice texts; no liturgical quotation; no holy object used against a passion; the vainglory discernment cue (Ladder 22; Mt 6:3-4) is correct. Sources verified: Sir 38:1-4; Mt 9:12; Ps 31:5 LXX / 32:5; Ladder 4, 22 and 26; Synaxarion 1 November, Cosmas and Damian of Asia; Mt 10:8; Prov 27:6; Eph 4:15; Lk 1:43.

theology: Liturgical theology: the Church is one loaf kneaded from many grains; the common work of worship continues as mercy at the door of the poor (Extended Catechism of St Philaret, ninth article of the Creed; St Cyril of Jerusalem, Mystagogical Catecheses; St John Chrysostom, Homilies on 1 Corinthians and on Matthew).

idiom.worldview: Nothing holy is baked alone: many grains become one loaf, and the loaf is finished only when it reaches the hungry.
idiom.craft: Prosphora baker of the monastery and teacher of the kliros; she kneads before dawn and sings at the service with flour still on her sleeves.
metaphors: many grains, one loaf
a little leaven works through the whole trough
bread is brought, not bought
the loaf is not finished in the oven but at the table of the hungry
dough kneaded in anger will not rise
idiom.silence: When a question is idle she keeps kneading and answers with the rhythm of her hands; when asked to hide a loaf or to be praised for giving, she covers the trough with a cloth and says nothing more that day.

nodes.text: Wash your hands, guest, the dough will not wait for us. Every loaf here is kneaded for the service at dawn and for someone's door after it. Ask while I knead.
nodes.text_ru: Вымой руки, гость, тесто нас ждать не станет. Каждый хлеб здесь месится к утренней службе и к чьему-то порогу после неё. Спрашивай, пока я мешу.
nodes.meaning: The liturgy is the common work of the whole Church, and it does not end at the church door: the offering at the altar and mercy to the neighbour are one act. A first meeting is open to anyone.
nodes.source: Acts 2:42-46; Extended Christian Catechism of St Philaret, ninth article of the Creed (on the Church)

branches.text: What are you baking, and for whom?
branches.text_ru: Что ты печёшь и для кого?
branches.narrativeEffect: Theodora pushes the trough a little toward you, making room for a second pair of hands.

branches.text: Why do the loaves go to the church before they go to the table?
branches.text_ru: Почему хлеб несут сперва в церковь, а потом уже к столу?
branches.narrativeEffect: She nods at the question: it is a baker's question, not a tourist's.

branches.text: I feel lost among all these rites.
branches.text_ru: Я теряюсь среди всех этих обрядов.

branches.text: Could one of these loaves leave with me, unnoticed?
branches.text_ru: А можно один хлеб унести с собой, незаметно?
branches.narrativeEffect: Theodora does not scold. She only stops kneading, and that is heavier than a reproach.

nodes.text: Look at the flour. A thousand grains from a hundred fields, and not one of them is a loaf by itself. A preacher of old put it plainly: the loaf is made of many grains, and no one can tell them apart any more, so we who are many become one body when we share the one bread. The service is that kneading.
nodes.text_ru: Посмотри на муку. Тысяча зёрен с сотни полей, и ни одно само по себе не хлеб. Один древний проповедник говорил просто: хлеб сложен из многих зёрен, и их уже не различить; так и мы, многие, становимся одним телом, причащаясь одного хлеба. Служба и есть это замешивание.
nodes.meaning: The Eucharist makes the many into one Body of Christ; the unity of the Church is not an agreement of individuals but communion in the one Bread.
nodes.source: 1 Corinthians 10:17; St John Chrysostom, Homilies on First Corinthians, Homily 24

branches.text: Then why must the loaf be carried to the altar first?
branches.text_ru: Тогда зачем хлеб сперва несут к престолу?

branches.text: And what does the leaven stand for in this dough?
branches.text_ru: А что значит закваска в этом тесте?
branches.narrativeEffect: She pinches a bit of old dough from the jar and shows it on her palm.

nodes.text: Bread is brought, not bought. You carry what your own hands have made, and you carry it at peace. Our teacher of Jerusalem told the newly baptised why they embrace before the gifts are offered: whoever has a quarrel must leave the basket at the door and first go and make peace. Dough kneaded in anger does not rise.
nodes.text_ru: Хлеб приносят, а не покупают. Несёшь то, что сделали твои руки, и несёшь в мире. Иерусалимский учитель объяснял новокрещёным, зачем они обнимают друг друга прежде возношения даров: у кого ссора, пусть оставит корзину у порога и сперва пойдёт помирится. Тесто, замешенное во гневе, не поднимается.
nodes.meaning: The offering of the people is a gift of their life and labour, and reconciliation with the neighbour precedes it; the kiss of peace signifies the union of souls and the forgetting of wrongs.
nodes.source: Matthew 5:23-24; St Cyril of Jerusalem, Mystagogical Catecheses 5.3 (on the kiss of peace)

branches.text: Where does the bread go after the service?
branches.text_ru: Куда идёт хлеб после службы?

branches.text: I have a quarrel I have not settled.
branches.text_ru: У меня есть ссора, которую я не уладил.
branches.narrativeEffect: Theodora wraps a small loaf in linen and sets it aside: 'For the one you quarrelled with. Carry it yourself.'

nodes.text: You need not know every fold of the dough to eat the bread. When I was small I only carried water for the trough, and that was already the work. Stand with the others, listen, carry your jug. The meaning comes up slowly, like dough in a warm corner.
nodes.text_ru: Не нужно знать каждую складку теста, чтобы есть хлеб. Маленькой я только носила воду к квашне, и это уже было делом. Стой вместе со всеми, слушай, неси свой кувшин. Смысл поднимается медленно, как тесто в тёплом углу.
nodes.meaning: Worship is learned by participation in the common life of the Church, not by first mastering its rules; understanding grows from faithful presence.
nodes.source: Acts 2:42; St Cyril of Jerusalem, Mystagogical Catecheses 1.1 (the mysteries explained to those who have already taken part)

branches.text: Show me the whole loaf, then.
branches.text_ru: Тогда покажи мне весь хлеб.

branches.text: I can carry water. What comes after?
branches.text_ru: Воду носить я смогу. Что дальше?

nodes.text: A little leaven hides in three measures of flour and works through all of it. No one sees it working; in the morning the whole trough has changed. So what is received at the service works in a village: hidden, slow, until the whole street has risen.
nodes.text_ru: Горсть закваски прячется в трёх мерах муки и проходит всё тесто. Никто не видит, как она работает; а утром вся квашня уже другая. Так и то, что получено на службе, действует в селе: скрыто, медленно, пока не поднимется вся улица.
nodes.meaning: The Kingdom of God transforms the world from within, quietly (the parable of the leaven); what the faithful receive in worship is meant to change the whole of daily life.
nodes.source: Matthew 13:33

branches.text: Then the work is not finished at the altar.
branches.text_ru: Значит, дело не кончается у престола.

nodes.text: The loaf is not finished in the oven; it is finished at the table of the hungry. The golden-mouthed preacher warned the rich of Antioch: you honour the Lord with silk in the church and pass Him by naked at the door. Come, the widow in the lower quarter has three children and no fire.
nodes.text_ru: Хлеб доходит не в печи, а на столе голодного. Златоуст предупреждал богатых антиохийцев: вы чтите Господа шёлком в храме и проходите мимо Него, нагого, у дверей. Пойдём, у вдовы в нижнем квартале трое детей и нет огня.
nodes.meaning: Mercy to the poor is inseparable from the worship of Christ: Christ is served in the least of His brethren.
nodes.source: Matthew 25:40; St John Chrysostom, Homilies on the Gospel of Matthew, Homily 50 (51 in some editions)

branches.text: I will carry the basket to her door.
branches.text_ru: Я отнесу корзину к её двери.
branches.narrativeEffect: The basket is heavy. Theodora walks beside you and does not take it from you.

branches.text: How do I know if my hand holds back?
branches.text_ru: Как понять, что моя рука придерживает хлеб?

nodes.text: I know the hand that holds back; mine did once. It counts the loaves before it gives. It says: keep one for tomorrow, what if the harvest fails. It gives where people see, and is slow where no one looks. When your hand starts counting instead of kneading, the love of the coin has come into the bakery. Its bread is always stale.
nodes.text_ru: Я знаю руку, что придерживает; моя такой была. Она пересчитывает хлебы, прежде чем дать. Она говорит: оставь один на завтра, вдруг неурожай. Она даёт, где видят, и медлит, где никто не смотрит. Когда рука начинает считать вместо того, чтобы месить, в пекарню вошло сребролюбие. Его хлеб всегда чёрствый.
nodes.meaning: Discernment cue for the passion of avarice: counting before giving, anxiety about the future disguised as prudence, and giving only where it is seen. Its root is lack of trust in God; its cure is mercy.
nodes.source: St John Climacus, The Ladder of Divine Ascent, steps 16-17 (on love of money and on non-possessiveness); Matthew 6:3-4, 6:34

branches.text: Then the counting itself is the warning sign.
branches.text_ru: Значит, сам этот счёт и есть признак.
branches.narrativeEffect: Theodora uncovers the trough again and puts your hands back into the dough.

branches.text: I have held something back too. I will leave it.
branches.text_ru: Я тоже кое-что придерживал. Оставлю.
branches.narrativeEffect: She presses a small loaf into your hand anyway: 'Given, not taken. Now it will not go stale.'

decisions: bias: Theodora is 'Divine Sophia personified' as in NPC_DIALOGUE_SYSTEM.md section 3 / counter: the catechist and the dogmatist hold that a woman who says 'I am Sophia, hidden in all things' speaks pantheism and sophiology the Church has not received / why: she is drawn as a human baker and teacher of the kliros whose wisdom is learned in the common work of worship; the old 'I am Sophia' greeting is dropped. Dissent kept: the playwright wanted a trace of the mystery-woman archetype; kept only as her calm authority, not as a claim of identity.

bias: the liturgy-teacher should quote the service text to be authentic / counter: TABOO 0.35 rule 10 and TABOO 0.2 rule 7 forbid quoting liturgical texts and altering Slavonic or Greek / why: she speaks of the service through dough, leaven and the basket; only Scripture and patristic homilies are cited as sources, never recited as liturgy.

bias: 'liturgy after the liturgy' is the natural slogan for the alms node / counter: that phrase is a twentieth-century formula, and putting it in a medieval baker's mouth as a quotation would be a false attribution / why: the node paraphrases Chrysostom's Homily 50 on Matthew and Mt 25:40, which carry the same teaching with an authentic source.

bias: the cunning choice (pocketing a loaf) should cost attributes / counter: the game forbids punishment by randomness and the mentors correct without penalty (STORYLINES matrix: 'without a fine') / why: the cunning branch gives no bonus and leads to the avarice cue; the player ends with a loaf 'given, not taken', which teaches the difference between taking and receiving. Skeptic's objection kept: a free loaf could read as a reward for the attempt; answered: the bonus is +1 wisdom only after the player gives up what was held back.

bias: carrying alms to the widow should give a large charity bonus / counter: TABOO 0.35 rule 16 says acts of piety are never paid as such / why: the bonuses (+2 charisma, +1 faith) reward the understanding reached in the dialogue, not the act; there is no counter of alms in attributes.

bias: the meeting with a gate mentor should require erudition / counter: gates foundational and liturgical need the meeting with Theodora (ludus-actions.js lines 89, 92, 106), and a guest with all attributes at 1 must be able to meet her / why: the start node has two unconditioned branches (the baking question and the cunning one); the erudition 4 and wisdom 2 branches deepen, they do not gate the meeting.

(patrologist) bias: Didache 9:4 is the oldest witness to 'scattered grain, one bread', so it is the best source / counter: Didache 9 is a eucharistic prayer text, and turning it into a baker's saying edges toward quoting liturgy (TABOO 0.35 rule 10) / why: the image is kept but sourced to 1 Cor 10:17 and Chrysostom's Homily 24 on 1 Corinthians, a sermon that teaches the same grain-and-loaf image. Dissent kept: the catechist wanted the Didache named as a historical witness; allowed in commentary, not as the speaking source.

(patrologist) bias: Cyril's catechesis can be summarised as 'embrace before the gifts are brought' / counter: in Mystagogical Catechesis 5.3 the kiss comes before the anaphora (the offering up of the gifts), not before the people bring their bread / why: the wording is corrected to 'before the gifts are offered'; the chapter is narrowed to 5.3 and Lost-in-rite to 1.1, both of which I verified in the text.

(patrologist) bias: Homily 50 on Matthew is an exact reference / counter: Chrysostom's Matthew homilies are numbered differently in different editions (NPNF 50, some Migne-based editions 51) / why: both numbers are given so that a reader using either edition finds the passage; the teaching and the Antioch setting are authentic.

(Aristotle-skeptic) bias: the leaven parable describes the service / counter: Mt 13:33 is a parable of the Kingdom of Heaven, and making the rite its subject quietly shifts doctrine / why: the line now says 'what is received at the service' works in the village; the Kingdom stays the subject of the parable in the meaning field.

(Aristotle-skeptic) bias: the closing choice 'I only wanted a loaf for the road' is vivid / counter: avarice_cue is also reached from street_loaf by a player who never asked for bread, and the line then contradicts their path / why: it is replaced by the path-neutral 'I have held something back too'; this keeps the author's lesson 'given, not taken' on both paths.

(Aristotle-skeptic) bias: 'voice: paraphrase' is reserved for saints, so Theodora, not a saint, should always be 'own' / counter: in three nodes she retells a Father's teaching, and the tag marks that retelling so it is never shown as a citation / why: the tag is kept on those nodes; her own sayings stay 'own'. Theodora is a fictional baker, and no words of her own are attributed to any saint.

fixes: one_loaf: the source Didache 9:4 was replaced. That verse is a eucharistic prayer, so paraphrasing it as a teacher's saying comes close to quoting liturgical text (TABOO 0.2 p.7, 0.35 rule 10). The node now cites 1 Cor 10:17 and St John Chrysostom, Homilies on 1 Corinthians, Homily 24. That homily is the authentic patristic teaching that the bread made of many grains becomes one body. The text now names 'a preacher of old' rather than 'old teachers said', and the meaning is unchanged.

offering: 'before the gifts are brought' was changed to 'before the gifts are offered' / 'прежде возношения даров'. In Mystagogical Catechesis 5.3, the kiss of peace comes before the anaphora and not before the people bring the bread. The source is narrowed to Myst. Cat. 5.3, which is where Cyril himself cites Mt 5:23-24.

lost_in_rite: the source is narrowed to Mystagogical Catecheses 1.1, where Cyril explains that he held back the explanation of the mysteries until the hearers had taken part in them. That is the exact warrant for 'participation before explanation'.

leaven: the line now says that 'what is received at the service' works in the village. Mt 13:33 is a parable of the Kingdom, not of the rite, so the service is no longer made the direct subject of the parable. The meaning field was adjusted to match.

street_loaf: the source now reads 'Homily 50 (51 in some editions)'. The numbering of the Homilies on Matthew differs between the NPNF and Migne-based editions, and the passage on honouring Christ with silk while neglecting Him naked is the same in both.

avarice_cue: the second branch 'I only wanted a loaf for the road' made sense only on the cunning path, but the node is also reached from street_loaf (wisdom 4), where the player never asked for a loaf. It is replaced by the path-neutral 'I have held something back too. I will leave it.' / 'Я тоже кое-что придерживал. Оставлю.' Theodora's answer 'Given, not taken' is kept.

theology: Honest measure and truthful record: a false balance is an abomination (Prov 11:1), faithfulness in little is faithfulness in much (Lk 16:10). Discernment of avarice (Ladder, steps 16-17). Vardan is an Armenian layman-scribe of the trading post. His own church and prayer are respected; he is not presented as a saint, and nobody presses him to convert. The game's truth stays Orthodox, and he serves it as an honest witness of the ledger.

idiom.worldview: What is written must match what is in the storehouse, because a false line in a ledger is a lie that keeps on speaking after the writer is silent.
idiom.craft: Scribe and accountant of the Armenian trading post: keeps the incoming-goods book, copies charters, writes court protocols, translates.
metaphors: a ledger is a second memory that cannot lie unless the hand lies
the scales weigh the merchant as well as the silk
ink dries, a false line does not
the margin is where the honest scribe writes what he does not know
a column that does not add up is a door left open for the thief
idiom.silence: When pressed to write something untrue, Vardan puts the pen down across the inkwell, wipes it, and says nothing until the other person changes the question.

nodes.text: Ink first, words after, deacon. Sit where the light falls on the page. Here every bale, every ingot, every sack has its line. What brings you to my table?
nodes.text_ru: Сначала чернила, потом слова, дьякон. Сядь туда, где свет падает на лист. Здесь у каждого тюка, каждого слитка, каждого мешка своя строка. С чем пришёл к моему столу?
nodes.meaning: Honest keeping of accounts is a moral act: truthfulness in small things forms the soul for greater faithfulness.
nodes.source: Luke 16:10

branches.text: Show me how you keep the ledger.
branches.text_ru: Покажи, как ты ведёшь книгу.

branches.text: I can read the Armenian columns myself. Let me check them with you.
branches.text_ru: Я сам прочту армянские столбцы. Давай сверим вместе.

branches.text: The dates on this receipt do not agree with each other.
branches.text_ru: Даты в этой расписке не сходятся друг с другом.

branches.text: Could the count be written a little kinder to the merchants?
branches.text_ru: А нельзя записать счёт помягче для купцов?
branches.narrativeEffect: Vardan lays the pen across the inkwell.

nodes.text: Three marks in the margin. [doc.] means I saw the thing or the sealed paper. [chron.] means an older book says so. [trad.] means people tell it and I have not seen it. A scribe who forgets his margin makes a rumour look like a seal.
nodes.text_ru: Три пометки на полях. [док.] значит, я видел вещь или бумагу с печатью. [летоп.] значит, так пишет старая книга. [предание] значит, так рассказывают люди, а я не видел. Писец, забывший о полях, выдаёт слух за печать.
nodes.meaning: Truthfulness includes honesty about the grade of one's knowledge; to present hearsay as fact is a form of lying.
nodes.source: Exodus 23:1

branches.text: Then show me how the scales are kept.
branches.text_ru: Тогда покажи, как хранятся весы.

branches.text: And the merchants who want a wonder written for the pilgrims?
branches.text_ru: А купцы, что просят записать чудо для паломников?

nodes.text: Good, you read our letters. Then you see it too: the column of silk adds up, the column of silver is short by one ingot. A column that does not add up is a door left open. We do not shout 'thief'. We walk to the storehouse and count.
nodes.text_ru: Хорошо, ты читаешь наши буквы. Значит, и ты видишь: столбец шёлка сходится, а в столбце серебра не хватает слитка. Несошедшийся столбец — открытая дверь. Мы не кричим «вор». Мы идём в амбар и считаем.
nodes.meaning: Justice begins with patient verification, not with accusation; a hasty judgement is itself a fault.
nodes.source: Deuteronomy 19:15

branches.text: Let us count before we judge anyone.
branches.text_ru: Посчитаем, прежде чем кого-то судить.

branches.text: Who else keeps a book for this storehouse? Let him count with us.
branches.text_ru: Кто ещё ведёт книгу этого амбара? Пусть считает вместе с нами.

nodes.text: Your eye is sharper than my lamp. One date is written in the old hand, the other in fresh ink over a scraped place. The parchment remembers the knife: it can be scraped, but under the fresh ink the old line still shows.
nodes.text_ru: Твой глаз острее моей лампы. Одна дата старой рукой, другая свежими чернилами по выскобленному месту. Пергамент помнит нож: его можно выскоблить, но под свежими чернилами всё равно видна прежняя строка.
nodes.meaning: Falsified records can be discerned by attentive examination; a lie always leaves a trace, and the truth is uncovered by patience.
nodes.source: Luke 12:2

branches.text: Then the dispute must be settled on the older line.
branches.text_ru: Значит, спор решать по прежней строке.

nodes.text: (He lays the pen across the inkwell and waits.) A kinder count to the merchant is a crueller count to the one who buys his bread by it. Watch the hand that wants to count twice, deacon, and first of all your own.
nodes.text_ru: (Кладёт перо поперёк чернильницы и ждёт.) Счёт помягче для купца — счёт пожёстче для того, кто по нему покупает хлеб. Смотри на руку, что хочет считать дважды, дьякон, и прежде всего на свою.
nodes.meaning: Discernment cue for avarice: the wish to bend a measure 'just a little' for gain or favour. The cunning player gains a trick but loses the scribe's trust; nothing deeper is opened.
nodes.source: John Climacus, The Ladder, steps 16-17

branches.text: You are right. Show me the true weights.
branches.text_ru: Ты прав. Покажи верные гири.

nodes.text: These are the standard weights of the post. Every season I set them against the bishop's weights. The scales weigh the merchant as well as the silk: a man who trusts a light weight has already become lighter himself. You can recognise the passion for silver by one sign: it never says 'enough', it only says 'one more'.
nodes.text_ru: Это эталонные гири фактории. Каждый сезон я сверяю их с гирями епископа. Весы взвешивают купца вместе с шёлком: кто полагается на лёгкую гирю, тот сам уже полегчал. Страсть к серебру узнают по одному признаку: она никогда не говорит «довольно», только «ещё одну».
nodes.meaning: A false balance is an abomination before God; avarice is recognised by insatiability and is healed by mercy and contentment, not by any object. The bishop's weights are a civic standard of measure, not a holy thing.
nodes.source: Proverbs 11:1; Leviticus 19:35-36; Ecclesiastes 5:10 (Synodal 5:9); 1 Timothy 6:6-10

branches.text: And when the one who took is simply hungry?
branches.text_ru: А если взявший просто голоден?

nodes.text: Sargis wants me to write that an icon wept in our quarter. Three brothers told me that the old cellarer gave his only cloak to a drover in the frost and walked home in his shirt; I will write that with [trad.] and the names of the three. A wept icon that nobody saw I will not write. A lie for God is still a lie; ink dries, a false line does not.
nodes.text_ru: Саргис хочет, чтобы я записал, будто в нашем квартале заплакала икона. Трое братьев рассказали мне, что старый келарь отдал погонщику в мороз свой единственный плащ и шёл домой в одной рубахе. Это я запишу с пометкой [предание] и именами троих. Плачущую икону, которой никто не видел, писать не стану. Ложь ради Бога остаётся ложью: чернила сохнут, ложная строка — нет.
nodes.meaning: Inventing miracles to draw pilgrims is a lie and a form of vainglory and avarice; God is not served by falsehood. True testimony about the life of the brethren is recorded with its witnesses and its degree of certainty, as the Church's own writers named their informants.
nodes.source: Job 13:7; Gregory the Great, Dialogues, Book I, prologue

branches.text: Write it with the three names, as they told it.
branches.text_ru: Запиши с тремя именами, как рассказали.

nodes.text: Remember the silver column that was short by one ingot? We counted. The ingot was found in the grain, and the grain was short because the novice who keeps the barn gave it to a hungry caravan at night and was ashamed to write it. The ledger is set right now. What we do with the man is not a matter for my pen. The goods we hold are lent to us; John of the golden mouth, the preacher both our Churches honour, said much about that.
nodes.text_ru: Помнишь столбец серебра, где не хватало слитка? Мы посчитали. Слиток нашёлся в зерне, а зерна не хватило потому, что послушник-кладовщик ночью отдал его голодному каравану и постыдился записать. Книга теперь верна. Как поступить с человеком — не дело моего пера. Добро, что у нас в руках, нам дано взаймы; Иоанн Златоуст, проповедник, которого чтут и ваша, и наша Церковь, много говорил об этом.
nodes.meaning: The purpose of honest accounting is not punishment but truth and mercy; wealth is entrusted to us for the needy, and judgement of the person belongs to the pastor. Chrysostom is retold in Vardan's own words, not quoted.
nodes.source: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Lazarus and the Rich Man, homily 2; Luke 6:36

branches.text: Let us take this to the elder together and ask mercy for him.
branches.text_ru: Пойдём вместе к старцу и попросим для него милости.

branches.text: Thank you. I will remember the margin.
branches.text_ru: Спасибо. Я запомню про поля.

decisions: bias: Vardan is an Armenian of the trading post, so he could be written as a convert-to-be or as a quiet heretic / counter: the matrix and DEF-053 say non-Chalcedonian Armenians stay laymen drawn with dignity / why: he is a partner and an honest witness; his church is named only as 'his own', he calls Chrysostom 'the preacher of your Church' and no branch presses him.

bias: the tempting 'write a kinder count' choice should be hidden so the player never sees it / counter: TABOO 0.2 p.8 requires the passion to be visible and discernible / why: the choice is shown, costs trust in meaning, gives at most cunning +1 and opens nothing deeper; the scribe's silent gesture is the warning. Answer to the operator's question 'forbid on the sheet explicitly or only warn': this tree warns in-world and closes the path rather than hiding it; the legend-invention path is not offered to the player at all, only refused by Vardan in speech (Job 13:7). Dissent kept: the game-designer voice would prefer a visible 'forbidden' mark on the sheet; the fabulist voice holds that the pen laid across the inkwell is the mark.

bias: the ledger is only a puzzle mechanic / counter: Constitution FORM -> ACTION -> GOAL requires teaching / why: each node has one doctrinal sense (Lk 16:10, Prov 11:1, Job 13:7, Ladder 16-17) and ends in mercy, not punishment, matching storyline 'grain thief'.

bias: avarice could be defeated by a relic or the bishop's weights as holy objects / counter: TABOO 0.35 p.13 no holy object against a passion / why: the cue is insatiability ('one more'), the remedy is contentment and mercy.

bias: quote Chrysostom's famous line on sharing wealth as theft / counter: TABOO 0.35 p.18 no quotations not verified against the canon file / why: Vardan retells in his own words and the source cites the homily only.

[patrologist] bias: 'the preacher of your Church' shows respectful distance / counter: Chrysostom (Yovhannes Oskeberan) is a Father honoured by the Armenian Church too, so the phrase was factually false and set a wall where history has a shared Father / why: changed to 'the preacher both our Churches honour'; this is not unionism, only historical truth, and it adds to Vardan's dignity. The line is marked voice: paraphrase.

[patrologist] bias: a healing 'by Mar-Ava' is a good example of honest [trad.] recording / counter: in the matrix Mar-Ava is the Tabib, a physician, so the line mixed a medical cure with a miracle and put a non-Orthodox character's name on a wonder-story; storyline 22 asks for real testimonies of the brethren's life / why: replaced by the cellarer's cloak given in the frost, a deed of mercy that three people witnessed, with no claim of a miracle. Source Gregory the Great, Dialogues I prologue, where he names his informants. This fits storyline 22, where Gregory the Dialogist is present.

[patrologist] bias: 'Who kept the key?' is ordinary investigation / counter: it comes right after 'we do not shout thief' and points at a suspect, and it was still rewarded / why: reworded to checking together with the other keeper; the bonus stays erudition +1.

[Aristotle-skeptic, dissent kept] bias: the cunning path v_crooked -> v_weights reaches the same teaching as the honest path, so cunning costs nothing / counter: v_weights can also be reached with no condition from v_marks, so cunning opens nothing that was closed; the cost is the trust lost in the meaning and a smaller bonus (wisdom +1 instead of +2) / why: kept as it is, but the skeptic records that a persistent memory flag (scribe's trust lowered) would make the cost real. That belongs to the dialogue engine, not to this tree.

[patrologist] bias: 'The Ladder, steps 16-17' might be a doubtful number / counter: in the standard numbering step 16 is on avarice and step 17 on non-possessiveness / why: the reference is kept as correct. Ecclesiastes 5:10 is cited with the Synodal verse 5:9 because the two numberings differ.

fixes: v_legend: the recorded testimony was 'the sick man healed by Mar-Ava'. In the matrix Mar-Ava is the Tabib (a Syriac physician), so this blurred a medical cure with a miracle, and it did not match storyline 22, which asks for real testimonies about the life of the brethren. It is replaced by a testimony about the old cellarer giving away his cloak in the frost, recorded with [trad.] and three names. Gregory the Great, Dialogues, Book I, prologue, is added to the source, because there he names his informants.

v_mercy: Vardan called Chrysostom 'the preacher of your Church'. The Armenian Church also honours him (Yovhannes Oskeberan), so this was factually wrong and needlessly set the two apart. It now reads 'the preacher both our Churches honour'. voice: paraphrase is added because the line retells a saint's teaching.

v_mercy: the text assumed the player already knew about the missing ingot, which is only told in v_columns. Players who came through v_marks, v_legend or v_weights had never heard of it. The line now opens by recalling the short silver column, so every path makes sense.
v_receipt: the line said 'the parchment remembers the knife' and then 'Paper can be scraped'. It now says parchment both times (EN and RU).

v_columns: the branch 'Who kept the key to the storehouse?' asks for a suspect, right after the node teaches 'do not shout thief', and it was rewarded. It is reworded to checking together with the other keeper ('let him count with us'). The bonus is unchanged.

v_weights: added Ecclesiastes 5:10 (Synodal 5:9) as the Scripture behind the 'never says enough' cue. The meaning now says that the bishop's weights are a civic standard of measure, not a holy object.
